7.s: atha paramarahasyo'yaṃ cakrāṇāṃ bhaṇyate'bhyudayaḥ // 1
7.d: अथ परमरहस्योऽयं चक्राणां भण्यतेऽभ्युदयः ॥ 1
7.m: Now this supreme secret, the rising of the wheels, is declared.

7.s:
ityayatnajamākhyātaṃ yatnajaṃ tu nigadyate /
bījapiṇḍātmakaṃ sarvaṃ saṃvidaḥ spandanātmatām // 2
7.d:
इत्ययत्नजमाख्यातं यत्नजं तु निगद्यते ।
बीजपिण्डात्मकं सर्वं संविदः स्पन्दनात्मताम् ॥ 2
7.m: Thus that which arises without effort has been explained; now, however, that which arises from effort is told, / which, consisting entirely of seed and cluster, brings about the dynamic vibration of consciousness // 2

7.s:
vidadhatparasaṃvittāvupāya iti varṇitam /
yathāraghaṭṭacakrāgraghaṭīyantraughavāhanam // 3
7.d:
विदधत्परसंवित्तावुपाय इति वर्णितम् ।
यथारघट्टचक्राग्रघटीयन्त्रौघवाहनम् ॥ 3
7.m: and is described as a means to supreme consciousness. / Just as the movement of the series of buckets at the rim of a waterwheel // 3

7.s:
ekānusaṃdhiyatnena citraṃ yantrodayaṃ bhajet /
ekānusaṃdhānabalājjāte mantrodaye'niśam // 4
7.d:
एकानुसंधियत्नेन चित्रं यन्त्रोदयं भजेत् ।
एकानुसंधानबलाज्जाते मन्त्रोदयेऽनिशम् ॥ 4
7.m: engages in a varied operation through the single effort of intention, / so when the rising of mantra occurs incessantly through the force of single intention, // 4

7.s:
tanmantradevatā yatnāttādātmyena prasīdati /
khe rasaikākṣi nityotthe tadardhaṃ dvikapiṇḍake // 5
7.d:
तन्मन्त्रदेवता यत्नात्तादात्म्येन प्रसीदति ।
खे रसैकाक्षि नित्योत्थे तदर्धं द्विकपिण्डके ॥ 5
7.m: the deity of that mantra is graciously revealed through effort by way of identity. / In the sky [of the heart], in the constant rising [of breath], it is twenty-one thousand six hundred; half of that is for a two-letter cluster; // 5

7.s:
trike sapta sahasrāṇi dviśatītyudayo mataḥ /
catuṣke tu sahasrāṇi pañca caiva catuḥśatī // 6
7.d:
त्रिके सप्त सहस्राणि द्विशतीत्युदयो मतः ।
चतुष्के तु सहस्राणि पञ्च चैव चतुःशती ॥ 6
7.m: for a triad, the rising is taught to be seven thousand two hundred; / but for a tetrad, it is five thousand four hundred; // 6

7.s:
pañcārṇe'bdhisahasrāṇi triśatī viṃśatistathā /
ṣaṭke sahasratritayaṃ ṣaṭśatī codayo bhavet // 7
7.d:
पञ्चार्णेऽब्धिसहस्राणि त्रिशती विंशतिस्तथा ।
षट्के सहस्रत्रितयं षट्शती चोदयो भवेत् ॥ 7
7.m: for a five-syllable [mantra], it is four thousand three hundred and twenty; / in a hexad, the rising would be three thousand six hundred; // 7

7.s:
saptake trisahasraṃ tu ṣaḍaśītyadhikaṃ smṛtam /
śataistu saptaviṃśatyā varṇāṣṭakavikalpite // 8
7.d:
सप्तके त्रिसहस्रं तु षडशीत्यधिकं स्मृतम् ।
शतैस्तु सप्तविंशत्या वर्णाष्टकविकल्पिते ॥ 8
7.m: in a heptad, it is recorded as three thousand and eighty-six; / and with twenty-seven hundred when arranged as an eight-syllable [mantra]; // 8

7.s:
caturviṃśatiśatyā tu navārṇeṣūdayo bhavet /
adhiṣaṣṭyekaviṃśatyā śatānāṃ daśavarṇake // 9
7.d:
चतुर्विंशतिशत्या तु नवार्णेषूदयो भवेत् ।
अधिषष्ट्येकविंशत्या शतानां दशवर्णके ॥ 9
7.m: in nine-syllable [mantras] the rising would be twenty-four hundred; / in a ten-syllable [mantra], it is twenty-one hundred and sixty; // 9

7.s:
ekānnaviṃśatiśataṃ catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ śivārṇake /
aṣṭādaśa śatāni syurudayo dvādaśārṇake // 10
7.d:
एकान्नविंशतिशतं चतुःषष्टिः शिवार्णके ।
अष्टादश शतानि स्युरुदयो द्वादशार्णके ॥ 10
7.m: in an eleven-syllable [mantra], it is nineteen hundred and sixty-four; / in a twelve-syllable [mantra], there would be eighteen hundred risings; // 10

7.s:
trayodaśārṇe dvāṣaṣṭyā śatāni kila ṣoḍaśa /
tricatvāriṃśatā pañcadaśeti bhuvanārṇake // 11
7.d:
त्रयोदशार्णे द्वाषष्ट्या शतानि किल षोडश ।
त्रिचत्वारिंशता पञ्चदशेति भुवनार्णके ॥ 11
7.m: in a thirteen-syllable [mantra], indeed, sixteen hundred and sixty-two; / in a fourteen-syllable [mantra], fifteen hundred and forty-three; // 11

7.s:
caturdaśaśatī khābdhiḥ syātpañcadaśavarṇake /
trayodaśaśatī sārdhā ṣoḍaśārṇe tu kathyate // 12
7.d:
चतुर्दशशती खाब्धिः स्यात्पञ्चदशवर्णके ।
त्रयोदशशती सार्धा षोडशार्णे तु कथ्यते ॥ 12
7.m: in a fifteen-syllable [mantra], it would be fourteen hundred and forty; / but in a sixteen-syllable [mantra], it is said to be thirteen hundred and fifty; // 12

7.s:
śatadvādaśikā saptadaśārṇe saikasaptatiḥ /
aṣṭādaśārṇe vijñeyā śatadvādaśikā budhaiḥ // 13
7.d:
शतद्वादशिका सप्तदशार्णे सैकसप्ततिः ।
अष्टादशार्णे विज्ञेया शतद्वादशिका बुधैः ॥ 13
7.m: in a seventeen-syllable [mantra], it is twelve hundred and seventy-one; / in an eighteen-syllable [mantra], it should be known by the wise as twelve hundred; // 13

7.s:
caturviṃśatisaṃkhyāke cakre navaśatī bhavet /
saptaviṃśatisaṃkhyāte tūdayo'ṣṭaśatātmakaḥ // 14
7.d:
चतुर्विंशतिसंख्याके चक्रे नवशती भवेत् ।
सप्तविंशतिसंख्याते तूदयोऽष्टशतात्मकः ॥ 14
7.m: in a wheel of twenty-four, there would be nine hundred; / but in one reckoned as twenty-seven, the rising consists of eight hundred; // 14

7.s:
dvātriṃśake mahācakre ṣaṭśatī pañcasaptatiḥ /
dvicaturviṃśake cakre sārdhāṃ śatacatuṣṭayīm // 15
7.d:
द्वात्रिंशके महाचक्रे षट्शती पञ्चसप्ततिः ।
द्विचतुर्विंशके चक्रे सार्धां शतचतुष्टयीम् ॥ 15
7.m: in the great wheel of thirty-two, it is six hundred and seventy-five; / in a wheel of forty-eight, four hundred and fifty: // 15

7.s:
udayaṃ piṇḍayogajñaḥ piṇḍamantreṣu lakṣayet /
catuṣpañcāśake cakre śatānāṃ tu catuṣṭayam // 16
7.d:
उदयं पिण्डयोगज्ञः पिण्डमन्त्रेषु लक्षयेत् ।
चतुष्पञ्चाशके चक्रे शतानां तु चतुष्टयम् ॥ 16
7.m: the knower of the union of clusters should observe this rising in cluster-mantras; / but in a wheel of fifty-four, it is four hundred; // 16

7.s:
saptatriṃśatsahārdhena triśatyaṣṭāṣṭake bhavet /
ardhamardhatribhāgaśca ṣaṭṣaṣṭirdviśatī bhavet // 17
7.d:
सप्तत्रिंशत्सहार्धेन त्रिशत्यष्टाष्टके भवेत् ।
अर्धमर्धत्रिभागश्च षट्षष्टिर्द्विशती भवेत् ॥ 17
7.m: in a sixty-four-[syllable wheel], it would be three hundred and thirty-seven and a half; / and two hundred and sixty-six and two-thirds; // 17

7.s:
ekāśītipade cakre udayaḥ prāṇacāragaḥ /
cakre tu ṣaṇṇavatyākhye sapādā dviśatī bhavet // 18
7.d:
एकाशीतिपदे चक्रे उदयः प्राणचारगः ।
चक्रे तु षण्णवत्याख्ये सपादा द्विशती भवेत् ॥ 18
7.m: in a wheel of eighty-one positions, the rising relates to the movement of vital breath; / while in the wheel called ninety-six, it would be two hundred and twenty-five; // 18

7.s:
aṣṭottaraśate cakre dviśatastūdayo bhavet /
krameṇetthamidaṃ cakraṃ ṣaṭkṛtvo dviguṇaṃ yadā // 19
7.d:
अष्टोत्तरशते चक्रे द्विशतस्तूदयो भवेत् ।
क्रमेणेत्थमिदं चक्रं षट्कृत्वो द्विगुणं यदा ॥ 19
7.m: in a wheel of one hundred and eight, the rising would be two hundred. / When this wheel, in this progressive manner, is doubled six times, // 19

7.s:
tato'pi dviguṇe'ṣṭāṃśasyārdhamadhyardhamekakam /
tato'pi sūkṣmakuśalairardhārdhādiprakalpane // 20
7.d:
ततोऽपि द्विगुणेऽष्टांशस्यार्धमध्यर्धमेककम् ।
ततोऽपि सूक्ष्मकुशलैरर्धार्धादिप्रकल्पने ॥ 20
7.m: and then doubled beyond that, [the movement is] one, one and a half, of half of an eighth part; / and beyond that, when conceived by those skilled in the subtle as half-of-a-half and so on, // 20

7.s:
bhāgaṣoḍaśakasthityā sūkṣmaścāro'bhilakṣyate /
evaṃ prayatnasaṃruddhaprāṇacārasya yoginaḥ // 21
7.d:
भागषोडशकस्थित्या सूक्ष्मश्चारोऽभिलक्ष्यते ।
एवं प्रयत्नसंरुद्धप्राणचारस्य योगिनः ॥ 21
7.m: the subtle movement is observed to abide as a sixteenth part. / For the yogin whose movement of vital breath is restrained by effort in this way, // 21

7.s:
krameṇa prāṇacārasya grāsa evopajāyate /
prāṇagrāsakramāvāptakālasaṃkarṣaṇasthitiḥ // 22
7.d:
क्रमेण प्राणचारस्य ग्रास एवोपजायते ।
प्राणग्रासक्रमावाप्तकालसंकर्षणस्थितिः ॥ 22
7.m: there arises gradually the devourment of the movement of vital breath. / Having attained the state of the drawing together of time through the gradual devourment of breath, // 22

7.s:
saṃvidekaiva pūrṇā syājjñānabhedavyapohanāt /
tathā hi prāṇacārasya navasyānudaye sati // 23
7.d:
संविदेकैव पूर्णा स्याज्ज्ञानभेदव्यपोहनात् ।
तथा हि प्राणचारस्य नवस्यानुदये सति ॥ 23
7.m: consciousness alone becomes full, because the differentiation of cognition is eliminated. / For when a new movement of vital breath does not arise, // 23

7.s:
na kālabhedajanito jñānabhedaḥ prakalpate /
saṃvedyabhedānna jñānaṃ bhinnaṃ śikharivṛttavat // 24
7.d:
न कालभेदजनितो ज्ञानभेदः प्रकल्पते ।
संवेद्यभेदान्न ज्ञानं भिन्नं शिखरिवृत्तवत् ॥ 24
7.m: no differentiation of cognition produced by the differentiation of time is constructed. / Cognition is not divided by the division of knowable objects, as with the cognition of a mountain. // 24

7.s:
kālastu bhedakastasya sa tu sūkṣmaḥ kṣaṇo mataḥ /
saukṣmyasya cāvadhirjñānaṃ yāvattiṣṭhati sa kṣaṇaḥ // 25
7.d:
कालस्तु भेदकस्तस्य स तु सूक्ष्मः क्षणो मतः ।
सौक्ष्म्यस्य चावधिर्ज्ञानं यावत्तिष्ठति स क्षणः ॥ 25
7.m: Time, however, is what divides it; and that [time] is held to be the subtle instant. / And the limit of subtleness is the instant for which a cognition endures; // 25

7.s:
anyathā na sa nirvaktuṃ nipuṇairapi pāryate /
jñānaṃ kiyadbhavettāvattadabhāvo na bhāsate // 26
7.d:
अन्यथा न स निर्वक्तुं निपुणैरपि पार्यते ।
ज्ञानं कियद्भवेत्तावत्तदभावो न भासते ॥ 26
7.m: otherwise, even the skilled are not able to define it. / As long as a cognition may endure, its absence does not appear; // 26

7.s:
tadabhāvaśca no tāvadyāvattatrākṣavartmani /
arthe vātmapradeśe vā na saṃyogavibhāgitā // 27
7.d:
तदभावश्च नो तावद्यावत्तत्राक्षवर्त्मनि ।
अर्थे वात्मप्रदेशे वा न संयोगविभागिता ॥ 27
7.m: and its absence does not occur as long as there is no conjunction or disjunction / in the pathway of the sense-faculties, in the object, or in a region of oneself. // 27

7.s:
sā cedudayate spandamayī tatprāṇagā dhruvam /
bhavedeva tataḥ prāṇaspandābhāve na sā bhavet // 28
7.d:
सा चेदुदयते स्पन्दमयी तत्प्राणगा ध्रुवम् ।
भवेदेव ततः प्राणस्पन्दाभावे न सा भवेत् ॥ 28
7.m: If that [conjunction or disjunction] arises, consisting of dynamic vibration, it must surely reside in vital breath; / therefore, in the absence of the dynamic vibration of vital breath, it would not exist. // 28

7.s:
tadabhāvānna vijñānābhāvaḥ saivaṃ tu saiva dhīḥ /
na cāsau vastuto dīrghā kālabhedavyapohanāt // 29
7.d:
तदभावान्न विज्ञानाभावः सैवं तु सैव धीः ।
न चासौ वस्तुतो दीर्घा कालभेदव्यपोहनात् ॥ 29
7.m: In its absence, there is no absence of cognition; rather, the intellect remains just that. / Nor is this [cognition] in reality prolonged, because the differentiation of time has been eliminated; // 29

7.s:
vastuto hyata eveyaṃ kālaṃ saṃvinna saṃspṛśet /
ata ekaiva saṃvittirnānārūpe tathātathā // 30
7.d:
वस्तुतो ह्यत एवेयं कालं संविन्न संस्पृशेत् ।
अत एकैव संवित्तिर्नानारूपे तथातथा ॥ 30
7.m: for this very reason, in reality, consciousness does not touch time. / Therefore, consciousness is only one, though experiencing variously // 30

7.s:
vindānā nirvikalpāpi vikalpo bhāvagocare /
spandāntaraṃ na yāvattaduditaṃ tāvadeva saḥ // 31
7.d:
विन्दाना निर्विकल्पापि विकल्पो भावगोचरे ।
स्पन्दान्तरं न यावत्तदुदितं तावदेव सः ॥ 31
7.m: in diverse forms, and even though non-conceptual, it is a conceptual construct in the realm of entities. / As long as another dynamic vibration has not arisen, for that long alone // 31

7.s:
tāvāneko vikalpaḥ syādvividhaṃ vastu kalpayan /
ye tvitthaṃ na vidusteṣāṃ vikalpo nopapadyate // 32
7.d:
तावानेको विकल्पः स्याद्विविधं वस्तु कल्पयन् ।
ये त्वित्थं न विदुस्तेषां विकल्पो नोपपद्यते ॥ 32
7.m: it remains a single conceptual construct constructing various things. / But for those who do not understand it thus, a conceptual construct is not tenable; // 32

7.s:
sa hyeko na bhavetkaścit trijagatyāpi jātucit /
śabdārūṣaṇayā jñānaṃ vikalpaḥ kila kathyate // 33
7.d:
स ह्येको न भवेत्कश्चित् त्रिजगत्यापि जातुचित् ।
शब्दारूषणया ज्ञानं विकल्पः किल कथ्यते ॥ 33
7.m: for no single [construct] would ever exist even in the three worlds. / A cognition is said to be a conceptual construct because it is permeated by words, // 33

7.s:
sā ca syātkramikaivetthaṃ kiṃ kathaṃ ko vikalpayet /
ghaṭa ityapi neyānsyādvikalpaḥ kā kathā sthitau // 34
7.d:
सा च स्यात्क्रमिकैवेत्थं किं कथं को विकल्पयेत् ।
घट इत्यपि नेयान्स्याद्विकल्पः का कथा स्थितौ ॥ 34
7.m: and that [verbalisation] must occur only in succession; thus, what would anyone conceptualise, and how? / Even ‘pot’ would not be this [single] conceptual construct—what to say of its continuity? // 34

7.s:
na vikalpaśca ko'pyasti yo mātrāmātraniṣṭhitaḥ /
na ca jñānasamūho'sti teṣāmayugapatsthiteḥ // 35
7.d:
न विकल्पश्च कोऽप्यस्ति यो मात्रामात्रनिष्ठितः ।
न च ज्ञानसमूहोऽस्ति तेषामयुगपत्स्थितेः ॥ 35
7.m: And there is no conceptual construct that rests on merely a single instant; / nor is there an aggregate of cognitions, because they do not exist simultaneously. // 35

7.s:
tenāstaṅgata evaiṣa vyavahāro vikalpajaḥ /
tasmātspandāntaraṃ yāvannodiyāttāvadekakam // 36
7.d:
तेनास्तङ्गत एवैष व्यवहारो विकल्पजः ।
तस्मात्स्पन्दान्तरं यावन्नोदियात्तावदेककम् ॥ 36
7.m: Therefore, this conventional transaction born of conceptual constructs would completely vanish. / Hence, as long as another dynamic vibration does not arise, for that long a single // 36

7.s:
vijñānaṃ tadvikalpātmadharmakoṭīrapi spṛśet /
ekāśītipadodāraśaktyāmarśātmakastataḥ // 37
7.d:
विज्ञानं तद्विकल्पात्मधर्मकोटीरपि स्पृशेत् ।
एकाशीतिपदोदारशक्त्यामर्शात्मकस्ततः ॥ 37
7.m: cognition, though of the nature of a conceptual construct, touches even millions of properties. / Therefore, the conceptual construct whose nature is the reflective awareness of power, sublime with eighty-one positions, // 37

7.s:
vikalpaḥ śivatādāyī pūrvameva nirūpitaḥ /
yathā karṇau nartayāmītyevaṃ yatnāttathā bhavet // 38
7.d:
विकल्पः शिवतादायी पूर्वमेव निरूपितः ।
यथा कर्णौ नर्तयामीत्येवं यत्नात्तथा भवेत् ॥ 38
7.m: which bestows the state of Śiva, has already been explained. / Just as [one thinks] ‘I will move my ears’ and it happens thus through effort, // 38

7.s:
cakracāragatādyatnāttadvattaccakragaiva dhīḥ /
japahomārcanādīnāṃ prāṇasāmyamato vidhiḥ // 39
7.d:
चक्रचारगताद्यत्नात्तद्वत्तच्चक्रगैव धीः ।
जपहोमार्चनादीनां प्राणसाम्यमतो विधिः ॥ 39
7.m: so through the initial effort directed toward the movement of the wheel, the intellect conforms to that wheel. / Therefore the rule for recitation, oblations, worship, and the like is the equilibrium of vital breath. // 39

7.s:
siddhāmate kuṇḍalinīśaktiḥ prāṇasamonmanā /
uktaṃ ca yoginīkaule tadetatparameśinā // 40
7.d:
सिद्धामते कुण्डलिनीशक्तिः प्राणसमोन्मना ।
उक्तं च योगिनीकौले तदेतत्परमेशिना ॥ 40
7.m: In the Siddhāmata, the kuṇḍalinī power is the Unminded equal to vital breath. / And this was stated by the Supreme Lord in the Yoginīkaula: // 40

7.s:
padamantrākṣare cakre vibhāgaṃ śaktitattvagam /
padeṣu kṛtvā mantrajño japādau phalabhāgbhavet // 41
7.d:
पदमन्त्राक्षरे चक्रे विभागं शक्तितत्त्वगम् ।
पदेषु कृत्वा मन्त्रज्ञो जपादौ फलभाग्भवेत् ॥ 41
7.m: ‘Having made the division pertaining to the principle of power in the wheel of words, mantras, and syllables, / into words, the knower of mantra partakes of the fruit in recitation and the like. // 41

7.s:
dvitrisaptāṣṭasaṃkhyātaṃ lopayecchatikodayam /
iti śaktisthitā mantrā vidyā vā cakranāyakāḥ // 42
7.d:
द्वित्रिसप्ताष्टसंख्यातं लोपयेच्छतिकोदयम् ।
इति शक्तिस्थिता मन्त्रा विद्या वा चक्रनायकाः ॥ 42
7.m: One should cause the rising of hundreds counted as two, three, seven, and eight to vanish; / thus mantras abiding in power, or vidyās, the lords of the wheel, // 42

7.s:
padapiṇḍasvarūpeṇa jñātvā yojyāḥ sadā priye /
nityodaye mahātattve udayasthe sadāśive // 43
7.d:
पदपिण्डस्वरूपेण ज्ञात्वा योज्याः सदा प्रिये ।
नित्योदये महातत्त्वे उदयस्थे सदाशिवे ॥ 43
7.m: having been understood in the nature of word and cluster, should always be united, O beloved, / in the constantly rising great principle, in Sadāśiva who abides in the rising. // 43

7.s:
ayuktāḥ śaktimārge tu na japtāścodayena ye /
te na siddhyanti yatnena japtāḥ koṭiśatairapi // 44
7.d:
अयुक्ताः शक्तिमार्गे तु न जप्ताश्चोदयेन ये ।
ते न सिद्ध्यन्ति यत्नेन जप्ताः कोटिशतैरपि ॥ 44
7.m: Those which are not united on the path of power and not recited with the rising / do not succeed through effort, even when recited hundreds of millions of times. // 44

7.s:
mālāmantreṣu sarveṣu mānaso japa ucyate /
upāṃśurvā śaktyudayaṃ teṣāṃ na parikalpayet // 45
7.d:
मालामन्त्रेषु सर्वेषु मानसो जप उच्यते ।
उपांशुर्वा शक्त्युदयं तेषां न परिकल्पयेत् ॥ 45
7.m: Mental recitation is taught for all rosary-mantras, / or whispered; one should not construct a rising of power for them. // 45

7.s:
padamantreṣu sarveṣu yāvattatpadaśaktigam /
śakyate satataṃ yuktaistāvajjapyaṃ tu sādhakaiḥ // 46
7.d:
पदमन्त्रेषु सर्वेषु यावत्तत्पदशक्तिगम् ।
शक्यते सततं युक्तैस्तावज्जप्यं तु साधकैः ॥ 46
7.m: In all word-mantras, as far as it reaches the power of that word, / adepts should recite as long as they are able, being constantly united; // 46

7.s:
tāvatī teṣu vai saṃkhyā padeṣu padasaṃjñitā /
tāvantamudayaṃ kṛtvā tripadoktyāditaḥ kramāt // 47
7.d:
तावती तेषु वै संख्या पदेषु पदसंज्ञिता ।
तावन्तमुदयं कृत्वा त्रिपदोक्त्यादितः क्रमात् ॥ 47
7.m: that is indeed the number in them designated by the word “pada”; / having performed that rising, gradually, beginning with the pronunciation of three words, // 47

7.s:
dvādaśākhye dvādaśite cakre sārdhaṃ śataṃ bhavet /
udayastaddhi sacatuścatvāriṃśacchataṃ bhavet // 48
7.d:
द्वादशाख्ये द्वादशिते चक्रे सार्धं शतं भवेत् ।
उदयस्तद्धि सचतुश्चत्वारिंशच्छतं भवेत् ॥ 48
7.m: in the wheel called twelve, divided into twelve, there would be one hundred and fifty; / that rising would indeed be one hundred and forty-four.’ // 48

7.s:
ṣoḍaśākhye dvādaśite dvānavatyadhike śate /
cārārdhena samaṃ proktaṃ śataṃ dvādaśakādhikam // 49
7.d:
षोडशाख्ये द्वादशिते द्वानवत्यधिके शते ।
चारार्धेन समं प्रोक्तं शतं द्वादशकाधिकम् ॥ 49
7.m: In the twelvefold [division] of the sixteen-spoked [wheel], it is one hundred ninety-two; / along with half a movement, it is stated to be one hundred twelve.

7.s:
ṣoḍaśākhye ṣoḍaśite bhaveccaturaśītigaḥ /
udayo dviśataṃ taddhi ṣaṭpañcāśatsamuttaram // 50
7.d:
षोडशाख्ये षोडशिते भवेच्चतुरशीतिगः ।
उदयो द्विशतं तद्धि षट्पञ्चाशत्समुत्तरम् ॥ 50
7.m: In the sixteenfold [division] of the sixteen-spoked [wheel], the rising consists of eighty-four; / that indeed becomes two hundred fifty-six.

7.s:
cārāṣṭabhāgāṃstrīnatra kathayantyadhikānbudhāḥ /
aṣṭāṣṭake dvādaśite pādārdhaṃ viṃśatiṃ vasūn // 51
7.d:
चाराष्टभागांस्त्रीनत्र कथयन्त्यधिकान्बुधाः ।
अष्टाष्टके द्वादशिते पादार्धं विंशतिं वसून् ॥ 51
7.m: Here the wise declare three eighths of a movement as surplus. / In the twelvefold [division] of the sixty-four [wheel], there are eight, twenty, and half a quarter [820.5];

7.s:
udayaḥ saptaśatikā sāṣṭā ṣaṣṭiryato hi saḥ /
eṣa cakrodayaḥ proktaḥ sādhakānāṃ hitāvahaḥ // 52
7.d:
उदयः सप्तशतिका साष्टा षष्टिर्यतो हि सः ।
एष चक्रोदयः प्रोक्तः साधकानां हितावहः ॥ 52
7.m: for the rising is seven hundred sixty-eight. / This rising of the wheels has been proclaimed, bringing benefit to adepts.

7.s:
niruddhya mānasīrvṛttīścakre viśrāntimāgataḥ /
vyutthāya yāvadviśrāmyettāvaccārodayo hyayam // 53
7.d:
निरुद्ध्य मानसीर्वृत्तीश्चक्रे विश्रान्तिमागतः ।
व्युत्थाय यावद्विश्राम्येत्तावच्चारोदयो ह्ययम् ॥ 53
7.m: Having restrained the mental activities, one arrives at rest in the wheel; / emerging, for as long as one rests, just so long indeed is this rising of the movement.

7.s:
pūrṇe samudaye tvatra praveśaikātmyanirgamāḥ /
traya ityata evoktaḥ siddhau madhyodayo varaḥ // 54
7.d:
पूर्णे समुदये त्वत्र प्रवेशैकात्म्यनिर्गमाः ।
त्रय इत्यत एवोक्तः सिद्धौ मध्योदयो वरः ॥ 54
7.m: In the complete rising, however, there are here three: entry, absorption, and egress; / for this very reason it is taught that in achieving accomplishment, the middle rising is best.

7.s:
ādyantodayanirmuktā madhyamodayasaṃyutāḥ /
mantravidyācakragaṇāḥ siddhibhājo bhavanti hi // 55
7.d:
आद्यन्तोदयनिर्मुक्ता मध्यमोदयसंयुताः ।
मन्त्रविद्याचक्रगणाः सिद्धिभाजो भवन्ति हि ॥ 55
7.m: Free from the initial and final risings, and endowed with the middle rising, / the assemblies of the wheels of mantras and vidyās indeed partake of accomplishment.

7.s:
mantracakrodayajñastu vidyācakrodayārthavit /
kṣipraṃ siddhyediti proktaṃ śrīmaddviṃśatike trike // 56
7.d:
मन्त्रचक्रोदयज्ञस्तु विद्याचक्रोदयार्थवित् ।
क्षिप्रं सिद्ध्येदिति प्रोक्तं श्रीमद्द्विंशतिके त्रिके ॥ 56
7.m: One who knows the rising of the mantra-wheel, however, and knows the meaning of the rising of the vidyā-wheel / is said to achieve spiritual accomplishment swiftly in the venerable Triṃśikā-Trika.

7.s:
dvistriścaturvā mātrābhirvidyāṃ vā cakrameva vā /
tattvodayayutaṃ nityaṃ pṛthagbhūtaṃ japetsadā // 57
7.d:
द्विस्त्रिश्चतुर्वा मात्राभिर्विद्यां वा चक्रमेव वा ।
तत्त्वोदययुतं नित्यं पृथग्भूतं जपेत्सदा ॥ 57
7.m: Whether by two, three, or four measures (mātrā), the vidyā or the wheel / should always be recited individually, united constantly with the rising of the principles (tattva).

7.s:
piṇḍākṣarapadairmantramekaikaṃ śaktitattvagam /
bahvakṣarastu yo mantro vidyā vā cakrameva vā // 58
7.d:
पिण्डाक्षरपदैर्मन्त्रमेकैकं शक्तितत्त्वगम् ।
बह्वक्षरस्तु यो मन्त्रो विद्या वा चक्रमेव वा ॥ 58
7.m: The mantra consisting of a single cluster of syllables reaches into the principle of power (śaktitattva); / but the mantra consisting of many syllables, or a vidyā, or a wheel,

7.s:
śaktisthaṃ naiva taṃ tatra vibhāgastvoṃnamontagaḥ /
asmiṃstattvodaye tasmādahorātrastriśastriśaḥ // 59
7.d:
शक्तिस्थं नैव तं तत्र विभागस्त्वोंनमोन्तगः ।
अस्मिंस्तत्त्वोदये तस्मादहोरात्रस्त्रिशस्त्रिशः ॥ 59
7.m: does not abide purely in power, for the division terminates in 'oṃ namaḥ'. / In this rising of the principles, therefore, day and night are divided threefold, threefold;

7.s:
vibhajyate vibhāgaśca punareva triśastriśaḥ /
pūrvodaye tu viśramya dvitīyenollasedyadā // 60
7.d:
विभज्यते विभागश्च पुनरेव त्रिशस्त्रिशः ।
पूर्वोदये तु विश्रम्य द्वितीयेनोल्लसेद्यदा ॥ 60
7.m: and each division is once again divided threefold, threefold. / Resting in the prior rising, when it blazes forth through the second,

7.s:
viśeccārdhardhikāyogāttadoktārdhodayo bhavet /
yadā pūrṇodayātmā tu samaḥ kālastrike sphuret // 61
7.d:
विशेच्चार्धर्धिकायोगात्तदोक्तार्धोदयो भवेत् ।
यदा पूर्णोदयात्मा तु समः कालस्त्रिके स्फुरेत् ॥ 61
7.m: and enters by the junction of increasing halves, then occurs the stated half-rising. / When, however, time shines uniform as the essence of the complete rising in the Trika,

7.s:
praveśaviśrāntyullāse syātsvatryaṃśodayastadā /
etyeṣa kālavibhavaḥ prāṇa eva pratiṣṭhitaḥ // 62
7.d:
प्रवेशविश्रान्त्युल्लासे स्यात्स्वत्र्यंशोदयस्तदा ।
एत्येष कालविभवः प्राण एव प्रतिष्ठितः ॥ 62
7.m: in entry, rest, and blazing forth, then there occurs the rising of its own three parts. / In this way, this majesty of time is grounded solely in the breath.

7.s:
sa spade khe sa taccityāṃ tenāsyāṃ viśvaniṣṭhiatiḥ /
ataḥ saṃvitpratiṣṭhānau yato viśvalayodayau // 63
7.d:
स स्पदे खे स तच्चित्यां तेनास्यां विश्वनिष्ठिअतिः ।
अतः संवित्प्रतिष्ठानौ यतो विश्वलयोदयौ ॥ 63
7.m: That [breath] is in pulsation (spanda), that in the void (kha), that in consciousness; through that, the universe is established in this [consciousness]. / Therefore, the dissolution and rising of the universe are grounded in consciousness;

7.s:
śaktyante'dhvani tatspandāsaṃkhyātā vāstavī tataḥ /
uktaṃ śrīmālinītantre gātre yatraiva kutracit // 64
7.d:
शक्त्यन्तेऽध्वनि तत्स्पन्दासंख्याता वास्तवी ततः ।
उक्तं श्रीमालिनीतन्त्रे गात्रे यत्रैव कुत्रचित् ॥ 64
7.m: hence, at the end of power on the path, its pulsation is countless and real. / In the venerable Mālinītantra it is stated: wherever in the body

7.s:
vikāra upajāyeta tattattvaṃ tattvamuttamam /
prāṇe pratiṣṭhitaḥ kālastadāviṣṭā ca yattanuḥ // 65
7.d:
विकार उपजायेत तत्तत्त्वं तत्त्वमुत्तमम् ।
प्राणे प्रतिष्ठितः कालस्तदाविष्टा च यत्तनुः ॥ 65
7.m: a modification arises, that principle is the supreme principle. / Time is established in the breath, and the body is pervaded by it;

7.s:
dehe pratiṣṭhitasyāsya tato rūpaṃ nirūpyate /
citspandaprāṇavṛttīnāmantyā yā sthūlatā suṣiḥ // 66
7.d:
देहे प्रतिष्ठितस्यास्य ततो रूपं निरूप्यते ।
चित्स्पन्दप्राणवृत्तीनामन्त्या या स्थूलता सुषिः ॥ 66
7.m: therefore its form as grounded in the body is now described. / The ultimate grossness, the hollow cavity, of the pulsations of consciousness and the activities of breath,

7.s:
sā nāḍīrūpatāmetya dehaṃ saṃtānayedimam /
śrīsvacchande'ta evoktaṃ yathā parṇaṃ svatantubhiḥ // 67
7.d:
सा नाडीरूपतामेत्य देहं संतानयेदिमम् ।
श्रीस्वच्छन्देऽत एवोक्तं यथा पर्णं स्वतन्तुभिः ॥ 67
7.m: assuming the form of channels (nāḍī), weaves this body together. / Therefore in the venerable Svacchanda it is said: just as a leaf is pervaded by its own veins,

7.s:
vyāptaṃ tadvattanurdvāradvāribhāvena nāḍibhiḥ /
pādāṅguṣṭhādikordhvasthabrahmakuṇḍalikāntagaḥ // 68
7.d:
व्याप्तं तद्वत्तनुर्द्वारद्वारिभावेन नाडिभिः ।
पादाङ्गुष्ठादिकोर्ध्वस्थब्रह्मकुण्डलिकान्तगः ॥ 68
7.m: so the body is pervaded by the channels in the relation of gateways and that which passes through them. / Ranging from the big toe and the like up to the high-seated brahmakuṇḍalikā,

7.s:
kālaḥ samastaścaturaśītāvevāṅguleṣvitaḥ /
dvādaśāntāvadhiṃ kiṃcitsūkṣmakālasthitiṃ viduḥ // 69
7.d:
कालः समस्तश्चतुरशीतावेवाङ्गुलेष्वितः ।
द्वादशान्तावधिं किंचित्सूक्ष्मकालस्थितिं विदुः ॥ 69
7.m: the entirety of time extends precisely over eighty-four finger-breadths. / Beyond this, extending up to the dvādaśānta, they know the subtle state of time to be somewhat [different].

7.s:
ṣaṇṇavatyāmadhaḥ ṣaḍdvikramāccāṣṭottaraṃ śatam /
atra madhyamasaṃcāriprāṇodayalayāntare // 70
7.d:
षण्णवत्यामधः षड्द्विक्रमाच्चाष्टोत्तरं शतम् ।
अत्र मध्यमसंचारिप्राणोदयलयान्तरे ॥ 70
7.m: In ninety-six [finger-breadths], downwards, in the order of six and two, it is one hundred and eight. / Here, within the interval of the rising and dissolution of the breath moving in the central channel,

7.s:
viśve sṛṣṭilayāste tu citrā vāyvantarakramāt /
ityeṣa sūkṣmaparimarśanaśīlanīyaścakrodayo'nubhavaśāstradṛśā mayoktaḥ // 71
7.d:
विश्वे सृष्टिलयास्ते तु चित्रा वाय्वन्तरक्रमात् ।
इत्येष सूक्ष्मपरिमर्शनशीलनीयश्चक्रोदयोऽनुभवशास्त्रदृशा मयोक्तः ॥ 71
7.m: the diverse emissions and dissolutions of the universe take place according to the succession of internal winds. / In this manner, this rising of the wheels, which is to be practiced through subtle reflective awareness, has been expounded by me through the vision of experiential scriptures.

8.s: deśādhvano'pyatha samāsavikāsayogātsaṃgīyate vidhirayaṃ śivaśāstradṛṣṭaḥ // 1
8.d: देशाध्वनोऽप्यथ समासविकासयोगात्संगीयते विधिरयं शिवशास्त्रदृष्टः ॥ 1
8.m: Next, this rule regarding the spatial path seen in Śiva's scriptures is proclaimed through the conjunction of synthesis and expansion.

8.s:
vicārito'yaṃ kālādhvā kriyāśaktimayaḥ prabhoḥ /
mūrtivaicitryajastajjo deśādhvātha nirūpyate // 2
8.d:
विचारितोऽयं कालाध्वा क्रियाशक्तिमयः प्रभोः ।
मूर्तिवैचित्र्यजस्तज्जो देशाध्वाथ निरूप्यते ॥ 2
8.m: This temporal path, consisting of the Lord's power of action, has been examined; / now the spatial path, born from it and produced from the diversity of forms, is described.

8.s:
adhvā samasta evāyaṃ cinmātre saṃpratiṣṭhitaḥ /
yattatra nahi viśrāntaṃ tannabhaḥkusumāyate // 3
8.d:
अध्वा समस्त एवायं चिन्मात्रे संप्रतिष्ठितः ।
यत्तत्र नहि विश्रान्तं तन्नभःकुसुमायते ॥ 3
8.m: This entire path is grounded solely in pure consciousness. / Whatever does not rest therein is like a flower in the sky.

8.s:
saṃviddvāreṇa tatsṛṣṭe śūnye dhiyi marutsu ca /
nāḍīcakrānucakreṣu bahirdehe'dhvasaṃsthitiḥ // 4
8.d:
संविद्द्वारेण तत्सृष्टे शून्ये धियि मरुत्सु च ।
नाडीचक्रानुचक्रेषु बहिर्देहेऽध्वसंस्थितिः ॥ 4
8.m: Through consciousness, the path is situated in the void, the intellect, the winds created by it, / in the channels, wheels, and subsidiary wheels, and externally in the body.

8.s:
tatrādhvaivaṃ nirūpyo'yaṃ yatastatprakriyākramam /
anusaṃdadhadeva drāg yogī bhairavatāṃ vrajet // 5
8.d:
तत्राध्वैवं निरूप्योऽयं यतस्तत्प्रक्रियाक्रमम् ।
अनुसंदधदेव द्राग् योगी भैरवतां व्रजेत् ॥ 5
8.m: There, this path is to be investigated in such a manner because, by continuously contemplating its orderly scheme, / the yogi rapidly attains the state of Bhairava.

8.s:
didṛkṣayaiva sarvārthān yadā vyāpyāvatiṣṭhate /
tadā kiṃ bahunoktena ityuktaṃ spandaśāsane // 6
8.d:
दिदृक्षयैव सर्वार्थान् यदा व्याप्यावतिष्ठते ।
तदा किं बहुनोक्तेन इत्युक्तं स्पन्दशासने ॥ 6
8.m: As is stated in the teachings on Spanda: 'When one stands pervading all things merely by the desire to perceive [them], / then what is the use of speaking much?'

8.s:
jñātvā samastamadhvānaṃ tadīśeṣu vilāpayet /
tān dehaprāṇadhīcakre pūrvavad gālayetkramāt // 7
8.d:
ज्ञात्वा समस्तमध्वानं तदीशेषु विलापयेत् ।
तान् देहप्राणधीचक्रे पूर्ववद् गालयेत्क्रमात् ॥ 7
8.m: Having known the entire path, one should dissolve it into its lords; / these one should gradually dissolve, as before, into the wheel of body, breath, and intellect.

8.s:
tatsamastaṃ svasaṃvittau sā saṃvidbharitātmikā /
upāsyamānā saṃsārasāgarapralayānalaḥ // 8
8.d:
तत्समस्तं स्वसंवित्तौ सा संविद्भरितात्मिका ।
उपास्यमाना संसारसागरप्रलयानलः ॥ 8
8.m: All that is [then dissolved] into one's own consciousness; that consciousness, full in its essence, / when contemplated, is the fire of cosmic dissolution for the ocean of cyclic existence (saṃsāra).

8.s:
śrīmahīkṣottare caitānadhveśān gururabravīt /
brahmānantātpradhānāntaṃ viṣṇuḥ puṃsaḥ kalāntagam // 9
8.d:
श्रीमहीक्षोत्तरे चैतानध्वेशान् गुरुरब्रवीत् ।
ब्रह्मानन्तात्प्रधानान्तं विष्णुः पुंसः कलान्तगम् ॥ 9
8.m: And in the venerable Mahīkṣottara the guru declared these lords of the path: / Brahmā from Ananta up to Pradhāna; Viṣṇu ranges from the soul up to kalā;

8.s:
rudro granthau ca māyāyāmīśaḥ sādākhyagocare /
anāśritaḥ śivastasmādvyāptā tadvyāpakaḥ paraḥ // 10
8.d:
रुद्रो ग्रन्थौ च मायायामीशः सादाख्यगोचरे ।
अनाश्रितः शिवस्तस्माद्व्याप्ता तद्व्यापकः परः ॥ 10
8.m: Rudra is in the knot and in Māyā; Īśa is in the sphere of Sadāśiva; / Śiva is Anāśrita; beyond that is the supreme pervader which encompasses it.

8.s:
evaṃ śivatvamāpannamiti matvā nyarūpyata /
na prakriyāparaṃ jñānamiti svacchandaśāsane // 11
8.d:
एवं शिवत्वमापन्नमिति मत्वा न्यरूप्यत ।
न प्रक्रियापरं ज्ञानमिति स्वच्छन्दशासने ॥ 11
8.m: Having considered that it has thus attained Śiva-hood, it was determined; / for in the doctrine of the Svacchanda it is said: 'Knowledge is not superior to the cosmic order (prakriyā).'

8.s:
triśiraḥśāsane bodho mūlamadhyāgrakalpitaḥ /
ṣaṭtriṃśattattvasaṃrambhaḥ smṛtirbhedavikalpanā // 12
8.d:
त्रिशिरःशासने बोधो मूलमध्याग्रकल्पितः ।
षट्त्रिंशत्तत्त्वसंरम्भः स्मृतिर्भेदविकल्पना ॥ 12
8.m: In the teachings of the Triśirobhairava, consciousness is conceived as root, middle, and tip: / the energetic arousal of the thirty-six principles is memory and differentiated conceptualisation.

8.s:
avyāhatavibhāgo'smibhāvo mūlaṃ tu bodhagam /
samastatattvabhāvo'yaṃ svātmanyevāvibhāgakaḥ // 13
8.d:
अव्याहतविभागोऽस्मिभावो मूलं तु बोधगम् ।
समस्ततत्त्वभावोऽयं स्वात्मन्येवाविभागकः ॥ 13
8.m: The unimpeded sense of 'I am' is the root belonging to consciousness; / this existence of all principles is undivided within one's own self alone.

8.s:
bodhamadhyaṃ bhavetkiṃcidādhārādheyalakṣaṇam /
tattvabhedavibhāgena svabhāvasthitilakṣaṇam // 14
8.d:
बोधमध्यं भवेत्किंचिदाधाराधेयलक्षणम् ।
तत्त्वभेदविभागेन स्वभावस्थितिलक्षणम् ॥ 14
8.m: The middle of consciousness has the character of somewhat [distinguished] container and contained; / it is characterised by abiding in one's own nature through the differentiation of principles.

8.s:
bodhāgraṃ tattu vidbodhaṃ nistaraṅgaṃ bṛhatsukham /
saṃvidekātmatānītabhūtabhāvapurādikaḥ // 15
8.d:
बोधाग्रं तत्तु विद्बोधं निस्तरङ्गं बृहत्सुखम् ।
संविदेकात्मतानीतभूतभावपुरादिकः ॥ 15
8.m: The tip of consciousness, however, is pure awakening, wave-free, immense bliss, / in which physical elements, states, worlds, and the like are brought into identity with consciousness;

8.s:
avyavacchinnasaṃvittirbhairavaḥ parameśvaraḥ /
śrīdevyāyāmale coktaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśattattvasundaram // 16
8.d:
अव्यवच्छिन्नसंवित्तिर्भैरवः परमेश्वरः ।
श्रीदेव्यायामले चोक्तं षट्त्रिंशत्तत्त्वसुन्दरम् ॥ 16
8.m: it is unfragmented consciousness, Bhairava, the Supreme Lord. / And in the venerable Devyāyāmala it is stated: 'Beautiful with the thirty-six principles,

8.s:
adhvānaṃ ṣaḍvidhaṃ dhyāyansadyaḥ śivamayo bhavet /
yadyapyamuṣya nāthasya saṃvittyanatirekiṇaḥ // 17
8.d:
अध्वानं षड्विधं ध्यायन्सद्यः शिवमयो भवेत् ।
यद्यप्यमुष्य नाथस्य संवित्त्यनतिरेकिणः ॥ 17
8.m: meditating on the sixfold path, one immediately becomes identical with Śiva.' / Although for this Lord, who does not transcend consciousness

8.s:
pūrṇasyordhvādimadhyāntavyavasthā nāsti vāstavī /
tathāpi pratipattṝṇāṃ pratipādayitustathā // 18
8.d:
पूर्णस्योर्ध्वादिमध्यान्तव्यवस्था नास्ति वास्तवी ।
तथापि प्रतिपत्तॄणां प्रतिपादयितुस्तथा ॥ 18
8.m: and is full, there is no real arrangement of above, middle, end, and so forth, / nevertheless, for learners as well as for the teacher,

8.s:
svasvarūpānusāreṇa madhyāditvādikalpanāḥ /
tataḥ pramātṛsaṃkalpaniyamāt pārthivaṃ viduḥ // 19
8.d:
स्वस्वरूपानुसारेण मध्यादित्वादिकल्पनाः ।
ततः प्रमातृसंकल्पनियमात् पार्थिवं विदुः ॥ 19
8.m: conceptions such as middle and the rest are made according to their own nature. / Therefore, by the restriction of the knower's intention, they know the earthly

8.s:
tattvaṃ sarvāntarālasthaṃ yatsarvāvaraṇairvṛtam /
tadatra pārthive tattve kathyate bhuvanasthitiḥ // 20
8.d:
तत्त्वं सर्वान्तरालस्थं यत्सर्वावरणैर्वृतम् ।
तदत्र पार्थिवे तत्त्वे कथ्यते भुवनस्थितिः ॥ 20
8.m: principle to be situated in the interior of all, covered by all envelopes. / Now, the arrangement of worlds in this earthly principle is explained.

8.s:
netā kaṭāharudrāṇāmanantaḥ kāmasevinām /
potārūḍho jalasyāntarmadyapānavighūrṇitaḥ // 21
8.d:
नेता कटाहरुद्राणामनन्तः कामसेविनाम् ।
पोतारूढो जलस्यान्तर्मद्यपानविघूर्णितः ॥ 21
8.m: The leader of the Kaṭāha-Rudras, Ananta, of those who pursue desires, / mounted on a boat in the midst of the water, reelingly drunk from drinking wine,

8.s:
sa devaṃ bhairavaṃ dhyāyan nāgaiśca parivāritaḥ /
kālāgrerbhuvanaṃ cordhve koṭiyojanamucchritam // 22
8.d:
स देवं भैरवं ध्यायन् नागैश्च परिवारितः ।
कालाग्रेर्भुवनं चोर्ध्वे कोटियोजनमुच्छ्रितम् ॥ 22
8.m: he, surrounded by serpents, meditates on the god Bhairava; / and above is the world of Kālāgni, rising to a height of one crore yojanas.

8.s:
lokānāṃ bhasmasādbhāvabhayānnordhva sa vīkṣate /
sa ca vyāptāpi viśvasya yasmātpluṣyannimāṃ bhuvam // 23
8.d:
लोकानां भस्मसाद्भावभयान्नोर्ध्व स वीक्षते ।
स च व्याप्तापि विश्वस्य यस्मात्प्लुष्यन्निमां भुवम् ॥ 23
8.m: For fear of turning the worlds to ashes, he does not look upward; / and even though he permeates the universe, because scorching this earth

8.s:
narakebhyaḥ purā vyaktastenāsau tadadho mataḥ /
daśa koṭyo vibhorjvālā tadardha śūnyamūrdhvataḥ // 24
8.d:
नरकेभ्यः पुरा व्यक्तस्तेनासौ तदधो मतः ।
दश कोट्यो विभोर्ज्वाला तदर्ध शून्यमूर्ध्वतः ॥ 24
8.m: he was manifested before the hells, therefore he is considered to be below them. / The lord's flame is ten crores [of leagues]; half of that, above, is empty space.

8.s:
tadūrdhve narakādhīśāḥ kramādduḥkhaikavedanāḥ /
śdho madhye tadūrdhve ca sthitā bhedāntarairvṛtāḥ // 25
8.d:
तदूर्ध्वे नरकाधीशाः क्रमाद्दुःखैकवेदनाः ।
श्धो मध्ये तदूर्ध्वे च स्थिता भेदान्तरैर्वृताः ॥ 25
8.m: Above that are the lords of hell, whose sole experience in succession is suffering; / stationed below, in the middle, and above it, surrounded by further divisions.

8.s:
avīcikumbhīpākākhyarauravāsteṣvanukramāt /
ekādaśaikādaśa ca daśetyantaḥ śarāgni tat // 26
8.d:
अवीचिकुम्भीपाकाख्यरौरवास्तेष्वनुक्रमात् ।
एकादशैकादश च दशेत्यन्तः शराग्नि तत् ॥ 26
8.m: Among them, in succession, are those named Avīci, Kumbhīpāka, and Raurava: / eleven, eleven, and ten, so within them are thirty-two.

8.s:
pratyekameṣāmekonā koṭirucchritirantaram /
lakṣamatra khavedāsyasaṃkhyānāmantarā sthitiḥ // 27
8.d:
प्रत्येकमेषामेकोना कोटिरुच्छ्रितिरन्तरम् ।
लक्षमत्र खवेदास्यसंख्यानामन्तरा स्थितिः ॥ 27
8.m: The height of each of these is one crore minus one [hundred thousand leagues]; the interval between them / is a hundred thousand; here, the interval between those numbering forty [hells] is situated.

8.s:
kūṣmāṇḍa ūrdhve lakṣonakoṭisthānastadīśitā /
śāstraviruddhācaraṇāt kṛṣṇaṃ ye karma vidadhate // 28
8.d:
कूष्माण्ड ऊर्ध्वे लक्षोनकोटिस्थानस्तदीशिता ।
शास्त्रविरुद्धाचरणात् कृष्णं ये कर्म विदधते ॥ 28
8.m: Above is Kūṣmāṇḍa, their ruler, whose realm is one crore minus a hundred thousand [leagues]. / Those who, through conduct opposed to scripture, perform black karma,

8.s:
tatra bhīmairlokapuruṣaiḥ pīḍyante bhogaparyantam /
ye sakṛdapi parameśaṃ śivamekāgreṇa cetasā śaraṇam // 29
8.d:
तत्र भीमैर्लोकपुरुषैः पीड्यन्ते भोगपर्यन्तम् ।
ये सकृदपि परमेशं शिवमेकाग्रेण चेतसा शरणम् ॥ 29
8.m: are tormented there by terrifying men of that realm until the completion of their experience. / Those who even once, with a concentrated mind, go for refuge to the supreme Lord Śiva

8.s:
yānti na te narakayujaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ teṣāṃ sukhālpatādāyi /
sahasranavakotsedhamekāntaramatha kramāt // 30
8.d:
यान्ति न ते नरकयुजः कृष्णं तेषां सुखाल्पतादायि ।
सहस्रनवकोत्सेधमेकान्तरमथ क्रमात् ॥ 30
8.m: do not meet hell; their black [karma] yields only a slight amount of pleasure. / Next, in succession, [each] having a height of nine thousand [leagues], with an interval of one [thousand] between each,

8.s:
pātālāṣṭakamekaikamaṣṭame hāṭakaḥ prabhuḥ /
pratilokaṃ niyuktātmā śrīkaṇṭho haṭhato bahūḥ // 31
8.d:
पातालाष्टकमेकैकमष्टमे हाटकः प्रभुः ।
प्रतिलोकं नियुक्तात्मा श्रीकण्ठो हठतो बहूः ॥ 31
8.m: is the group of eight netherworlds, one after another; in the eighth is the sovereign Hāṭaka. / Śrīkaṇṭha, who has appointed himself in each world, forcibly

8.s:
siddhīrdadātyasāvevaṃ śrīmadrauravaśāsane /
vratino ye cikarmasthā niṣiddhācārakāriṇaḥ // 32
8.d:
सिद्धीर्ददात्यसावेवं श्रीमद्रौरवशासने ।
व्रतिनो ये चिकर्मस्था निषिद्धाचारकारिणः ॥ 32
8.m: grants many spiritual accomplishments: thus [it is taught] in the venerable Raurava teaching. / Those vow-holders who, established in ritual acts, perform prohibited conduct,

8.s:
dīkṣitā api ye luptasamayā naca kurvate /
prāyaścittāṃstathā tatsthā vāmācārasya dūṣakāḥ // 33
8.d:
दीक्षिता अपि ये लुप्तसमया नच कुर्वते ।
प्रायश्चित्तांस्तथा तत्स्था वामाचारस्य दूषकाः ॥ 33
8.m: and those who, though initiated, have broken their rules and do not perform / expiations; likewise, those stationed there who slander the Vāma conduct;

8.s:
devāgnidravyavṛttyaṃśajīvinaścottamasthitāḥ /
adhaḥsthagāruḍādyanyamantrasevāparāyaṇāḥ // 34
8.d:
देवाग्निद्रव्यवृत्त्यंशजीविनश्चोत्तमस्थिताः ।
अधःस्थगारुडाद्यन्यमन्त्रसेवापरायणाः ॥ 34
8.m: those who live on the portions of livelihoods or wealth of the deities and the fire, and those established in the highest [ranks] / who are devoted to serving other mantras such as the lower Gāruḍa mantras:

8.s:
te hāṭakavibhoragre kiṅkarā vividhātmakāḥ /
te tu tatrāpi deveśaṃ bhaktyā cetparyupāsate // 35
8.d:
ते हाटकविभोरग्रे किङ्करा विविधात्मकाः ।
ते तु तत्रापि देवेशं भक्त्या चेत्पर्युपासते ॥ 35
8.m: they become various kinds of servants before the sovereign Hāṭaka. / But if, even there, they worship the Lord of gods with devotion,

8.s:
tadīśatattve līyante kramācca parame śive /
anyathā ye tu vartante tadbhoganiratātmakāḥ // 36
8.d:
तदीशतत्त्वे लीयन्ते क्रमाच्च परमे शिवे ।
अन्यथा ये तु वर्तन्ते तद्भोगनिरतात्मकाः ॥ 36
8.m: they dissolve into the reality of the Lord, and gradually into supreme Śiva. / Those, however, who behave otherwise, whose souls are devoted to the enjoyments of that [realm],

8.s:
te kālavahnisaṃtāpadīnākrandaparāyaṇāḥ /
guṇatattve nilīyante tataḥ sṛṣṭimukhe punaḥ // 37
8.d:
ते कालवह्निसंतापदीनाक्रन्दपरायणाः ।
गुणतत्त्वे निलीयन्ते ततः सृष्टिमुखे पुनः ॥ 37
8.m: devoted to wretched wailing from the torment of the fire of time, / dissolve into the reality of the qualities; thereafter, at the beginning of creation, again

8.s:
pātyante mātṛbhirghorayātanaughapurassaram /
adhamādhamadeheṣu nijakarmānurūpataḥ // 38
8.d:
पात्यन्ते मातृभिर्घोरयातनौघपुरस्सरम् ।
अधमाधमदेहेषु निजकर्मानुरूपतः ॥ 38
8.m: they are cast down by the Mothers, preceded by a multitude of terrible tortures, / into the lowest of low bodies, in accordance with their own karma.

8.s:
mānuṣānteṣu tatrāpi kecinmantravidaḥ kramāt /
mucyante'nye tu badhyante pūrvakṛtyānusārataḥ // 39
8.d:
मानुषान्तेषु तत्रापि केचिन्मन्त्रविदः क्रमात् ।
मुच्यन्तेऽन्ये तु बध्यन्ते पूर्वकृत्यानुसारतः ॥ 39
8.m: Among them, ending in humans, some who know mantras are gradually / liberated; others, however, are bound according to their past deeds.

8.s:
ityeṣa gaṇavṛttānto nāmnā hulahulādinā /
proktaṃ bhagavatā śrīmadānandādhikaśāsane // 40
8.d:
इत्येष गणवृत्तान्तो नाम्ना हुलहुलादिना ।
प्रोक्तं भगवता श्रीमदानन्दाधिकशासने ॥ 40
8.m: Thus this account of the attendants, with names such as Hulahula and the rest, / was declared by the Blessed One in the venerable teaching of Ānandādhika.

8.s:
pātālordhve sahasrāṇi viṃśatirbhūkaṭāhakaḥ /
siddhātantre tu pātālapṛṣṭhe yakṣīsamāvṛtam // 41
8.d:
पातालोर्ध्वे सहस्राणि विंशतिर्भूकटाहकः ।
सिद्धातन्त्रे तु पातालपृष्ठे यक्षीसमावृतम् ॥ 41
8.m: Above the netherworlds is the caldron of the earth, twenty thousand [leagues]. / In the Siddhātantra, however, upon the back of the netherworld, surrounded by Yakṣīs,

8.s:
bhadrakālyāḥ puraṃ yatra tābhiḥ krīḍanti sādhakāḥ /
tatastamastaptabhūmistataḥśūnyaṃ tato'hayaḥ // 42
8.d:
भद्रकाल्याः पुरं यत्र ताभिः क्रीडन्ति साधकाः ।
ततस्तमस्तप्तभूमिस्ततःशून्यं ततोऽहयः ॥ 42
8.m: is the city of Bhadrakālī, where adepts sport with them. / Thence is the dark region, the heated ground, thence empty space, thence the horse-faced fire;

8.s:
etāni yātanāsthānaṃ gurumantrādidūṣiṇām /
tato bhūmyūrdhva [madhya] to meruḥ sahasrāṇi sa ṣoḍaśa // 43
8.d:
एतानि यातनास्थानं गुरुमन्त्रादिदूषिणाम् ।
ततो भूम्यूर्ध्व [मध्य] तो मेरुः सहस्राणि स षोडश ॥ 43
8.m: these are the places of torture for abusers of gurus, mantras, and the like. / Thence, [in the middle] above the earth, is Meru; sixteen thousand [leagues]

8.s:
magnastanmūlavistārastaddvayenordhvavistṛtiḥ /
sahasrābdhivasūcchrāyo haimaḥ sarvāmarālayaḥ // 44
8.d:
मग्नस्तन्मूलविस्तारस्तद्द्वयेनोर्ध्वविस्तृतिः ।
सहस्राब्धिवसूच्छ्रायो हैमः सर्वामरालयः ॥ 44
8.m: is it sunken; its base has that [same] breadth; its upper width is twice that. / Its height is eighty-four thousand [leagues]; it is golden, the abode of all immortals.

8.s:
madhyordhvādhaḥ samudvṛttaśarāvacaturaśrakaḥ /
bhairavīyaṃ ca talliṅgaṃ dharaṇī cāsya pīṭhikā // 45
8.d:
मध्योर्ध्वाधः समुद्वृत्तशरावचतुरश्रकः ।
भैरवीयं च तल्लिङ्गं धरणी चास्य पीठिका ॥ 45
8.m: In the middle, top, and bottom, it is like a saucer turned upward, four-cornered. / And that is the liṅga of Bhairava, and the earth is its pedestal.

8.s:
sarve devā nilīnā hi tatra tatpūjitaṃ sadā /
madhye merusabhā dhātustadīśadiśi ketanam // 46
8.d:
सर्वे देवा निलीना हि तत्र तत्पूजितं सदा ।
मध्ये मेरुसभा धातुस्तदीशदिशि केतनम् ॥ 46
8.m: For all the gods are dissolved there; that is worshipped eternally. / In the center is the assembly of the Creator on Meru; in the northeast direction is the residence,

8.s:
jyotiṣkaśikharaṃ śaṃbhoḥ śrīkaṇṭhāṃśaśca sa prabhuḥ /
avaruhya sahasrāṇi manovatyāścaturdaśa // 47
8.d:
ज्योतिष्कशिखरं शंभोः श्रीकण्ठांशश्च स प्रभुः ।
अवरुह्य सहस्राणि मनोवत्याश्चतुर्दश ॥ 47
8.m: the peak of light, of Śambhu, and that lord is a portion of Śrīkaṇṭha. / Having descended fourteen thousand [leagues] from Manovatī,

8.s:
cakravāṭaścaturdikko meruratra tu lokapāḥ /
amarāvatikendrasya pūrvasyāṃ dakṣiṇena tām // 48
8.d:
चक्रवाटश्चतुर्दिक्को मेरुरत्र तु लोकपाः ।
अमरावतिकेन्द्रस्य पूर्वस्यां दक्षिणेन ताम् ॥ 48
8.m: there is the circular mountain range in the four directions; but here on Meru are the world-protectors. / Amarāvatikā of Indra is in the east; to the south of it

8.s:
atsaraḥsiddhasādhyāstāmuttareṇa vināyakāḥ /
tejovatī svadiśyagneḥ purī tāṃ paścimena tu // 49
8.d:
अत्सरःसिद्धसाध्यास्तामुत्तरेण विनायकाः ।
तेजोवती स्वदिश्यग्नेः पुरी तां पश्चिमेन तु ॥ 49
8.m: are the Apsarases, Siddhas, and Sādhyas; to the north of it are the Vināyakas. / Tejovatī, the city of Agni, is in his own direction; to the west of it

8.s:
viśvedevā viśvakarmā kramāttadanugāśca ye /
yāmyāṃ saṃyamanī tāṃ tu paścimena kramāt sthitāḥ // 50
8.d:
विश्वेदेवा विश्वकर्मा क्रमात्तदनुगाश्च ये ।
याम्यां संयमनी तां तु पश्चिमेन क्रमात् स्थिताः ॥ 50
8.m: are the Viśvedevas, Viśvakarman, and those who follow him in succession. / In the southern [direction] is Saṃyamanī; to the west of it are situated in succession

8.s:
mātṛnandā svasaṃkhyātā rudrāstatsādhakāstathā /
kṛṣṇāṅgārā nirṛtiśca tāṃ pūrveṇa piśācakāḥ // 51
8.d:
मातृनन्दा स्वसंख्याता रुद्रास्तत्साधकास्तथा ।
कृष्णाङ्गारा निरृतिश्च तां पूर्वेण पिशाचकाः ॥ 51
8.m: the Mothers, the Nandās, the Rudras of their own number, and their adepts. / Kṛṣṇāṅgārā of Nirṛti is [in the southwest]; to the east of it are the Piśācas,

8.s:
rakṣāṃsi siddhagandharvāstūttareṇottareṇa tām /
vāruṇī śuddhavatyākhyā bhūtaugho dakṣiṇena tām // 52
8.d:
रक्षांसि सिद्धगन्धर्वास्तूत्तरेणोत्तरेण ताम् ।
वारुणी शुद्धवत्याख्या भूतौघो दक्षिणेन ताम् ॥ 52
8.m: the Rākṣasas, Siddhas, and Gandharvas; further and further north of it / is the [city] of Varuṇa named Śuddhavatī; to the south of it is the host of spirits;

8.s:
uttareṇottareṇaināṃ vasuvidyādharāḥ kramāt /
vāyorgandhavatī tasyā dakṣiṇe kinnarāḥ punaḥ // 53
8.d:
उत्तरेणोत्तरेणैनां वसुविद्याधराः क्रमात् ।
वायोर्गन्धवती तस्या दक्षिणे किन्नराः पुनः ॥ 53
8.m: further and further north of this are the Vasus and Vidyādharas in succession. / Gandhavatī is of Vāyu; to the south of it, further,

8.s:
vīṇāsarasvatī devī nāradastumburustathā /
mahodayendorguhyāḥ syuḥ paścime'syāḥ punaḥ punaḥ // 54
8.d:
वीणासरस्वती देवी नारदस्तुम्बुरुस्तथा ।
महोदयेन्दोर्गुह्याः स्युः पश्चिमेऽस्याः पुनः पुनः ॥ 54
8.m: are the Goddess Sarasvatī of the lute, Nārada, and Tumburu. / Mahodayā is of the Moon; Guhyakas are repeatedly to the west of it;

8.s:
kuberaḥ karmadevāśca tathā tatsādhakā api /
yaśasvinī maheśasya tasyāḥ paścimato hariḥ // 55
8.d:
कुबेरः कर्मदेवाश्च तथा तत्साधका अपि ।
यशस्विनी महेशस्य तस्याः पश्चिमतो हरिः ॥ 55
8.m: Kubera and the ritual gods, and likewise their adepts. / Yaśasvinī is of Maheśa; to the west of it is Hari;

8.s:
dakṣiṇe dakṣiṇe brahmāśvinau dhanvantariḥ kramāt /
mairave cakravāṭe'sminnevaṃ mukhyāḥ puro'ṣṭadhā // 56
8.d:
दक्षिणे दक्षिणे ब्रह्माश्विनौ धन्वन्तरिः क्रमात् ।
मैरवे चक्रवाटेऽस्मिन्नेवं मुख्याः पुरोऽष्टधा ॥ 56
8.m: further and further to the south are Brahmā, the two Aśvins, and Dhanvantari, in order. / Thus, in this enclosure on Meru, the chief cities are eightfold.

8.s:
antarālagatāstvanyāḥ punaḥ ṣaḍviṃśatiḥ smṛtāḥ /
iṣṭāpūrtaratāḥ puṇye varṣeye bhārate narāḥ // 57
8.d:
अन्तरालगतास्त्वन्याः पुनः षड्विंशतिः स्मृताः ।
इष्टापूर्तरताः पुण्ये वर्षेये भारते नराः ॥ 57
8.m: The others situated in the intermediate spaces, moreover, are remembered as twenty-six. / Humans in the holy realm of Bhārata who are devoted to sacrificial and charitable works,

8.s:
te merugāḥ sakṛcchambhuṃ ye vārcanti yathocitam /
meroḥ pradakṣiṇāpyodagdikṣu viṣkambhaparvatāḥ // 58
8.d:
ते मेरुगाः सकृच्छम्भुं ये वार्चन्ति यथोचितम् ।
मेरोः प्रदक्षिणाप्योदग्दिक्षु विष्कम्भपर्वताः ॥ 58
8.m: they go to Meru, as do those who worship Śambhu suitably even once. / In the south, west, and north directions of Meru are the supporting mountains:

8.s:
mandaro gandhamādaśca vipulo'tha supārśvakaḥ /
sitapītanīlaraktāste kramātpādaparvatāḥ // 59
8.d:
मन्दरो गन्धमादश्च विपुलोऽथ सुपार्श्वकः ।
सितपीतनीलरक्तास्ते क्रमात्पादपर्वताः ॥ 59
8.m: Mandara, Gandhamādana, Vipula, and Supārśva; / white, yellow, blue, and red respectively, they are the foot-mountains.

8.s:
etairbhuvamavaṣṭabhya merustiṣṭhati niścalaḥ /
caitrarathanandanākhye vaiśrājaṃ pitṛvanaṃ vanānyāhuḥ // 60
8.d:
एतैर्भुवमवष्टभ्य मेरुस्तिष्ठति निश्चलः ।
चैत्ररथनन्दनाख्ये वैश्राजं पितृवनं वनान्याहुः ॥ 60
8.m: Supporting the earth with these, Meru stands motionless. / The forests, they say, are named Caitraratha, Nandana, Vaiśrāja, and Pitṛvana;

8.s:
raktodamānasasitaṃ bhadraṃ caitaccatuṣṭayaṃ sarasām /
vṛkṣāḥ kadambajambvaśvatthanyagrodhakāḥ kramaśaḥ // 61
8.d:
रक्तोदमानससितं भद्रं चैतच्चतुष्टयं सरसाम् ।
वृक्षाः कदम्बजम्ब्वश्वत्थन्यग्रोधकाः क्रमशः ॥ 61
8.m: Raktoda, Mānasa, Sita, and Bhadra—this is the group of four lakes. / The trees are the Kadamba, Jambu, Aśvattha, and Nyagrodha in succession.

8.s:
eṣu ca caturṣvacaleṣu trayaṃ trayaṃ kramaśa etadāmnātam /
mervadho lavaṇābdhyantaṃ jambudvīpaḥ samantataḥ // 62
8.d:
एषु च चतुर्ष्वचलेषु त्रयं त्रयं क्रमश एतदाम्नातम् ।
मेर्वधो लवणाब्ध्यन्तं जम्बुद्वीपः समन्ततः ॥ 62
8.m: And on these four mountains, this triad [of forest, lake, and tree] is traditionally handed down in succession. / Below Meru, ending at the salt ocean, on all sides is Jambudvīpa.

8.s:
lakṣamātraḥ sa navadhā jāto maryādaparvataiḥ /
niṣadho hemakūṭaśca himavāndakṣiṇe trayaḥ // 63
8.d:
लक्षमात्रः स नवधा जातो मर्यादपर्वतैः ।
निषधो हेमकूटश्च हिमवान्दक्षिणे त्रयः ॥ 63
8.m: Measuring a hundred thousand [leagues], it is divided into nine parts by the boundary mountains. / Niṣadha, Hemakūṭa, and Himavat are three to the south:

8.s:
lakṣaṃ sahasranavatistadaśītiriti kramāt /
nīlaḥ śvetastriśṛṅgaśca tāvantaḥ savyataḥ punaḥ // 64
8.d:
लक्षं सहस्रनवतिस्तदशीतिरिति क्रमात् ।
नीलः श्वेतस्त्रिशृङ्गश्च तावन्तः सव्यतः पुनः ॥ 64
8.m: one hundred thousand, ninety thousand, and eighty [thousand leagues in length] respectively. / Nīla, Śveta, and Śṛṅgin are of the same dimensions, further to the left.

8.s:
meroḥ ṣaḍete maryādācalāḥ pūrvāparāyatāḥ /
pūrvato mālyavānpaścādgandhamādanasaṃjñitaḥ // 65
8.d:
मेरोः षडेते मर्यादाचलाः पूर्वापरायताः ।
पूर्वतो माल्यवान्पश्चाद्गन्धमादनसंज्ञितः ॥ 65
8.m: These six boundary mountains of Meru extend from east to west. / In the east is Mālyavat; in the west is the one named Gandhamādana.

8.s:
savyottarāyatau tau tu catustriṃśatsahasrakau /
aṣṭāvete tato'pyanyau dvau dvau pūrvādiṣu kramāt // 66
8.d:
सव्योत्तरायतौ तौ तु चतुस्त्रिंशत्सहस्रकौ ।
अष्टावेते ततोऽप्यन्यौ द्वौ द्वौ पूर्वादिषु क्रमात् ॥ 66
8.m: Those two, extending south and north, are thirty-four thousand [leagues]. / These are eight; and besides them, two by two in succession in the east and other directions,

8.s:
jāṭharaḥ kūṭahimavadyātrajārudhiśṛṅgiṇaḥ /
evaṃ sthito vibhāgo'tra varṣasiddhyai nirūpyate // 67
8.d:
जाठरः कूटहिमवद्यात्रजारुधिशृङ्गिणः ।
एवं स्थितो विभागोऽत्र वर्षसिद्ध्यै निरूप्यते ॥ 67
8.m: are Jāṭhara, Kūṭahimavat, Yātra, Jārudhi, and Śṛṅgin. / Thus the division situated here is described for the determination of the realms.

8.s:
samantāccakravāṭādho'narkendu caturaśrakam /
sahasranavavistīrṇamilākhyaṃ trimukhāyuṣam // 68
8.d:
समन्ताच्चक्रवाटाधोऽनर्केन्दु चतुरश्रकम् ।
सहस्रनवविस्तीर्णमिलाख्यं त्रिमुखायुषम् ॥ 68
8.m: All around below the circular mountain range, devoid of sun and moon, four-cornered, / extending nine thousand [leagues], is the [realm] named Ilā, whose life-span is three thousand [years].

8.s:
meroḥ paścimato gandhamādo yastasya paścime /
ketumālaṃ kulādrīṇāṃ saptakena vibhūṣitam // 69
8.d:
मेरोः पश्चिमतो गन्धमादो यस्तस्य पश्चिमे ।
केतुमालं कुलाद्रीणां सप्तकेन विभूषितम् ॥ 69
8.m: West of Meru is Gandhamādana; to the west of that / is Ketumāla, adorned with the seven family mountains.

8.s:
meroḥ pūrva mālyavānyo bhadrāśvastasya pūrvataḥ /
sahasradaśakāyustatsapañcakulaparvatam // 70
8.d:
मेरोः पूर्व माल्यवान्यो भद्राश्वस्तस्य पूर्वतः ।
सहस्रदशकायुस्तत्सपञ्चकुलपर्वतम् ॥ 70
8.m: To the east of Meru is Mālyavān, and east of that is Bhadrāśva; / its [inhabitants'] lifespan is ten thousand [years], and it is endowed with five clan-mountains.

8.s:
pūrvapaścimataḥ savyottarataśca kramādime /
dvātriṃśacca catustriṃśatsahasrāṇi nirūpite // 71
8.d:
पूर्वपश्चिमतः सव्योत्तरतश्च क्रमादिमे ।
द्वात्रिंशच्च चतुस्त्रिंशत्सहस्राणि निरूपिते ॥ 71
8.m: East and west, and then south and north, in order, these / are described as measuring thirty-two and thirty-four thousand [yojanas].

8.s:
merorudak śṛṅgavānyastadbahiḥ kuruvarṣakam /
cāpavannavasāhasramāyustatra trayodaśa // 72
8.d:
मेरोरुदक् शृङ्गवान्यस्तद्बहिः कुरुवर्षकम् ।
चापवन्नवसाहस्रमायुस्तत्र त्रयोदश ॥ 72
8.m: North of Meru is Śṛṅgavān, and beyond that lies Kuruvarṣa; / bow-shaped, measuring nine thousand [yojanas], lifespan there is thirteen [thousand years].

8.s:
kuruvarṣasyottare'tha vāyavye'bdhau kramāccharāḥ /
daśa ceti sahasrāṇi dvīpau candro'tha bhadrakaḥ // 73
8.d:
कुरुवर्षस्योत्तरेऽथ वायव्येऽब्धौ क्रमाच्छराः ।
दश चेति सहस्राणि द्वीपौ चन्द्रोऽथ भद्रकः ॥ 73
8.m: North of Kuruvarṣa, in the northwestern ocean, measuring in order five / and ten thousand [yojanas], are two islands: Candra and Bhadraka.

8.s:
yau śvetaśṛṅgiṇau merorvāme madhye hiraṇmayam /
tayornavakavistīrṇamāyuścārdhatrayodaśa // 74
8.d:
यौ श्वेतशृङ्गिणौ मेरोर्वामे मध्ये हिरण्मयम् ।
तयोर्नवकविस्तीर्णमायुश्चार्धत्रयोदश ॥ 74
8.m: To the left of Meru are Śveta and Śṛṅgī, between which lies Hiraṇmaya; / its extent is nine [thousand yojanas], and the lifespan is twelve and a half [thousand years].

8.s:
tatra vai vāmataḥ śvetanīlayo ramyako'ntare /
sahasranavavistīrṇamāyurdvādaśa tāni ca // 75
8.d:
तत्र वै वामतः श्वेतनीलयो रम्यकोऽन्तरे ।
सहस्रनवविस्तीर्णमायुर्द्वादश तानि च ॥ 75
8.m: There, on the left between Śveta and Nīla, is Ramyaka; / its extent is nine thousand [yojanas], and lifespan is twelve of them [i.e., twelve thousand years].

8.s:
merordakṣiṇato hemaniṣadhau yau tadantare /
haryākhyaṃ navasāhasraṃ tatsahasrādhikāyuṣam // 76
8.d:
मेरोर्दक्षिणतो हेमनिषधौ यौ तदन्तरे ।
हर्याख्यं नवसाहस्रं तत्सहस्राधिकायुषम् ॥ 76
8.m: South of Meru are Hema and Niṣadha; between them / lies the realm named Hari, measuring nine thousand [yojanas], with a lifespan a thousand years longer than that [i.e., ten thousand].

8.s:
tatraiva dakṣiṇe hemahimavaddvitayāntare /
kainnaraṃ navasāhasraṃ tatsahasrādhikāyuṣam // 77
8.d:
तत्रैव दक्षिणे हेमहिमवद्द्वितयान्तरे ।
कैन्नरं नवसाहस्रं तत्सहस्राधिकायुषम् ॥ 77
8.m: Right there to the south, between the pair Hema and Himavat, / lies Kinnara, measuring nine thousand [yojanas], with a lifespan a thousand years longer than that.

8.s:
tatraiva dakṣiṇe merorhimavānyasya dakṣiṇe /
bhārataṃ navasāhasraṃ cāpavatkarmabhogabhūḥ // 78
8.d:
तत्रैव दक्षिणे मेरोर्हिमवान्यस्य दक्षिणे ।
भारतं नवसाहस्रं चापवत्कर्मभोगभूः ॥ 78
8.m: Right there to the south of Meru is Himavat, south of which / lies Bhārata, measuring nine thousand [yojanas], bow-shaped, a land of action and enjoyment.

8.s:
ilāvṛtaṃ ketubhadraṃ kuruhairaṇyaramyakam /
harikinnaravarṣe ca bhogabhūrna tu karmabhūḥ // 79
8.d:
इलावृतं केतुभद्रं कुरुहैरण्यरम्यकम् ।
हरिकिन्नरवर्षे च भोगभूर्न तु कर्मभूः ॥ 79
8.m: Ilāvṛta, Ketumāla, Bhadra, Kuru, Hairaṇya, Ramyaka, / and the realms of Hari and Kinnara are lands of enjoyment, not lands of action.

8.s:
atra bāhulyataḥ karmabhūbhāvo'trāpyakarmaṇām /
paśūnāṃ karmasaṃskāraḥ syāttādṛgdṛḍhasaṃskṛteḥ // 80
8.d:
अत्र बाहुल्यतः कर्मभूभावोऽत्राप्यकर्मणाम् ।
पशूनां कर्मसंस्कारः स्यात्तादृग्दृढसंस्कृतेः ॥ 80
8.m: Here [in Bhārata], for the most part, is the nature of a land of action; yet even here, bound souls devoid of rites / may possess karmic impressions due to firmly rooted latent tendencies of such a kind.

8.s:
saṃbhavantyapyasaṃskārā bhārate'nyatra cāpi hi /
dṛḍhaprāktanasaṃskārādīśecchātaḥ śubhāśubham // 81
8.d:
संभवन्त्यप्यसंस्कारा भारतेऽन्यत्र चापि हि ।
दृढप्राक्तनसंस्कारादीशेच्छातः शुभाशुभम् ॥ 81
8.m: Even those devoid of impressions arise in Bhārata and elsewhere too; / by the Lord's will, auspicious and inauspicious [fruits] arise from firm past impressions.

8.s:
sthānāntare'pi karmāsti dṛṣṭaṃ tacca purātane /
tatra tretā sadā kālo bhārate tu caturyugam // 82
8.d:
स्थानान्तरेऽपि कर्मास्ति दृष्टं तच्च पुरातने ।
तत्र त्रेता सदा कालो भारते तु चतुर्युगम् ॥ 82
8.m: In other places too action exists, as seen in ancient tradition; / there, the time is always Tretā[-yuga], but in Bhārata there are four world-ages.

8.s:
bhārate navakhaṇḍaṃ ca sāmudreṇāmbhasātra ca /
sthalaṃ pañcaśatī tadvajjalaṃ ceti vibhajyate // 83
8.d:
भारते नवखण्डं च सामुद्रेणाम्भसात्र च ।
स्थलं पञ्चशती तद्वज्जलं चेति विभज्यते ॥ 83
8.m: And Bhārata has nine divisions, separated by ocean waters; / the dry land is five hundred [yojanas], and likewise the water is divided.

8.s:
indraḥ kaśerustāmrābho nāgīyaḥ prāggabhastimān /
saumyagāndharvavārāhāḥ kanyākhyaṃ cāsamudrataḥ // 84
8.d:
इन्द्रः कशेरुस्ताम्राभो नागीयः प्राग्गभस्तिमान् ।
सौम्यगान्धर्ववाराहाः कन्याख्यं चासमुद्रतः ॥ 84
8.m: Indra, Kaśeru, Tāmra, Nāga, and to the east Gabhastimat, / Saumya, Gāndharva, Vārāha, and the realm named Kanyā, up to the ocean.

8.s:
kanyādvīpe ca navame dakṣiṇenābdhimadhyagāḥ /
upadvīpāḥ ṣaṭ kulādrisaptakena vibhūṣite // 85
8.d:
कन्याद्वीपे च नवमे दक्षिणेनाब्धिमध्यगाः ।
उपद्वीपाः षट् कुलाद्रिसप्तकेन विभूषिते ॥ 85
8.m: And in Kanyādvīpa, the ninth, situated in the middle of the southern ocean / are six sub-islands, adorned with seven clan-mountains:

8.s:
aṅgayavamalayaśaṅkuḥ kumudavarāhau ca malayago'gastya /
tatraiva ca trikūṭe laṅkā ṣaḍamī hyupadvīpāḥ // 86
8.d:
अङ्गयवमलयशङ्कुः कुमुदवराहौ च मलयगोऽगस्त्य ।
तत्रैव च त्रिकूटे लङ्का षडमी ह्युपद्वीपाः ॥ 86
8.m: Aṅga, Yava, Malaya, Śaṅku, Kumuda, and Varāha; Agastya resides on Malaya, / and right there on Trikūṭa is Laṅkā; these indeed are the six sub-islands.

8.s:
dvīpopadvīpagāḥ prāyo mlecchā nānāvidhā janāḥ /
muktākāñcanaratnāḍhyā iti śrīruruśāsane // 87
8.d:
द्वीपोपद्वीपगाः प्रायो म्लेच्छा नानाविधा जनाः ।
मुक्ताकाञ्चनरत्नाढ्या इति श्रीरुरुशासने ॥ 87
8.m: Those who inhabit these islands and sub-islands are mostly barbarians of diverse kinds, / rich in pearls, gold, and gems—thus it is taught in the venerable Rurutantra.

8.s:
bhārate yatkṛtaṃ karma kṣapitaṃ vāpyavīcitaḥ /
śivāntaṃ tena muktirvā kanyākhye tu viśeṣataḥ // 88
8.d:
भारते यत्कृतं कर्म क्षपितं वाप्यवीचितः ।
शिवान्तं तेन मुक्तिर्वा कन्याख्ये तु विशेषतः ॥ 88
8.m: Karma performed or exhausted in Bhārata leads to anywhere from Avīci / up to Śiva, or to liberation, and especially so in the division named Kanyā.

8.s:
mahākālādikā rudrakoṭiratraiva bhārate /
gaṅgādipañcaśatikā janma tenātra durlabham // 89
8.d:
महाकालादिका रुद्रकोटिरत्रैव भारते ।
गङ्गादिपञ्चशतिका जन्म तेनात्र दुर्लभम् ॥ 89
8.m: The crore of Rudras beginning with Mahākāla resides right here in Bhārata, / along with the five hundred [holy rivers] beginning with the Gaṅgā; therefore, birth here is hard to attain.

8.s:
anyavarṣeṣu paśuvad bhogātkarmātivāhanam /
prāpyaṃ manorathātītamapi bhāratajanmanām // 90
8.d:
अन्यवर्षेषु पशुवद् भोगात्कर्मातिवाहनम् ।
प्राप्यं मनोरथातीतमपि भारतजन्मनाम् ॥ 90
8.m: In other realms, karmic exhaustion occurs through enjoyment, like animals; / but for those born in Bhārata, even what lies beyond wishful imagination can be attained.

8.s:
nānāvarṇāśramācārasukhaduḥkhavicitratā /
kanyādvīpe yatastena karmabhūḥ seyamuttamā // 91
8.d:
नानावर्णाश्रमाचारसुखदुःखविचित्रता ।
कन्याद्वीपे यतस्तेन कर्मभूः सेयमुत्तमा ॥ 91
8.m: Because there is a manifold variety of pleasures, pains, classes, life-stages, and customs / in Kanyādvīpa, this is the supreme land of action.

8.s:
puṃsā sitāsitānyatra kurvatāṃ kila siddhyataḥ /
parāparau svarnirayāviti rauravavārtike // 92
8.d:
पुंसा सितासितान्यत्र कुर्वतां किल सिद्ध्यतः ।
परापरौ स्वर्निरयाविति रौरववार्तिके ॥ 92
8.m: For persons performing light and dark deeds here, / heaven and hell, higher and lower, are accomplished—so says the Rauravavārttika.

8.s:
evaṃ meroradho jambūrabhito yaḥ sa vistarāt /
syāt saptadaśadhā khaṇḍairnavabhistu samāsataḥ // 93
8.d:
एवं मेरोरधो जम्बूरभितो यः स विस्तरात् ।
स्यात् सप्तदशधा खण्डैर्नवभिस्तु समासतः ॥ 93
8.m: Thus, below Meru and all around it is the Jambū [continent], which in detail / consists of seventeen divisions, but concisely of nine.

8.s:
manoḥ svāyaṃbhuvasyāsan sutā daśa tatastrayaḥ /
prāvrajannatha jambvākhye rājā yo'gnīdhranāmakaḥ // 94
8.d:
मनोः स्वायंभुवस्यासन् सुता दश ततस्त्रयः ।
प्राव्रजन्नथ जम्ब्वाख्ये राजा योऽग्नीध्रनामकः ॥ 94
8.m: Manu Svāyambhuva had ten sons; of them, three / renounced; then the one who became king over the continent named Jambū was named Āgnīdhra.

8.s:
tasyābhavannava sutāstato'yaṃ navakhaṇḍakaḥ /
nābhiryo navamastasya naptā bharata ārṣabhiḥ // 95
8.d:
तस्याभवन्नव सुतास्ततोऽयं नवखण्डकः ।
नाभिर्यो नवमस्तस्य नप्ता भरत आर्षभिः ॥ 95
8.m: He had nine sons, and thence came these nine divisions; / the ninth was Nābhi, whose grandson was Bharata, son of Ṛṣabha.

8.s:
tasyāṣṭau tanayāḥ sākaṃ kanyayā navamo'ṃśakaḥ /
bhuktaistairnavadhā tasmāllakṣayojanamātrakāt // 96
8.d:
तस्याष्टौ तनयाः साकं कन्यया नवमोऽंशकः ।
भुक्तैस्तैर्नवधा तस्माल्लक्षयोजनमात्रकात् ॥ 96
8.m: He had eight sons along with a daughter, as the ninth share; / it was enjoyed by them in nine parts, from that [continent] measuring one hundred thousand yojanas.

8.s:
lakṣaikamātro lavaṇastadbāhye'sya puro'drayaḥ /
ṛṣabho dundubhirdhūmraḥ kaṅkadroṇendavo hyudak // 97
8.d:
लक्षैकमात्रो लवणस्तद्बाह्येऽस्य पुरोऽद्रयः ।
ऋषभो दुन्दुभिर्धूम्रः कङ्कद्रोणेन्दवो ह्युदक् ॥ 97
8.m: The Salt Ocean measures one hundred thousand [yojanas]; beyond it, facing it, are mountains: / Ṛṣabha, Dundubhi, Dhūmra, Kaṅka, Droṇa, and Indu to the north,

8.s:
varāhanandanāśokāḥ paścāt sahabalāhakau /
dakṣiṇa cakramainākau vāḍavo'ntastayoḥ sthitaḥ // 98
8.d:
वराहनन्दनाशोकाः पश्चात् सहबलाहकौ ।
दक्षिण चक्रमैनाकौ वाडवोऽन्तस्तयोः स्थितः ॥ 98
8.m: Varāha, Nandana, and Aśoka to the west, together with Balāhaka; / to the south are Cakra and Maināka, between which the submarine fire resides.

8.s:
abdherdakṣiṇataḥ khākṣisahasrātikramād giriḥ /
vidyutvāṃstrisahasrocchridāyāmo'tra phalāśinaḥ // 99
8.d:
अब्धेर्दक्षिणतः खाक्षिसहस्रातिक्रमाद् गिरिः ।
विद्युत्वांस्त्रिसहस्रोच्छ्रिदायामोऽत्र फलाशिनः ॥ 99
8.m: South of the ocean, crossing twenty-five thousand [yojanas], is the mountain / Vidyutvān, three thousand [yojanas] in height and extent; here fruit-eaters reside,

8.s:
maladigdhā dīrghakeśaśmaśravo gosadharmakāḥ /
nagnāḥ saṃvatsarāśītijīvinastṛṇabhojinaḥ // 100
8.d:
मलदिग्धा दीर्घकेशश्मश्रवो गोसधर्मकाः ।
नग्नाः संवत्सराशीतिजीविनस्तृणभोजिनः ॥ 100
8.m: smeared with dirt, with long hair and beards, behaving like cattle, / naked, living for eighty years, and grazing on grass.

8.s:
niryantrāṇi sadā tatra dvārāṇi bilasiddhaye /
ityetad gurubhirgītaṃ śrīmadrauravaśāsane // 101
8.d:
निर्यन्त्राणि सदा तत्र द्वाराणि बिलसिद्धये ।
इत्येतद् गुरुभिर्गीतं श्रीमद्रौरवशासने ॥ 101
8.m: Always unobstructed there are the doors to the accomplishment of subterranean realms— / this is sung by the gurus in the venerable teachings of the Rauravatantra.

8.s:
itthaṃ ya eṣa lavaṇasamudraḥ pratipāditaḥ /
tadbahiḥ ṣaḍamī dvīpāḥ pratyekaṃ svārṇavairvṛtāḥ // 102
8.d:
इत्थं य एष लवणसमुद्रः प्रतिपादितः ।
तद्बहिः षडमी द्वीपाः प्रत्येकं स्वार्णवैर्वृताः ॥ 102
8.m: Thus has been explained this Salt Ocean; / beyond it are these six continents, each surrounded by its own ocean,

8.s:
kramadviguṇitāḥ ṣaḍbhirmanuputrairadhiṣṭhitāḥ /
śākakuśakrauñcāḥ śalmaligomedhābjamiti ṣaḍdvīpāḥ /
kṣīradadhisarpiraikṣavamadirāmadhurāmbukāḥ ṣaḍambudhayaḥ // 103
8.d:
क्रमद्विगुणिताः षड्भिर्मनुपुत्रैरधिष्ठिताः ।
शाककुशक्रौञ्चाः शल्मलिगोमेधाब्जमिति षड्द्वीपाः ।
क्षीरदधिसर्पिरैक्षवमदिरामधुराम्बुकाः षडम्बुधयः ॥ 103
8.m: doubling successively in size, governed by six sons of Manu: / Śāka, Kuśa, Krauñca, Śālmali, Gomeda, and Abja are the six continents; / milk, curd, clarified butter, sugarcane juice, liquor, and sweet water are the six oceans.

8.s:
medhātithirvapuṣmāñjyotiṣmāndyutimatā havī rājā /
saṃvara iti śākādiṣu jambudvīpe nyarūpi cāgnīdhraḥ // 104
8.d:
मेधातिथिर्वपुष्माञ्ज्योतिष्मान्द्युतिमता हवी राजा ।
संवर इति शाकादिषु जम्बुद्वीपे न्यरूपि चाग्नीध्रः ॥ 104
8.m: Medhātithi, Vapuṣmān, Jyotiṣmān, Dyutimān, King Havya, / and Saṃvara [rule] Śāka and the rest, while Āgnīdhra was described in Jambūdvīpa.

8.s:
girisaptakaparikalpitatāvatkhaṇḍāstu pañca śākādyāḥ /
puṣkarasaṃjño dvidalo hariyamavaruṇendavo'tra pūrvādau // 105
8.d:
गिरिसप्तकपरिकल्पिततावत्खण्डास्तु पञ्च शाकाद्याः ।
पुष्करसंज्ञो द्विदलो हरियमवरुणेन्दवोऽत्र पूर्वादौ ॥ 105
8.m: The five continents beginning with Śāka have as many divisions made by seven mountains; / the one named Puṣkara has two halves; here, in the east and other quarters, are Hari, Yama, Varuṇa, and Indu.

8.s:
tripañcāśacca lakṣāṇi dvikoṭyayutapañcakam /
svādvarṇavāntaṃ mervardhādyojananāmiyaṃ pramā // 106
8.d:
त्रिपञ्चाशच्च लक्षाणि द्विकोट्ययुतपञ्चकम् ।
स्वाद्वर्णवान्तं मेर्वर्धाद्योजननामियं प्रमा ॥ 106
8.m: Two crores, fifty-three lakhs, / and fifty thousand yojanas: / this is the measurement up to the sweet-water ocean from the midpoint of Meru.

8.s:
saptamajaladherbāhye haimī bhūḥ koṭidaśakamatha lakṣam /
ucchrityā vistārādayutaṃ loketarācalaḥ kathitaḥ // 107
8.d:
सप्तमजलधेर्बाह्ये हैमी भूः कोटिदशकमथ लक्षम् ।
उच्छ्रित्या विस्तारादयुतं लोकेतराचलः कथितः ॥ 107
8.m: Beyond the seventh ocean is the golden land of one hundred million [yojanas]; / then the Lokāloka mountain is described, one hundred thousand [yojanas] in height and ten thousand in width.

8.s:
lokālokadigaṣṭaka saṃsthaṃ rudrāṣṭakaṃ salokeśam /
kevalamityapi kecillokālokāntare ravirna bahiḥ // 108
8.d:
लोकालोकदिगष्टक संस्थं रुद्राष्टकं सलोकेशम् ।
केवलमित्यपि केचिल्लोकालोकान्तरे रविर्न बहिः ॥ 108
8.m: The eight Rudras along with the world-guardians dwell in the eight directions of Lokāloka; / some say they dwell alone; the sun remains inside Lokāloka, not outside.

8.s:
pitṛdevapathāvasyodagdakṣiṇagau svajātpare vīthyau /
bhānoruttaradakṣiṇamayanadvayametadeva kathayanti // 109
8.d:
पितृदेवपथावस्योदग्दक्षिणगौ स्वजात्परे वीथ्यौ ।
भानोरुत्तरदक्षिणमयनद्वयमेतदेव कथयन्ति ॥ 109
8.m:
The paths of the ancestors and the gods run north and south of it, in avenues beyond its own course; / this very [movement] they call the two solstices of the sun, northern and southern.
“For all [beings], Meru is the north, and Lokāloka is the south.”

8.s: udayāstamayāvitthaṃ sūryasya paribhāvayet // 110
8.d: उदयास्तमयावित्थं सूर्यस्य परिभावयेत् ॥ 110
8.m: In this manner one should contemplate the sunrise and sunset.

8.s:
ardharātro'marāvatyāṃ yāmyāyāmastameva ca /
madhyandinaṃ tadvāruṇyāṃ saumye sūryodayaḥ smṛtaḥ // 111
8.d:
अर्धरात्रोऽमरावत्यां याम्यायामस्तमेव च ।
मध्यन्दिनं तद्वारुण्यां सौम्ये सूर्योदयः स्मृतः ॥ 111
8.m: When it is midnight in Amarāvatī, it is sunset in the southern [city]; / likewise, it is midday in the western, and sunrise is taught to be in the northern.

8.s:
udayo yo'marāvatyāṃ so'rdharātro yamālaye /
ke'staṃ saumye ca madhyāhna itthaṃ sūryagatāgate // 112
8.d:
उदयो योऽमरावत्यां सोऽर्धरात्रो यमालये ।
केऽस्तं सौम्ये च मध्याह्न इत्थं सूर्यगतागते ॥ 112
8.m: What is sunrise in Amarāvatī is midnight in the abode of Yama, / sunset in [the western city], and midday in the northern: such are the sun's movements.

8.s:
pañcatriṃ śatkoṭisaṃkhyā lakṣāṇyekonaviṃśatiḥ /
catvāriṃśatsahasrāṇi dhvāntaṃ lokācalādbahiḥ // 113
8.d:
पञ्चत्रिं शत्कोटिसंख्या लक्षाण्येकोनविंशतिः ।
चत्वारिंशत्सहस्राणि ध्वान्तं लोकाचलाद्बहिः ॥ 113
8.m: Thirty-five crores, / nineteen lakhs, / and forty thousand [yojanas] of darkness extend beyond the world-mountain [Lokāloka].

8.s:
saptasāgaramānastu garbhodākhyaḥ samudrarāṭ /
lokālokasya parato yadgarbhe nikhilaiva bhūḥ // 114
8.d:
सप्तसागरमानस्तु गर्भोदाख्यः समुद्रराट् ।
लोकालोकस्य परतो यद्गर्भे निखिलैव भूः ॥ 114
8.m:
saptasāgaramānastu garbhodākhyaḥ samudrarāṭ
lokālokasya parato yadgarbhe nikhilaiva bhūḥ // 114

8.s:
siddhātantre'tra garbhābdhestīre kauśeyasaṃjñitam /
maṇḍalaṃ garuḍastatra siddhapakṣasamāvṛtaḥ // 115
8.d:
सिद्धातन्त्रेऽत्र गर्भाब्धेस्तीरे कौशेयसंज्ञितम् ।
मण्डलं गरुडस्तत्र सिद्धपक्षसमावृतः ॥ 115
8.m:
siddhātantre@tra garbhābdhestīre kauśeyasaṃjñitam
maṇḍalaṃ garuḍastatra siddhapakṣasamāvṛtaḥ // 115

8.s:
krīḍantiṃ parvatāgre te nava cātra kulādrayaḥ /
tata uṣṇodakāstriṃśannadyaḥpātālagāstataḥ // 116
8.d:
क्रीडन्तिं पर्वताग्रे ते नव चात्र कुलाद्रयः ।
तत उष्णोदकास्त्रिंशन्नद्यःपातालगास्ततः ॥ 116
8.m:
krīḍantiṃ parvatāgre te nava cātra kulādrayaḥ
tata uṣṇodakāstriṃśannadyaḥpātālagāstataḥ // 116

8.s:
caturdiṅnaimirodyānaṃ yoginīsevitaṃ sadā /
tato merustato nāgā meghā hemāṇḍakaṃ tataḥ // 117
8.d:
चतुर्दिङ्नैमिरोद्यानं योगिनीसेवितं सदा ।
ततो मेरुस्ततो नागा मेघा हेमाण्डकं ततः ॥ 117
8.m:
caturdiṅnaimirodyānaṃ yoginīsevitaṃ sadā
tato merustato nāgā meghā hemāṇḍakaṃ tataḥ // 117

8.s:
brahmaṇo'ṇḍakaṭāhena merorardhena koṭayaḥ /
pañcāśadevaṃ daśasu dicu bhūrlokasaṃjñitam // 118
8.d:
ब्रह्मणोऽण्डकटाहेन मेरोरर्धेन कोटयः ।
पञ्चाशदेवं दशसु दिचु भूर्लोकसंज्ञितम् ॥ 118
8.m:
brahmaṇo@ṇḍakaṭāhena merorardhena koṭayaḥ
pañcāśadevaṃ daśasu dicu bhūrlokasaṃjñitam // 118

8.s:
paśukhagamṛgatarumānuṣasarīsṛpaiḥ ṣaḍbhireṣa bhūrlokaḥ /
vyāptaḥ piśācarakṣogandharvāṇāṃ sayakṣāṇām // 119
8.d:
पशुखगमृगतरुमानुषसरीसृपैः षड्भिरेष भूर्लोकः ।
व्याप्तः पिशाचरक्षोगन्धर्वाणां सयक्षाणाम् ॥ 119
8.m:
paśukhagamṛgatarumānuṣasarīsṛpaiḥ ṣaḍbhireṣa bhūrlokaḥ
vyāptaḥ piśācarakṣogandharvāṇāṃ sayakṣāṇām // 119

8.s:
vidyābhṛtāṃ ca kiṃ vā bahunā sarvasya bhūtasargasya /
abhimānato yatheṣṭaṃ bhogasthānaṃ nivāsaśca // 120
8.d:
विद्याभृतां च किं वा बहुना सर्वस्य भूतसर्गस्य ।
अभिमानतो यथेष्टं भोगस्थानं निवासश्च ॥ 120
8.m:
vidyābhṛtāṃ ca kiṃ vā bahunā sarvasya bhūtasargasya
abhimānato yatheṣṭaṃ bhogasthānaṃ nivāsaśca // 120

8.s:
bhuvarlokastathā tvārkāllakṣamekaṃ tadantare /
daśa vāyupathāste ca pratyekamayutāntarāḥ // 121
8.d:
भुवर्लोकस्तथा त्वार्काल्लक्षमेकं तदन्तरे ।
दश वायुपथास्ते च प्रत्येकमयुतान्तराः ॥ 121
8.m:
bhuvarlokastathā tvārkāllakṣamekaṃ tadantare
daśa vāyupathāste ca pratyekamayutāntarāḥ // 121

8.s:
ādyo vāyupathastatra vitataḥ paricarcyate /
pañcāśadyojanordhve syādṛtarddhirnāma mārutaḥ // 122
8.d:
आद्यो वायुपथस्तत्र विततः परिचर्च्यते ।
पञ्चाशद्योजनोर्ध्वे स्यादृतर्द्धिर्नाम मारुतः ॥ 122
8.m:
ādyo vāyupathastatra vitataḥ paricarcyate
pañcāśadyojanordhve syādṛtarddhirnāma mārutaḥ // 122

8.s:
āpyāyakaḥ sa jantūnāṃ tataḥ prācetaso bhavet /
pañcāśadyojanādūrdhva tasmādūrdhva śatena tu // 123
8.d:
आप्यायकः स जन्तूनां ततः प्राचेतसो भवेत् ।
पञ्चाशद्योजनादूर्ध्व तस्मादूर्ध्व शतेन तु ॥ 123
8.m:
āpyāyakaḥ sa jantūnāṃ tataḥ prācetaso bhavet
pañcāśadyojanādūrdhva tasmādūrdhva śatena tu // 123

8.s:
senānīvāyuratraite mūkameghāstaḍinmucaḥ /
ye mahyāḥ krośamātreṇa tiṣṭhanti jalavarṣiṇaḥ // 124
8.d:
सेनानीवायुरत्रैते मूकमेघास्तडिन्मुचः ।
ये मह्याः क्रोशमात्रेण तिष्ठन्ति जलवर्षिणः ॥ 124
8.m:
senānīvāyuratraite mūkameghāstaḍinmucaḥ
ye mahyāḥ krośamātreṇa tiṣṭhanti jalavarṣiṇaḥ // 124

8.s:
tebhya ūrdhva śatānmeghā bhekādiprāṇivarṣiṇaḥ /
pañcāśadūrdhvamogho'tra viṣavāripravarṣiṇaḥ // 125
8.d:
तेभ्य ऊर्ध्व शतान्मेघा भेकादिप्राणिवर्षिणः ।
पञ्चाशदूर्ध्वमोघोऽत्र विषवारिप्रवर्षिणः ॥ 125
8.m:
tebhya ūrdhva śatānmeghā bhekādiprāṇivarṣiṇaḥ
pañcāśadūrdhvamogho@tra viṣavāripravarṣiṇaḥ // 125

8.s:
meghāḥ skandodbhavāścānye piśācā oghamārute /
tataḥ pañcāśadūrdhvaṃ syurmeghā mārakasaṃjñakāḥ // 126
8.d:
मेघाः स्कन्दोद्भवाश्चान्ये पिशाचा ओघमारुते ।
ततः पञ्चाशदूर्ध्वं स्युर्मेघा मारकसंज्ञकाः ॥ 126
8.m:
meghāḥ skandodbhavāścānye piśācā oghamārute
tataḥ pañcāśadūrdhvaṃ syurmeghā mārakasaṃjñakāḥ // 126

8.s:
tatra sthāne mahādevajanmānaste vināyakāḥ /
ye haranti kṛtaṃ karma narāṇāmakṛtātmanām // 127
8.d:
तत्र स्थाने महादेवजन्मानस्ते विनायकाः ।
ये हरन्ति कृतं कर्म नराणामकृतात्मनाम् ॥ 127
8.m:
tatra sthāne mahādevajanmānaste vināyakāḥ
ye haranti kṛtaṃ karma narāṇāmakṛtātmanām // 127

8.s:
pañcāśadūrdhvaṃ vajrāṅko vāyuratropalāmbudāḥ /
vidyādharādhamāścātra vajrāṅke saṃpratiṣṭhitāḥ // 128
8.d:
पञ्चाशदूर्ध्वं वज्राङ्को वायुरत्रोपलाम्बुदाः ।
विद्याधराधमाश्चात्र वज्राङ्के संप्रतिष्ठिताः ॥ 128
8.m:
pañcāśadūrdhvaṃ vajrāṅko vāyuratropalāmbudāḥ
vidyādharādhamāścātra vajrāṅke saṃpratiṣṭhitāḥ // 128

8.s:
ye vidyāpauruṣe ye ca śmaśānādiprasādhane /
mṛtāstatsiddhisiddhāste vajrāṃke maruti sthitāḥ // 129
8.d:
ये विद्यापौरुषे ये च श्मशानादिप्रसाधने ।
मृतास्तत्सिद्धिसिद्धास्ते वज्रांके मरुति स्थिताः ॥ 129
8.m:
ye vidyāpauruṣe ye ca śmaśānādiprasādhane
mṛtāstatsiddhisiddhāste vajrāṃke maruti sthitāḥ // 129

8.s:
pañcāśadūrdhvaṃ vajrāṃkādvaidyuto'śanivarṣiṇaḥ /
abdā apsarasaścātra ye ca puṇyakṛto narāḥ // 130
8.d:
पञ्चाशदूर्ध्वं वज्रांकाद्वैद्युतोऽशनिवर्षिणः ।
अब्दा अप्सरसश्चात्र ये च पुण्यकृतो नराः ॥ 130
8.m:
pañcāśadūrdhvaṃ vajrāṃkādvaidyuto@śanivarṣiṇaḥ
abdā apsarasaścātra ye ca puṇyakṛto narāḥ // 130

8.s:
bhṛgau vahnau jale ye ca saṃgrāme cānivartinaḥ /
gograhe vadhyamokṣe vā mṛtāste vaidyute sthitāḥ // 131
8.d:
भृगौ वह्नौ जले ये च संग्रामे चानिवर्तिनः ।
गोग्रहे वध्यमोक्षे वा मृतास्ते वैद्युते स्थिताः ॥ 131
8.m:
bhṛgau vahnau jale ye ca saṃgrāme cānivartinaḥ
gograhe vadhyamokṣe vā mṛtāste vaidyute sthitāḥ // 131

8.s:
vaidyutādraivatastāvāṃstatra puṣṭivahāmbudāḥ /
ūrdhvaṃ ca rogāmbumucaḥ saṃvartāstadanantare // 132
8.d:
वैद्युताद्रैवतस्तावांस्तत्र पुष्टिवहाम्बुदाः ।
ऊर्ध्वं च रोगाम्बुमुचः संवर्तास्तदनन्तरे ॥ 132
8.m:
vaidyutādraivatastāvāṃstatra puṣṭivahāmbudāḥ
ūrdhvaṃ ca rogāmbumucaḥ saṃvartāstadanantare // 132

8.s:
rocanāñjanabhasmādisiddhāstatraiva raivate /
krodhodakamucāṃ sthānaṃ viṣāvartaḥ sa mārutaḥ // 133
8.d:
रोचनाञ्जनभस्मादिसिद्धास्तत्रैव रैवते ।
क्रोधोदकमुचां स्थानं विषावर्तः स मारुतः ॥ 133
8.m:
rocanāñjanabhasmādisiddhāstatraiva raivate
krodhodakamucāṃ sthānaṃ viṣāvartaḥ sa mārutaḥ // 133

8.s:
pañcāśadūrdhvaṃ tatraiva durdinābdā hutāśajāḥ /
vidyādharaviśeṣāśca tathā ye parameśvaram // 134
8.d:
पञ्चाशदूर्ध्वं तत्रैव दुर्दिनाब्दा हुताशजाः ।
विद्याधरविशेषाश्च तथा ये परमेश्वरम् ॥ 134
8.m:
pañcāśadūrdhvaṃ tatraiva durdinābdā hutāśajāḥ
vidyādharaviśeṣāśca tathā ye parameśvaram // 134

8.s:
gāndharveṇa sadārcanti viṣāvarte'tha te sthitāḥ /
viṣāvartācchatādūrdhva durjayaḥ śvāsasaṃbhavaḥ // 135
8.d:
गान्धर्वेण सदार्चन्ति विषावर्तेऽथ ते स्थिताः ।
विषावर्ताच्छतादूर्ध्व दुर्जयः श्वाससंभवः ॥ 135
8.m:
gāndharveṇa sadārcanti viṣāvarte@tha te sthitāḥ
viṣāvartācchatādūrdhva durjayaḥ śvāsasaṃbhavaḥ // 135

8.s:
brahmaṇo'tra sthitā meghāḥ pralaye vātakāriṇaḥ /
puṣkarābdā vāyugamā gandharvāśca parāvahe // 136
8.d:
ब्रह्मणोऽत्र स्थिता मेघाः प्रलये वातकारिणः ।
पुष्कराब्दा वायुगमा गन्धर्वाश्च परावहे ॥ 136
8.m:
brahmaṇo@tra sthitā meghāḥ pralaye vātakāriṇaḥ
puṣkarābdā vāyugamā gandharvāśca parāvahe // 136

8.s:
jīmūtameghāstatsaṃjñāstathā vidyādharottamāḥ /
ye ca rūpavratā lokā āvahe te pratiṣṭhitāḥ // 137
8.d:
जीमूतमेघास्तत्संज्ञास्तथा विद्याधरोत्तमाः ।
ये च रूपव्रता लोका आवहे ते प्रतिष्ठिताः ॥ 137
8.m:
jīmūtameghāstatsaṃjñāstathā vidyādharottamāḥ
ye ca rūpavratā lokā āvahe te pratiṣṭhitāḥ // 137

8.s:
mahāvahe tvīśakṛtāḥ prajāhitakarāmbudāḥ /
mahāparivahe meghāḥ kapālotthā maheśituḥ // 138
8.d:
महावहे त्वीशकृताः प्रजाहितकराम्बुदाः ।
महापरिवहे मेघाः कपालोत्था महेशितुः ॥ 138
8.m:
mahāvahe tvīśakṛtāḥ prajāhitakarāmbudāḥ
mahāparivahe meghāḥ kapālotthā maheśituḥ // 138

8.s:
mahāparivahānto'yamṛtarddheḥ prāṅmarutpathaḥ /
agnikanyā mātaraśca rudraśaktyā tvadhiṣṭhitāḥ // 139
8.d:
महापरिवहान्तोऽयमृतर्द्धेः प्राङ्मरुत्पथः ।
अग्निकन्या मातरश्च रुद्रशक्त्या त्वधिष्ठिताः ॥ 139
8.m:
mahāparivahānto@yamṛtarddheḥ prāṅmarutpathaḥ
agnikanyā mātaraśca rudraśaktyā tvadhiṣṭhitāḥ // 139

8.s:
dvitīye tatpare siddhacāraṇā nijakarmajāḥ /
turye devāyudhānyaṣṭau diggajāḥ pañcame punaḥ // 140
8.d:
द्वितीये तत्परे सिद्धचारणा निजकर्मजाः ।
तुर्ये देवायुधान्यष्टौ दिग्गजाः पञ्चमे पुनः ॥ 140
8.m:
dvitīye tatpare siddhacāraṇā nijakarmajāḥ
turye devāyudhānyaṣṭau diggajāḥ pañcame punaḥ // 140

8.s:
ṣaṣṭhe garutmānanyasmiṅgaṅgānyatra vṛṣo vibhuḥ /
dakṣastu navame brahmaśaktyā samadhiti[ni]ṣṭhitaḥ // 141
8.d:
षष्ठे गरुत्मानन्यस्मिङ्गङ्गान्यत्र वृषो विभुः ।
दक्षस्तु नवमे ब्रह्मशक्त्या समधिति[नि]ष्ठितः ॥ 141
8.m:
ṣaṣṭhe garutmānanyasmiṅgaṅgānyatra vṛṣo vibhuḥ
dakṣastu navame brahmaśaktyā samadhiti[ni]ṣṭhitaḥ // 141

8.s:
daśame vasavo rudrā ādityāśca marutpathe /
navayojanasāhasro vigraho'rkasya maṇḍalam // 142
8.d:
दशमे वसवो रुद्रा आदित्याश्च मरुत्पथे ।
नवयोजनसाहस्रो विग्रहोऽर्कस्य मण्डलम् ॥ 142
8.m:
daśame vasavo rudrā ādityāśca marutpathe
navayojanasāhasro vigraho@rkasya maṇḍalam // 142

8.s:
triguṇaṃ jñānaśaktiḥ sā tapatyarkatayā prabhoḥ /
svarlokastu bhuvarlokāddhruvāntaṃ paribhāṣyate // 143
8.d:
त्रिगुणं ज्ञानशक्तिः सा तपत्यर्कतया प्रभोः ।
स्वर्लोकस्तु भुवर्लोकाद्ध्रुवान्तं परिभाष्यते ॥ 143
8.m:
triguṇaṃ jñānaśaktiḥ sā tapatyarkatayā prabhoḥ
svarlokastu bhuvarlokāddhruvāntaṃ paribhāṣyate // 143

8.s:
sūryāllakṣeṇa śītāṃśuḥ kriyāśaktiḥ śivasya sā /
candrāllakṣeṇa nākṣatraṃ tato lakṣadvayena tu // 144
8.d:
सूर्याल्लक्षेण शीतांशुः क्रियाशक्तिः शिवस्य सा ।
चन्द्राल्लक्षेण नाक्षत्रं ततो लक्षद्वयेन तु ॥ 144
8.m:
sūryāllakṣeṇa śītāṃśuḥ kriyāśaktiḥ śivasya sā
candrāllakṣeṇa nākṣatraṃ tato lakṣadvayena tu // 144

8.s:
pratyekaṃ bhaumataḥ sūryasutānte pañcakaṃ viduḥ /
saurāllakṣeṇa saptarṣivargastasmāddhruvastathā // 145
8.d:
प्रत्येकं भौमतः सूर्यसुतान्ते पञ्चकं विदुः ।
सौराल्लक्षेण सप्तर्षिवर्गस्तस्माद्ध्रुवस्तथा ॥ 145
8.m:
pratyekaṃ bhaumataḥ sūryasutānte pañcakaṃ viduḥ
saurāllakṣeṇa saptarṣivargastasmāddhruvastathā // 145

8.s:
brahmaivāpararūpeṇa brahmasthāne dhruvo'calaḥ /
medhībhūto vimānānāṃ sarveṣāmupari dhruvaḥ // 146
8.d:
ब्रह्मैवापररूपेण ब्रह्मस्थाने ध्रुवोऽचलः ।
मेधीभूतो विमानानां सर्वेषामुपरि ध्रुवः ॥ 146
8.m:
brahmaivāpararūpeṇa brahmasthāne dhruvo@calaḥ
medhībhūto vimānānāṃ sarveṣāmupari dhruvaḥ // 146

8.s:
atra baddhāni sarvāṇyapyūhyante'nilamaṇḍale /
svassapta mārutaskandhā āmeghādyāḥ pradhānataḥ // 147
8.d:
अत्र बद्धानि सर्वाण्यप्यूह्यन्तेऽनिलमण्डले ।
स्वस्सप्त मारुतस्कन्धा आमेघाद्याः प्रधानतः ॥ 147
8.m:
atra baddhāni sarvāṇyapyūhyante@nilamaṇḍale
svassapta mārutaskandhā āmeghādyāḥ pradhānataḥ // 147

8.s:
itaśca kratuhotrādi kṛtvā jñānavivarjitāḥ /
svaryānti tatkṣaye lokaṃ mānuṣyaṃ puṇyaśeṣataḥ // 148
8.d:
इतश्च क्रतुहोत्रादि कृत्वा ज्ञानविवर्जिताः ।
स्वर्यान्ति तत्क्षये लोकं मानुष्यं पुण्यशेषतः ॥ 148
8.m:
itaśca kratuhotrādi kṛtvā jñānavivarjitāḥ
svaryānti tatkṣaye lokaṃ mānuṣyaṃ puṇyaśeṣataḥ // 148

8.s:
evaṃ bhūmerdhruvāntaṃ syāllakṣāṇi daśa pañca ca /
dve koṭī pañca cāśītirlakṣāṇi svargato mahān // 149
8.d:
एवं भूमेर्ध्रुवान्तं स्याल्लक्षाणि दश पञ्च च ।
द्वे कोटी पञ्च चाशीतिर्लक्षाणि स्वर्गतो महान् ॥ 149
8.m:
evaṃ bhūmerdhruvāntaṃ syāllakṣāṇi daśa pañca ca
dve koṭī pañca cāśītirlakṣāṇi svargato mahān // 149

8.s:
mārkaṇḍādyā ṛṣimunisiddhāstatra pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
nivartitādhikārāśca devā mahati saṃsthitāḥ // 150
8.d:
मार्कण्डाद्या ऋषिमुनिसिद्धास्तत्र प्रतिष्ठिताः ।
निवर्तिताधिकाराश्च देवा महति संस्थिताः ॥ 150
8.m:
mārkaṇḍādyā ṛṣimunisiddhāstatra pratiṣṭhitāḥ
nivartitādhikārāśca devā mahati saṃsthitāḥ // 150

8.s:
mahāntarāle tatrānye tvadhikārabhujo janāḥ /
aṣṭau koṭyo mahallokājjano'tra kapilādayaḥ // 151
8.d:
महान्तराले तत्रान्ये त्वधिकारभुजो जनाः ।
अष्टौ कोट्यो महल्लोकाज्जनोऽत्र कपिलादयः ॥ 151
8.m:
mahāntarāle tatrānye tvadhikārabhujo janāḥ
aṣṭau koṭyo mahallokājjano@tra kapilādayaḥ // 151

8.s:
tiṣṭhanti sādhyāstatraiva bahavaḥ sukhabhāginaḥ /
janāttaporkakoṭyo'tra sanakādyā mahādhiyaḥ // 152
8.d:
तिष्ठन्ति साध्यास्तत्रैव बहवः सुखभागिनः ।
जनात्तपोर्ककोट्योऽत्र सनकाद्या महाधियः ॥ 152
8.m:
tiṣṭhanti sādhyāstatraiva bahavaḥ sukhabhāginaḥ
janāttaporkakoṭyo@tra sanakādyā mahādhiyaḥ // 152

8.s:
prajāpatīnāṃ tatrādhikāro brahmātmajanmanām /
brahmālayastu tapasaḥ satyaḥ ṣoḍaśa koṭayaḥ // 153
8.d:
प्रजापतीनां तत्राधिकारो ब्रह्मात्मजन्मनाम् ।
ब्रह्मालयस्तु तपसः सत्यः षोडश कोटयः ॥ 153
8.m:
prajāpatīnāṃ tatrādhikāro brahmātmajanmanām
brahmālayastu tapasaḥ satyaḥ ṣoḍaśa koṭayaḥ // 153

8.s:
tatra sthitaḥ sa svayambhūrviśvamāviṣkarotyadaḥ /
satye vedāstathā cānye karmadhyānena bhāvitāḥ // 154
8.d:
तत्र स्थितः स स्वयम्भूर्विश्वमाविष्करोत्यदः ।
सत्ये वेदास्तथा चान्ये कर्मध्यानेन भाविताः ॥ 154
8.m:
tatra sthitaḥ sa svayambhūrviśvamāviṣkarotyadaḥ
satye vedāstathā cānye karmadhyānena bhāvitāḥ // 154

8.s:
ānandaniṣṭhāstatrordhvekoṭirvairiñcamāsanam /
brahmāsanātkoṭiyugmaṃ puraṃ viṣṇornirūpitam // 155
8.d:
आनन्दनिष्ठास्तत्रोर्ध्वेकोटिर्वैरिञ्चमासनम् ।
ब्रह्मासनात्कोटियुग्मं पुरं विष्णोर्निरूपितम् ॥ 155
8.m:
ānandaniṣṭhāstatrordhvekoṭirvairiñcamāsanam
brahmāsanātkoṭiyugmaṃ puraṃ viṣṇornirūpitam // 155

8.s:
dhyānapūjājapairviṣṇorbhaktā gacchanti tatpadam /
vaiṣṇavātsaptakoṭībhirbhuvanaṃ parameśituḥ // 156
8.d:
ध्यानपूजाजपैर्विष्णोर्भक्ता गच्छन्ति तत्पदम् ।
वैष्णवात्सप्तकोटीभिर्भुवनं परमेशितुः ॥ 156
8.m:
dhyānapūjājapairviṣṇorbhaktā gacchanti tatpadam
vaiṣṇavātsaptakoṭībhirbhuvanaṃ parameśituḥ // 156

8.s:
rudrasya sṛṣṭisaṃhārakarturbrahmāṇḍavartmani /
dīkṣājñānavihīnā ye liṅgārādhanatatparāḥ // 157
8.d:
रुद्रस्य सृष्टिसंहारकर्तुर्ब्रह्माण्डवर्त्मनि ।
दीक्षाज्ञानविहीना ये लिङ्गाराधनतत्पराः ॥ 157
8.m:
