rudrasya sṛṣṭisaṃhārakarturbrahmāṇḍavartmani
dīkṣājñānavihīnā ye liṅgārādhanatatparāḥ // 157

8.s:
te yāntyaṇḍāntare raudraṃ puraṃ nādhaḥ kadācana /
tatsthāḥ sarve śivaṃ yānti rudrāḥ śrīkaṇṭhadīkṣitāḥ // 158
8.d:
ते यान्त्यण्डान्तरे रौद्रं पुरं नाधः कदाचन ।
तत्स्थाः सर्वे शिवं यान्ति रुद्राः श्रीकण्ठदीक्षिताः ॥ 158
8.m:
te yāntyaṇḍāntare raudraṃ puraṃ nādhaḥ kadācana
tatsthāḥ sarve śivaṃ yānti rudrāḥ śrīkaṇṭhadīkṣitāḥ // 158

8.s:
adhikārakṣaye sākaṃ rudrakanyāgaṇena te /
puraṃ puraṃ ca rudrordhvamuttarottaravṛddhitaḥ // 159
8.d:
अधिकारक्षये साकं रुद्रकन्यागणेन ते ।
पुरं पुरं च रुद्रोर्ध्वमुत्तरोत्तरवृद्धितः ॥ 159
8.m:
When their term of office is exhausted, together with the host of Rudra-maidens,
they [proceed] from city to city above the Rudras through progressive ascent. // 159

8.s:
brahmāṇḍādhaśca rudrordhva daṇḍapāṇeḥ puraṃ sa ca /
śivecchayā dṛṇātyaṇḍaṃ mokṣamārga karoti ca // 160
8.d:
ब्रह्माण्डाधश्च रुद्रोर्ध्व दण्डपाणेः पुरं स च ।
शिवेच्छया दृणात्यण्डं मोक्षमार्ग करोति च ॥ 160
8.m:
Below the cosmic egg of Brahmā and above the Rudras is the city of Daṇḍapāṇi; and he,
by Śiva's will, pierces the cosmic egg and prepares the path to liberation. // 160

8.s:
śarvarudrau bhīmabhavāvugro devo mahānatha /
īśāna iti bhūrlokāt sapta lokeśvarāḥ śivāḥ // 161
8.d:
शर्वरुद्रौ भीमभवावुग्रो देवो महानथ ।
ईशान इति भूर्लोकात् सप्त लोकेश्वराः शिवाः ॥ 161
8.m:
Śarva, Rudra, Bhīma, Bhava, Ugra, Mahādeva, and then
Īśāna—these seven, starting from Bhūrloka, are the benevolent lords of the worlds. // 161

8.s:
sthūlairviśeṣairārabdhāḥ sapta lokāḥ pare punaḥ /
sūkṣmairiti guruścaiva rurau samyaṅnyarūpayat // 162
8.d:
स्थूलैर्विशेषैरारब्धाः सप्त लोकाः परे पुनः ।
सूक्ष्मैरिति गुरुश्चैव रुरौ सम्यङ्न्यरूपयत् ॥ 162
8.m:
The seven worlds are constituted by the gross specific [elements], but the higher ones
by subtle ones—so the guru explained thoroughly in the Raurava. // 162

8.s:
ye brahmaṇādisarge svaśarīrānnirmitāḥ prabhūtākhyāḥ /
sthūlāḥ pañca viśeṣāḥ saptāmī tanmayā lokāḥ // 163
8.d:
ये ब्रह्मणादिसर्गे स्वशरीरान्निर्मिताः प्रभूताख्याः ।
स्थूलाः पञ्च विशेषाः सप्तामी तन्मया लोकाः ॥ 163
8.m:
Those five gross specific [elements] termed 'elements' (prabhūta), created by Brahmā and others from their own bodies at the beginning of creation—
these seven worlds consist of them. // 163

8.s:
parato liṅgādhāraiḥ sūkṣmaistanmātrajairmahābhūtaiḥ /
lokānāmāvaraṇairviṣṭabhya parasperaṇa gandhādyaiḥ // 164
8.d:
परतो लिङ्गाधारैः सूक्ष्मैस्तन्मात्रजैर्महाभूतैः ।
लोकानामावरणैर्विष्टभ्य परस्पेरण गन्धाद्यैः ॥ 164
8.m:
Beyond that, [the worlds are constituted] by the subtle gross elements born of the subtle elements, which are the receptacles of subtle bodies;
supporting each other through smell and the other [qualities] as the coverings of the worlds. // 164

8.s:
kālāgnerdaṇḍapāṇyantamaṣṭānavatikoṭayaḥ /
ata ūrdhvaṃ kaṭāho'ṇḍe sa ghanaḥ koṭiyojanam // 165
8.d:
कालाग्नेर्दण्डपाण्यन्तमष्टानवतिकोटयः ।
अत ऊर्ध्वं कटाहोऽण्डे स घनः कोटियोजनम् ॥ 165
8.m:
From Kālāgni up to Daṇḍapāṇi is ninety-eight crores [of yojanas].
Above this, the hemisphere of the cosmic egg is solid, one crore of yojanas [thick]. // 165

8.s:
pañcāśatkoṭayaścordhvaṃ bhūpṛṣṭhādadharaṃ tathā /
evaṃ koṭiśataṃ bhūḥ syāt sauvarṇastaṇḍulastataḥ // 166
8.d:
पञ्चाशत्कोटयश्चोर्ध्वं भूपृष्ठादधरं तथा ।
एवं कोटिशतं भूः स्यात् सौवर्णस्तण्डुलस्ततः ॥ 166
8.m:
Fifty crores [extend] upward from the surface of the earth, and likewise below.
Thus the earth measures one hundred crores; beyond that is the golden grain. // 166

8.s:
śatarudrāvadhirhuphaṭ bhedayettattu duḥśamam /
pratidikkaṃ daśa daśetyevaṃ rudraśataṃ bahiḥ // 167
8.d:
शतरुद्रावधिर्हुफट् भेदयेत्तत्तु दुःशमम् ।
प्रतिदिक्कं दश दशेत्येवं रुद्रशतं बहिः ॥ 167
8.m:
Reaching up to the hundred Rudras, 'huṃ phaṭ' pierces that which is difficult to subdue.
Ten in each direction: thus a hundred Rudras dwell outside, // 167

8.s:
brahmāṇḍādhārakaṃ tacca svaprabhāveṇa sarvataḥ /
aṇḍasvarūpaṃ gurubhiścoktaṃ śrīrauravādiṣu // 168
8.d:
ब्रह्माण्डाधारकं तच्च स्वप्रभावेण सर्वतः ।
अण्डस्वरूपं गुरुभिश्चोक्तं श्रीरौरवादिषु ॥ 168
8.m:
supporting the cosmic egg everywhere by their own power.
The nature of the cosmic egg has also been explained by the teachers in the venerable Raurava and other scriptures: // 168

8.s:
vyakterabhimukhībhūtaḥ pracyutaḥ śaktirūpataḥ /
āvāpavānanirbhakto vastupiṇḍo'ṇḍa ucyate // 169
8.d:
व्यक्तेरभिमुखीभूतः प्रच्युतः शक्तिरूपतः ।
आवापवाननिर्भक्तो वस्तुपिण्डोऽण्ड उच्यते ॥ 169
8.m:
'Turned toward manifestation, fallen from the condition of power,
having internal differentiation and undivided—such an aggregate of entities is called a cosmic egg.' // 169

8.s:
tamoleśānuviddhasya kapālaṃ sattvamuttaram /
rajo'nuviddhaṃ nirmṛṣṭaṃ sattvamasyādharaṃ tamaḥ // 170
8.d:
तमोलेशानुविद्धस्य कपालं सत्त्वमुत्तरम् ।
रजोऽनुविद्धं निर्मृष्टं सत्त्वमस्याधरं तमः ॥ 170
8.m:
Its upper hemisphere is sattva touched by a trace of tamas;
its lower hemisphere is tamas, wiped clean [yet] touched by rajas and sattva. // 170

8.s:
vastupiṇḍa iti proktaṃ śivaśaktisamūhabhāk /
aṇḍaḥ syāditi tadvyaktau saṃmukhībhāva ucyate // 171
8.d:
वस्तुपिण्ड इति प्रोक्तं शिवशक्तिसमूहभाक् ।
अण्डः स्यादिति तद्व्यक्तौ संमुखीभाव उच्यते ॥ 171
8.m:
It is called an 'aggregate of entities' because it comprises the collection of Śiva's powers;
that it 'would be a cosmic egg' means it is oriented toward its manifestation. // 171

8.s:
tathāpi śivamagnānāṃ śaktīnāmaṇḍatā bhavet /
tadartha vākyamaparaṃ tā hi na cyutaśaktitaḥ // 172
8.d:
तथापि शिवमग्नानां शक्तीनामण्डता भवेत् ।
तदर्थ वाक्यमपरं ता हि न च्युतशक्तितः ॥ 172
8.m:
Even so, powers merged in Śiva could be considered a cosmic egg;
for that purpose another phrase [is given]: 'they indeed have not fallen from the condition of power.' // 172

8.s:
tanvakṣādau mā prasāṅkṣīdaṇḍateti padāntaram /
tanvakṣādiṣu naivāste kasyāpyāvāpanaṃ yataḥ // 173
8.d:
तन्वक्षादौ मा प्रसाङ्क्षीदण्डतेति पदान्तरम् ।
तन्वक्षादिषु नैवास्ते कस्याप्यावापनं यतः ॥ 173
8.m:
Lest the nature of a cosmic egg be erroneously applied to the body, sense organs, and so on, there is another word:
for in the body, sense organs, and so forth, there is no internal differentiation whatsoever. // 173

8.s:
tanvakṣasamudāyatve kathamekatvamityataḥ /
anirbhakta iti proktaṃ sājātyaparidarśakam // 174
8.d:
तन्वक्षसमुदायत्वे कथमेकत्वमित्यतः ।
अनिर्भक्त इति प्रोक्तं साजात्यपरिदर्शकम् ॥ 174
8.m:
To answer how oneness exists when there is an aggregate of bodies, organs, and so on,
it is said to be 'undivided', indicating a common genus. // 174

8.s:
vināpi vastupiṇḍākhyapadenaikaikaśo bhavet /
tattveṣvaṇḍasvabhāvatvaṃ nanvevamapi kiṃ na tat // 175
8.d:
विनापि वस्तुपिण्डाख्यपदेनैकैकशो भवेत् ।
तत्त्वेष्वण्डस्वभावत्वं नन्वेवमपि किं न तत् ॥ 175
8.m:
[Objection:] Even without the term 'aggregate of entities', each principle individually
would possess the nature of a cosmic egg. Indeed, even so, why is it not that? // 175

8.s:
guṇatanmātrabhūtaughamaye tattve prasajyate /
ucyate vastuśabdena tanvakṣabhuvanātmakam // 176
8.d:
गुणतन्मात्रभूतौघमये तत्त्वे प्रसज्यते ।
उच्यते वस्तुशब्देन तन्वक्षभुवनात्मकम् ॥ 176
8.m:
It would apply to a principle consisting of the guṇas, subtle elements, and gross elements.
[Reply:] By the word 'entity' (vastu) is meant that which consists of body, organs, and worlds; // 176

8.s:
rūpamuktaṃ yatastena tatsamūho'ṇḍa ucyate /
bhavecca tatsamūhatvaṃ patyurviśvavapurbhṛtaḥ // 177
8.d:
रूपमुक्तं यतस्तेन तत्समूहोऽण्ड उच्यते ।
भवेच्च तत्समूहत्वं पत्युर्विश्ववपुर्भृतः ॥ 177
8.m:
since that form has been stated, their aggregate is called a cosmic egg.
And that status of an aggregate would also belong to the Lord who bears the cosmic form; // 177

8.s:
tadartha bhedakānyanyānyupāttānīti darśitam /
tāvanmātrāsvavasthāsu māyādhīne'dhvamaṇḍale // 178
8.d:
तदर्थ भेदकान्यन्यान्युपात्तानीति दर्शितम् ।
तावन्मात्रास्ववस्थासु मायाधीनेऽध्वमण्डले ॥ 178
8.m:
for that reason other distinguishing terms have been adopted—this has been shown.
In such states alone, within the circle of the path dependent on Māyā, // 178

8.s:
mā bhūdaṇḍatvamityāhuranye bhedakayojanam /
itthamuktaviriñcāṇḍamṛto rudrāḥ śataṃ hi yat // 179
8.d:
मा भूदण्डत्वमित्याहुरन्ये भेदकयोजनम् ।
इत्थमुक्तविरिञ्चाण्डमृतो रुद्राः शतं हि यत् ॥ 179
8.m:
lest there be egg-nature—so say others explaining the application of the distinguishing attributes.
Thus, outside the described cosmic egg of Brahmā, there are indeed a hundred Rudras; // 179

8.s:
teṣāṃ sve patayo rudrā ekādaśa mahārciṣaḥ /
ananto'tha kapālyāgniryamanairṛtakau balaḥ // 180
8.d:
तेषां स्वे पतयो रुद्रा एकादश महार्चिषः ।
अनन्तोऽथ कपाल्याग्निर्यमनैरृतकौ बलः ॥ 180
8.m:
their own lords are eleven Rudras of great radiance:
Ananta, then Kapālī, Agni, Yama, Nirṛti, Bala, // 180

8.s:
śīghro nidhīśo vidyeśaḥ śambhuḥ savīrabhadrakaḥ /
madhu madhukṛtaḥ kadambaṃ kesarajālāni yadvadāvṛṇate // 181
8.d:
शीघ्रो निधीशो विद्येशः शम्भुः सवीरभद्रकः ।
मधु मधुकृतः कदम्बं केसरजालानि यद्वदावृणते ॥ 181
8.m:
Śīghra, Nidhīśa, Vidyeśa, Śambhu, together with Vīrabhadra.
Just as the filaments enclose the sweet kadamba blossom that produces honey, // 181

8.s:
tadvatte śivarudrā brahmāṇḍamasaṃkhyaparivārāḥ /
śarāṣṭaniyutaṃ koṭirityeṣāṃ sanniveśanam // 182
8.d:
तद्वत्ते शिवरुद्रा ब्रह्माण्डमसंख्यपरिवाराः ।
शराष्टनियुतं कोटिरित्येषां सन्निवेशनम् ॥ 182
8.m:
so these Rudras of Śiva, having countless retinues, surround the cosmic egg;
their disposition is five times eight lakhs, one crore. // 182

8.s:
śrīkaṇṭhādhiṣṭhitāste ca sṛjanti saṃharanti ca /
īśvaratvaṃ diviṣadāmiti rauravavārtike // 183
8.d:
श्रीकण्ठाधिष्ठितास्ते च सृजन्ति संहरन्ति च ।
ईश्वरत्वं दिविषदामिति रौरववार्तिके ॥ 183
8.m:
And presided over by Śrīkaṇṭha, they create and dissolve;
such is the lordship over the celestials, according to the Rauravavārttika. // 183

8.s:
siddhātantre tu hemāṇḍācchatakoṭerbahiḥ śatam /
aṇḍānāṃ kramaśo dvidviguṇaṃ rūpyādiyojitam // 184
8.d:
सिद्धातन्त्रे तु हेमाण्डाच्छतकोटेर्बहिः शतम् ।
अण्डानां क्रमशो द्विद्विगुणं रूप्यादियोजितम् ॥ 184
8.m:
In the Siddhātantra, however, outside the hundred crores of the golden egg, there are a hundred
cosmic eggs, sequentially doubled in size, made of silver and so on. // 184

8.s:
teṣu krameṇa brahmāṇaḥ saṃsyurdviguṇajīvitāḥ /
kṣīyante kramaśaste ca tadante tattvamammayam // 185
8.d:
तेषु क्रमेण ब्रह्माणः संस्युर्द्विगुणजीविताः ।
क्षीयन्ते क्रमशस्ते च तदन्ते तत्त्वमम्मयम् ॥ 185
8.m:
In them, in succession, there are Brahmās whose lifespans are doubled;
they are destroyed in turn, and at their end is the water principle. // 185

8.s:
dharāto'tra jalādi syāduttarottarataḥ kramāt /
daśadhāhaṅkṛtāntaṃ dhīstasyāḥ syācchatadhā tataḥ // 186
8.d:
धरातोऽत्र जलादि स्यादुत्तरोत्तरतः क्रमात् ।
दशधाहङ्कृतान्तं धीस्तस्याः स्याच्छतधा ततः ॥ 186
8.m:
From the earth here, water and the rest proceed upward in succession:
[the sphere of water] ten times [the earth], intellect up to egoity ten times [that], and beyond that [prakṛti] a hundred times; // 186

8.s:
sahasradhā vyaktamataḥ pauṃsnaṃ daśasahasradhā /
niyatirlakṣadhā tasmāttasyāstu daśalakṣadhā // 187
8.d:
सहस्रधा व्यक्तमतः पौंस्नं दशसहस्रधा ।
नियतिर्लक्षधा तस्मात्तस्यास्तु दशलक्षधा ॥ 187
8.m:
then the unmanifest a thousand times; the self ten thousand times;
niyati a hundred thousand times; and above that [rāga] ten hundred thousand times; // 187

8.s:
kalāntaṃ koṭidhā tasmānmāyā viddaśakoṭidhā /
īśvaraḥ śatakoṭiḥ syāttasmātkoṭisahasradhā // 188
8.d:
कलान्तं कोटिधा तस्मान्माया विद्दशकोटिधा ।
ईश्वरः शतकोटिः स्यात्तस्मात्कोटिसहस्रधा ॥ 188
8.m:
up to kalā a crore of times; from that, Māyā a crore; knowledge ten crores;
Īśvara a hundred crores; and beyond that [Sadāśiva] a thousand crores; // 188

8.s:
sādākhyaṃ vyaśnute tacca śaktirvṛndena saṃkhyayā /
vyāpinī sarvamadhvānaṃ vyāpyadevī vyavasthitā // 189
8.d:
सादाख्यं व्यश्नुते तच्च शक्तिर्वृन्देन संख्यया ।
व्यापिनी सर्वमध्वानं व्याप्यदेवी व्यवस्थिता ॥ 189
8.m:
it pervades the Sadāśiva principle; and Śakti, with her multitudes,
as the all-pervading goddess, Vyāpinī, stands pervading the entire path. // 189

8.s:
aprameyaṃ tataḥ śuddhaṃ śivatattvaṃ paraṃ viduḥ /
jalādeḥ śivatattvāntaṃ na dṛṣṭaṃ kenacicchivāt // 190
8.d:
अप्रमेयं ततः शुद्धं शिवतत्त्वं परं विदुः ।
जलादेः शिवतत्त्वान्तं न दृष्टं केनचिच्छिवात् ॥ 190
8.m:
Beyond that, they know the immeasurable, pure Śiva principle to be supreme.
From water up to the Śiva principle, nothing has been seen by anyone except from Śiva; // 190

8.s:
ṛte tataḥ śivajñānaṃ paramaṃ mokṣakāraṇam /
tathā cāha mahādevaḥ śrīmatsvacchandaśāsane // 191
8.d:
ऋते ततः शिवज्ञानं परमं मोक्षकारणम् ।
तथा चाह महादेवः श्रीमत्स्वच्छन्दशासने ॥ 191
8.m:
therefore knowledge of Śiva is the supreme cause of liberation.
And so the Great God declared in the venerable Svacchandaśāsana: // 191

8.s:
nānyathā mokṣamāyāti paśurjñānaśatairapi /
śivajñānaṃ na bhavati dīkṣāmaprāpya śāṅkarīm // 192
8.d:
नान्यथा मोक्षमायाति पशुर्ज्ञानशतैरपि ।
शिवज्ञानं न भवति दीक्षामप्राप्य शाङ्करीम् ॥ 192
8.m:
'The bound soul does not attain liberation otherwise, even through hundreds of teachings;
knowledge of Śiva does not arise without receiving the initiation of Śaṅkara.' // 192

8.s:
prāktanī pārameśī sā pauruṣeyī ca sā punaḥ /
śatarudrordhvato bhadrakālyā nīlaprabhaṃ jayam // 193
8.d:
प्राक्तनी पारमेशी सा पौरुषेयी च सा पुनः ।
शतरुद्रोर्ध्वतो भद्रकाल्या नीलप्रभं जयम् ॥ 193
8.m:
That [initiation] is primordial, belonging to the Supreme Lord, and it is also human.
Above the hundred Rudras is Jayā, the city of Bhadrakālī of blue lustre. // 193

8.s:
na yajñadānatapasā prāpyaṃ kālyāḥ puraṃ jayam /
tadbhaktāstatra gacchanti tanmaṇḍalasudīkṣitāḥ // 194
8.d:
न यज्ञदानतपसा प्राप्यं काल्याः पुरं जयम् ।
तद्भक्तास्तत्र गच्छन्ति तन्मण्डलसुदीक्षिताः ॥ 194
8.m:
Jayā, the city of Kālī, is not to be attained by sacrifice, gifts, or austerity;
her devotees go there, well-initiated in her maṇḍala. // 194

8.s:
nirbījadīkṣayā mokṣaṃ dadāti parameśvarī /
vidyeśāvaraṇe dīkṣāṃ yāvatīṃ kurute nṛṇām // 195
8.d:
निर्बीजदीक्षया मोक्षं ददाति परमेश्वरी ।
विद्येशावरणे दीक्षां यावतीं कुरुते नृणाम् ॥ 195
8.m:
Through seedless initiation, the Supreme Goddess grants liberation;
to whatever extent she performs initiation for men within the retinue of the Lord of Knowledge, // 195

8.s:
tāvatīṃ gatimāyānti bhuvane'tra niveśitāḥ /
tataḥ koṭyā vīrabhadro yugāntāgnisamaprabhaḥ // 196
8.d:
तावतीं गतिमायान्ति भुवनेऽत्र निवेशिताः ।
ततः कोट्या वीरभद्रो युगान्ताग्निसमप्रभः ॥ 196
8.m:
to that extent they attain the destination, established in this realm.
Beyond that, at a distance of a crore, is Vīrabhadra, radiant as the fire of cosmic dissolution. // 196

8.s:
vijayākhyaṃ puraṃ cāsya ye smaranto maheśvaram /
jaleṣu maruṣu cāgnau śiraśchedena vā mṛtāḥ // 197
8.d:
विजयाख्यं पुरं चास्य ये स्मरन्तो महेश्वरम् ।
जलेषु मरुषु चाग्नौ शिरश्छेदेन वा मृताः ॥ 197
8.m:
And his city is called Vijayā; those who, remembering the Great Lord,
have died in water, in deserts, in fire, or by decapitation, // 197

8.s:
te yānti bodhamaiśānaṃ vīrabhadraṃ mahādyutim /
vairabhadrordhvataḥ koṭirviṣkambhādvistṛtaṃ tridhā // 198
8.d:
ते यान्ति बोधमैशानं वीरभद्रं महाद्युतिम् ।
वैरभद्रोर्ध्वतः कोटिर्विष्कम्भाद्विस्तृतं त्रिधा ॥ 198
8.m:
attain the divine consciousness, Vīrabhadra of great splendour.
Above Vīrabhadra's [city], one crore in diameter, extended threefold, // 198

8.s:
rudrāṇḍaṃ sālilaṃ tvaṇḍaṃ śakracāpākṛti sthitam /
ā vīrabhadrabhuvanādbhadrakālyālayāttathā // 199
8.d:
रुद्राण्डं सालिलं त्वण्डं शक्रचापाकृति स्थितम् ।
आ वीरभद्रभुवनाद्भद्रकाल्यालयात्तथा ॥ 199
8.m:
is the cosmic egg of Rudra, the watery egg, situated in the shape of Indra's bow [a rainbow],
extending from the world of Vīrabhadra and the abode of Bhadrakālī, // 199

8.s:
trayodaśabhiranyaiśca bhuvanairupaśobhitam /
tato bhuvaḥ sahādreḥ pūrgandhatanmātradhāraṇāt // 200
8.d:
त्रयोदशभिरन्यैश्च भुवनैरुपशोभितम् ।
ततो भुवः सहाद्रेः पूर्गन्धतन्मात्रधारणात् ॥ 200
8.m:
adorned with thirteen other worlds.
Beyond that is the city of Earth with the mountain: by holding the subtle element of smell, // 200

8.s:
mṛtā gacchanti tāṃ bhūmiṃ dharitryāḥ paramāṃ budhāḥ /
abdheḥ puraṃ tatastvāpyaṃ rasatanmātradhāraṇāt // 201
8.d:
मृता गच्छन्ति तां भूमिं धरित्र्याः परमां बुधाः ।
अब्धेः पुरं ततस्त्वाप्यं रसतन्मात्रधारणात् ॥ 201
8.m:
the wise, upon dying, go to that supreme land of the Earth.
Then is the city of the Ocean, watery, [attained] by holding the subtle element of taste. // 201

8.s:
tataḥ śriyaḥ puraṃ rudrakrīḍāvataraṇeṣvatha /
prayāgādau śrīgirau ca viśeṣānmaraṇena tat // 202
8.d:
ततः श्रियः पुरं रुद्रक्रीडावतरणेष्वथ ।
प्रयागादौ श्रीगिरौ च विशेषान्मरणेन तत् ॥ 202
8.m:
Then is the city of Śrī; and in the places of descent for Rudra's play,
at Prayāga and elsewhere, and especially through dying on Śrīparvata, [that city is attained]. // 202

8.s:
sārasvataṃ puraṃ tasmācchabdabrahmavidāṃ padam /
rudrocitāstā mukhyatvādrudrebhyo'nyāstathā sthitāḥ // 203
8.d:
सारस्वतं पुरं तस्माच्छब्दब्रह्मविदां पदम् ।
रुद्रोचितास्ता मुख्यत्वाद्रुद्रेभ्योऽन्यास्तथा स्थिताः ॥ 203
8.m:
Beyond that is the city of Sarasvatī, the abode of those who know the sound-Brahman;
those suitable for Rudras, being foremost, are situated distinct from the [ordinary] Rudras. // 203

8.s:
pureṣu bahudhā gaṅgā devādau śrīḥ sarasvatī /
lakulādyamareśāntā aṣṭāvapsu surādhipāḥ // 204
8.d:
पुरेषु बहुधा गङ्गा देवादौ श्रीः सरस्वती ।
लकुलाद्यमरेशान्ता अष्टावप्सु सुराधिपाः ॥ 204
8.m: In the cities the Gaṅgā flows in many streams; in heaven and elsewhere dwell Śrī and Sarasvatī; / and the eight lords of the gods, beginning with Lakulin and ending with Amareśa, reside in the waters.

8.s:
tatastu taijasaṃ tattvaṃ śivāgneratra saṃsthitiḥ /
te cainaṃ vahnimāyānti vāhnīṃ ye dhāraṇāṃ śritāḥ // 205
8.d:
ततस्तु तैजसं तत्त्वं शिवाग्नेरत्र संस्थितिः ।
ते चैनं वह्निमायान्ति वाह्नीं ये धारणां श्रिताः ॥ 205
8.m: Then, however, is the element of fire; here is the dwelling of the fire of Śiva. / And those who have relied upon the concentration on fire attain this fire. // 205

8.s:
bhairavādiharīndvantaṃ taijase nāyakāṣṭakam /
prāṇasya bhuvanaṃ vāyordaśadhā daśadhā tu tat // 206
8.d:
भैरवादिहरीन्द्वन्तं तैजसे नायकाष्टकम् ।
प्राणस्य भुवनं वायोर्दशधा दशधा तु तत् ॥ 206
8.m: In the fiery [element] there is an octad of rulers beginning with Bhairava and ending with Harīndu. / The realm of wind, of prāṇa, however, is tenfold and tenfold. // 206

8.s:
dhyātvā tyaktvātha vā prāṇān kṛtvā tatraiva dhāraṇām /
taṃ viśanti mahātmāno vāyubhūtāḥ khamūrtayaḥ // 207
8.d:
ध्यात्वा त्यक्त्वाथ वा प्राणान् कृत्वा तत्रैव धारणाम् ।
तं विशन्ति महात्मानो वायुभूताः खमूर्तयः ॥ 207
8.m: Having meditated, or else having abandoned the vital breaths, performing concentration right there, / the great-souled ones enter it, having become wind, forms of space. // 207

8.s:
bhīmādigayaparyantamaṣṭakaṃ vāyutattvagam /
khatattve bhuvanaṃ vyomnaḥ prāpyaṃ tadvyomadhāraṇāt // 208
8.d:
भीमादिगयपर्यन्तमष्टकं वायुतत्त्वगम् ।
खतत्त्वे भुवनं व्योम्नः प्राप्यं तद्व्योमधारणात् ॥ 208
8.m: The octad beginning with Bhīma and ending with Gaya belongs to the element of wind. / In the element of space is the realm of ether, attainable by concentration on that ether. // 208

8.s:
vastrāpadāntaṃ sthāṇvādi vyomatattve surāṣṭakam /
adīkṣitā ye bhūteṣu śivatattvābhimāninaḥ // 209
8.d:
वस्त्रापदान्तं स्थाण्वादि व्योमतत्त्वे सुराष्टकम् ।
अदीक्षिता ये भूतेषु शिवतत्त्वाभिमानिनः ॥ 209
8.m: The octad of gods beginning with Sthāṇu and ending with Vastrāpada is in the element of space. / Those uninitiated who identify with the principle of Śiva among the elements, // 209

8.s:
jñānahīnā api prauḍhadhāraṇāste'ṇḍato bahiḥ /
dharābdhitejo'nilakhapuragā dīkṣitāśca vā // 210
8.d:
ज्ञानहीना अपि प्रौढधारणास्तेऽण्डतो बहिः ।
धराब्धितेजोऽनिलखपुरगा दीक्षिताश्च वा ॥ 210
8.m: though devoid of knowledge, having fully developed concentration, outside the egg [of Brahmā], / go to the cities of earth, water, fire, wind, and space; or those initiated // 210

8.s:
tāvatsaṃskārayogārthaṃ na paraṃ padamīhitum /
tathāvidhāvatāreṣu mṛtāścāyataneṣu ye // 211
8.d:
तावत्संस्कारयोगार्थं न परं पदमीहितुम् ।
तथाविधावतारेषु मृताश्चायतनेषु ये ॥ 211
8.m: merely for the sake of purification, without striving for the supreme state, / and those who die in sanctuaries during such incarnations, // 211

8.s:
tatpadaṃ te samāsādya kramādyānti śivātmatām /
punaḥ punaridaṃ coktaṃ śrīmaddevyākhyayāmale // 212
8.d:
तत्पदं ते समासाद्य क्रमाद्यान्ति शिवात्मताम् ।
पुनः पुनरिदं चोक्तं श्रीमद्देव्याख्ययामले ॥ 212
8.m: having attained that state, gradually attain the nature of Śiva. / And this has been stated again and again in the venerable Devyākhyayāmala. // 212

8.s:
śrīkāmikāyāṃ kaśmīravarṇane coktavānvibhuḥ /
sureśvarīmahādhāmni ye mriyante ca tatpure // 213
8.d:
श्रीकामिकायां कश्मीरवर्णने चोक्तवान्विभुः ।
सुरेश्वरीमहाधाम्नि ये म्रियन्ते च तत्पुरे ॥ 213
8.m: And in the venerable Kāmikā, in the description of Kashmir, the all-pervading Lord has spoken: / 'Those who die in the great abode of Sureśvarī and in that city, // 213

8.s:
brāhmaṇādyāḥ saṅkarāntāḥ paśavaḥ sthāvarāntagāḥ /
rudrajātaya evaite ityāha bhagavāñchivaḥ // 214
8.d:
ब्राह्मणाद्याः सङ्करान्ताः पशवः स्थावरान्तगाः ।
रुद्रजातय एवैते इत्याह भगवाञ्छिवः ॥ 214
8.m: whether Brahmins down to mixed castes, animals, down to immovable beings, / are indeed of the lineage of Rudra'—thus spoke the blessed Śiva. // 214

8.s:
ākāśāvaraṇādūrdhvamahaṅkārādadhaḥ priye /
tanmātrādimano'ntānāṃ purāṇi śivaśāsane // 215
8.d:
आकाशावरणादूर्ध्वमहङ्कारादधः प्रिये ।
तन्मात्रादिमनोऽन्तानां पुराणि शिवशासने ॥ 215
8.m: Above the enclosure of space, and below the ego, O dear one, / are the cities of [the principles] beginning with the subtle elements and ending with the mind, according to the teaching of Śiva. // 215

8.s:
pañcavarṇayutaṃ gandhatanmātramaṇḍalaṃ mahat /
ācchādya yojanānekakoṭibhiḥ sthitamantarā // 216
8.d:
पञ्चवर्णयुतं गन्धतन्मात्रमण्डलं महत् ।
आच्छाद्य योजनानेककोटिभिः स्थितमन्तरा ॥ 216
8.m: The great orb of the subtle element of odor, endowed with five colors, / having covered many crores of leagues, is situated within. // 216

8.s:
evaṃ rasādimātrāṇāṃ maṇḍalāni svavarṇata /
śarvo bhavaḥ paśupatirīśo bhīma iti kramāt // 217
8.d:
एवं रसादिमात्राणां मण्डलानि स्ववर्णत ।
शर्वो भवः पशुपतिरीशो भीम इति क्रमात् ॥ 217
8.m: In the same way are the orbs of the subtle elements of taste and the rest, according to their own colors. / Śarva, Bhava, Paśupati, Īśa, and Bhīma, in succession, // 217

8.s:
tanmātreśā yadicchātaḥ śabdādyāḥ khādikāriṇaḥ /
tataḥ sūryenduvedānāṃ maṇḍalāni vibhurmahān // 218
8.d:
तन्मात्रेशा यदिच्छातः शब्दाद्याः खादिकारिणः ।
ततः सूर्येन्दुवेदानां मण्डलानि विभुर्महान् ॥ 218
8.m: are the lords of the subtle elements, by whose will sound and the rest bring forth ether and the others. / Then are the orbs of the sun, moon, and Vedas; the all-pervading, the Great, // 218

8.s:
ugraścetyeṣu patayastebhyo'rkendū sayājakau /
ityaṣṭau tanavaḥ śaṃbhoryāḥ parāḥ parikīrtitāḥ // 219
8.d:
उग्रश्चेत्येषु पतयस्तेभ्योऽर्केन्दू सयाजकौ ।
इत्यष्टौ तनवः शंभोर्याः पराः परिकीर्तिताः ॥ 219
8.m: and Ugra are the lords in these; beyond them are the sun and the moon together with the sacrificer. / Thus are the eight cosmic forms of Śambhu which are proclaimed as supreme. // 219

8.s:
aparā brahmaṇo'ṇḍe tā vyāpya sarvaṃ vyavasthitāḥ /
kalpe kalpe prasūyante dharādyāstābhya eva tu // 220
8.d:
अपरा ब्रह्मणोऽण्डे ता व्याप्य सर्वं व्यवस्थिताः ।
कल्पे कल्पे प्रसूयन्ते धराद्यास्ताभ्य एव तु ॥ 220
8.m: The lower ones, having pervaded everything in the egg of Brahmā, are established; / in aeon after aeon, earth and the others are born from these alone. // 220

8.s:
tato vāgādikarmākṣayuktaṃ karaṇamaṇḍalam /
agnīndraviṣṇumitrāḥ sabrahmāṇasteṣu nāyakāḥ // 221
8.d:
ततो वागादिकर्माक्षयुक्तं करणमण्डलम् ।
अग्नीन्द्रविष्णुमित्राः सब्रह्माणस्तेषु नायकाः ॥ 221
8.m: Then comes the sphere of the organs of action, beginning with speech; / Agni, Indra, Viṣṇu, and Mitra, together with Brahmā, are the chiefs among them. // 221

8.s:
prakāśamaṇḍalaṃ tasmācchrutaṃ buddhyakṣapañcakam /
digvidyudarkavaruṇabhuvaḥ śrotrādidevatāḥ // 222
8.d:
प्रकाशमण्डलं तस्माच्छ्रुतं बुद्ध्यक्षपञ्चकम् ।
दिग्विद्युदर्कवरुणभुवः श्रोत्रादिदेवताः ॥ 222
8.m: Beyond that is the realm of light, taught as the five organs of sense; / the directions, lightning, sun, Varuṇa, and earth are the deities of hearing and the rest. // 222

8.s:
prakāśamaṇḍalādūrdhvaṃ sthitaṃ pañcārthamaṇḍalam /
manomaṇḍalametasmāt somenādhiṣṭhitaṃ yataḥ // 223
8.d:
प्रकाशमण्डलादूर्ध्वं स्थितं पञ्चार्थमण्डलम् ।
मनोमण्डलमेतस्मात् सोमेनाधिष्ठितं यतः ॥ 223
8.m: Above the realm of light is situated the realm of the five sense-objects. / Beyond this is the realm of the mind, because it is presided over by Soma; // 223

8.s:
bāhyadeveṣvadhiṣṭhātā sāmyaiśvaryasukhātmakaḥ /
manodevastato divyaḥ somo vibhurudīritaḥ // 224
8.d:
बाह्यदेवेष्वधिष्ठाता साम्यैश्वर्यसुखात्मकः ।
मनोदेवस्ततो दिव्यः सोमो विभुरुदीरितः ॥ 224
8.m: he is the presiding deity among the external gods, consisting of equanimity, sovereignty, and bliss. / Therefore the god of mind is said to be the divine, all-pervasive Soma. // 224

8.s:
tato'pi sakalākṣāṇāṃ yonerbuddhyakṣajanmanaḥ /
sthūlādicchagalāntāṣṭayuktaṃ cāhaṅkṛteḥ puram // 225
8.d:
ततोऽपि सकलाक्षाणां योनेर्बुद्ध्यक्षजन्मनः ।
स्थूलादिच्छगलान्ताष्टयुक्तं चाहङ्कृतेः पुरम् ॥ 225
8.m: Beyond that, the source of all the sense-organs, which gives birth to the senses of cognition, / is the city of ego, endowed with an octad beginning with Sthūla and ending with Chagala. // 225

8.s:
buddhitattvaṃ tato devayonyaṣṭakapurādhipam /
paiśācaprabhṛtibrāhmaparyantaṃ tacca kīrtitam // 226
8.d:
बुद्धितत्त्वं ततो देवयोन्यष्टकपुराधिपम् ।
पैशाचप्रभृतिब्राह्मपर्यन्तं तच्च कीर्तितम् ॥ 226
8.m: Then comes the principle of intellect, master of the cities of the eight classes of divine beings; / and that is proclaimed as beginning with the Paiśāca and extending up to the Brāhma. // 226

8.s:
etāni devayonīnāṃ sthānānyeva purāṇyataḥ /
avatīryātmajanmānaṃ dhyāyantaḥ saṃbhavanti te // 227
8.d:
एतानि देवयोनीनां स्थानान्येव पुराण्यतः ।
अवतीर्यात्मजन्मानं ध्यायन्तः संभवन्ति ते ॥ 227
8.m: These are indeed the abodes of the divine classes, for the cities; / having descended, meditating upon their own origin, they are born. // 227

8.s:
parameśaniyogācca codyamānāśca māyayā /
niyāmitā niyatyā ca brahmaṇo'vyaktajanmanaḥ // 228
8.d:
परमेशनियोगाच्च चोद्यमानाश्च मायया ।
नियामिता नियत्या च ब्रह्मणोऽव्यक्तजन्मनः ॥ 228
8.m: Impelled by the command of the Supreme Lord, spurred on by māyā, / and regulated by necessity (niyati), they [manifest] from Brahmā, whose birth is the unmanifest. // 228

8.s:
vyajyante tena sargādau nāmarūpairanekadhā /
svāṃśanaiva mahātmāno na tyajanti svaketanam // 229
8.d:
व्यज्यन्ते तेन सर्गादौ नामरूपैरनेकधा ।
स्वांशनैव महात्मानो न त्यजन्ति स्वकेतनम् ॥ 229
8.m: They are manifested by him at the beginning of creation in manifold ways through name and form; / yet the great-souled ones, through their own portion, do not abandon their own abode. // 229

8.s:
uktaṃ ca śivatanāvidamadhikārapadasthitena guruṇā naḥ /
aṣṭānāṃ devānāṃ śaktyāvirbhāvayonayo hyetāḥ // 230
8.d:
उक्तं च शिवतनाविदमधिकारपदस्थितेन गुरुणा नः ।
अष्टानां देवानां शक्त्याविर्भावयोनयो ह्येताः ॥ 230
8.m: And this has been stated in the Śivatanu by our guru, who is established in the station of authority: / 'These are indeed the birth-sources for the manifestation of the powers of the eight gods. // 230

8.s:
tanubhogāḥ punareṣāmadhaḥ prabhūtātmakāḥ proktāḥ /
catvāriṃśattulyopabhogadeśādhikāni bhuvanāni // 231
8.d:
तनुभोगाः पुनरेषामधः प्रभूतात्मकाः प्रोक्ताः ।
चत्वारिंशत्तुल्योपभोगदेशाधिकानि भुवनानि ॥ 231
8.m: Again, their bodily enjoyments, consisting of physical elements, are declared below. / There are forty worlds, along with additional areas of equal enjoyment; // 231

8.s:
sādhanabhedātkevalamaṣṭakapañcakatayoktāni /
etāni bhaktiyogaprāṇatyāgādigamyāni // 232
8.d:
साधनभेदात्केवलमष्टकपञ्चकतयोक्तानि ।
एतानि भक्तियोगप्राणत्यागादिगम्यानि ॥ 232
8.m: they are stated as a pentad of octads merely through the distinction of practices, / and these are attainable through devotion, yoga, abandonment of the vital breaths, and the like. // 232

8.s:
teṣūmāpatireva prabhuḥ svatantrendriyo vikaraṇātmā /
taratamayogena tato'pi devayonyaṣṭakaṃ lakṣyaṃ tu // 233
8.d:
तेषूमापतिरेव प्रभुः स्वतन्त्रेन्द्रियो विकरणात्मा ।
तरतमयोगेन ततोऽपि देवयोन्यष्टकं लक्ष्यं तु ॥ 233
8.m: Among them, Umāpati alone is the lord, whose sense-organs are autonomous, who is devoid of instruments. / And beyond that, through graded degrees, the octad of classes of gods is to be recognized, // 233

8.s:
lokānāmakṣāṇi ca viṣayaparicchittikaraṇāni /
gandhādermahadantādekādhikyena jātamaiśvaryam // 234
8.d:
लोकानामक्षाणि च विषयपरिच्छित्तिकरणानि ।
गन्धादेर्महदन्तादेकाधिक्येन जातमैश्वर्यम् ॥ 234
8.m: and the sense-organs of the beings, which are instruments for delimiting sense-objects. / The sovereignty born from odor and the rest up to the intellect increases by one degree each, // 234

8.s:
aṇimādyātmakamasminpaiśācādye viriñcānte /
jñātvaivaṃ śodhayedbuddhiṃ sārdhaṃ puryaṣṭakendriyaiḥ // 235
8.d:
अणिमाद्यात्मकमस्मिन्पैशाचाद्ये विरिञ्चान्ते ।
ज्ञात्वैवं शोधयेद्बुद्धिं सार्धं पुर्यष्टकेन्द्रियैः ॥ 235
8.m: consisting of powers such as atomicity, in this [series] beginning with the Paiśāca and ending with Viriñca. / Knowing thus, one should purify the intellect together with the senses of the subtle body (puryaṣṭaka).' // 235

8.s:
krodheśāṣṭakamānīlaṃ saṃvartādyaṃ tato viduḥ /
tejoṣṭakaṃ balādhyakṣaprabhṛtikrodhanāṣtakāt // 236
8.d:
क्रोधेशाष्टकमानीलं संवर्ताद्यं ततो विदुः ।
तेजोष्टकं बलाध्यक्षप्रभृतिक्रोधनाष्तकात् ॥ 236
8.m: Then, they know the bluish octad of Krodheśas, beginning with Saṃvarta, / and the fiery octad beginning with Balādhyakṣa, from the octad of Krodhanas. // 236

8.s:
akṛtādi tato buddhau yogāṣṭakamudāhṛtam /
svacchandaśāsane tattu mūle śrīpūrvaśāsane // 237
8.d:
अकृतादि ततो बुद्धौ योगाष्टकमुदाहृतम् ।
स्वच्छन्दशासने तत्तु मूले श्रीपूर्वशासने ॥ 237
8.m: Then, in the intellect, the octad of yoga beginning with Akṛta is declared. / That is stated in the teaching of the Svacchanda, but in the root venerable Pūrva-śāsana, // 237

8.s:
yogāṣṭakapade yattu some śraikaṇṭhameva ca /
tato māyāpuraṃ bhūyaḥ śrīkaṇṭhasya ca kathyate // 238
8.d:
योगाष्टकपदे यत्तु सोमे श्रैकण्ठमेव च ।
ततो मायापुरं भूयः श्रीकण्ठस्य च कथ्यते ॥ 238
8.m: in the station of the octad of yoga, there is [the city] belonging to Soma and Śrīkaṇṭha. / Then the city of Māyā and that of Śrīkaṇṭha are mentioned again. // 238

8.s:
tena dvitīyaṃ bhuvanaṃ tayoḥ pratyekamucyate /
tatra māyāpuraṃ devyā yayā viśvamadhiṣṭhitam // 239
8.d:
तेन द्वितीयं भुवनं तयोः प्रत्येकमुच्यते ।
तत्र मायापुरं देव्या यया विश्वमधिष्ठितम् ॥ 239
8.m: By this, a second realm is spoken of for each of the two. / There the city of Māyā belongs to the Goddess by whom the universe is presided over. // 239

8.s:
pratikalpaṃ nāmabhedairbhaṇyate sā maheśvarī /
umāpateḥ puraṃ paścānmātṛbhiḥ parivāritam // 240
8.d:
प्रतिकल्पं नामभेदैर्भण्यते सा महेश्वरी ।
उमापतेः पुरं पश्चान्मातृभिः परिवारितम् ॥ 240
8.m: In every aeon that Great Goddess is spoken of by various names. / Next is the city of Umāpati, surrounded by the Mothers. // 240

8.s:
śrīkaṇṭha eva parayā mūrtyomāpatirucyate /
brāhmyaiśī skandajā hārī vārāhyaindrī saviccikā [carcikā] // 241
8.d:
श्रीकण्ठ एव परया मूर्त्योमापतिरुच्यते ।
ब्राह्म्यैशी स्कन्दजा हारी वाराह्यैन्द्री सविच्चिका [चर्चिका] ॥ 241
8.m: It is Śrīkaṇṭha himself who is called Umāpati through his supreme form. / Brāhmī, Aiśī, Skandajā, Hārī, Vārāhī, Aindrī, together with Carcikā, // 241

8.s:
pītā śuklā pītanīle nīlā śuklāruṇā kramāt /
agnīśasaumyayāmyāpyapūrvanairṛtagāstu tāḥ // 242
8.d:
पीता शुक्ला पीतनीले नीला शुक्लारुणा क्रमात् ।
अग्नीशसौम्ययाम्याप्यपूर्वनैरृतगास्तु ताः ॥ 242
8.m: are, in order, yellow, white, yellow-and-black, black, white, and red; / and they are situated in the southeast, northeast, northwest, south, west, east, and southwest. // 242

8.s:
aṃśena mānuṣe loke dhātrā tā hyavatāritāḥ /
svacchandāstāḥ parāścānyāḥ pare vyomni vyavasthitāḥ // 243
8.d:
अंशेन मानुषे लोके धात्रा ता ह्यवतारिताः ।
स्वच्छन्दास्ताः पराश्चान्याः परे व्योम्नि व्यवस्थिताः ॥ 243
8.m: By a portion, they were brought down into the mortal world by the Creator; / but the transcendent Svacchandā goddesses and others are established in the supreme ether. // 243

8.s:
svacchandaṃ tā niṣevante saptadheyamumā yataḥ /
umāpatipurasyordhva sthitaṃ mūrtyaṣṭakaṃ param // 244
8.d:
स्वच्छन्दं ता निषेवन्ते सप्तधेयमुमा यतः ।
उमापतिपुरस्योर्ध्व स्थितं मूर्त्यष्टकं परम् ॥ 244
8.m: They attend upon Svacchanda, since this Umā is sevenfold. / Above the city of Umāpati is situated the supreme octad of cosmic forms, // 244

8.s:
śarvādikaṃ yasya sṛṣṭirdharādyā yājakāntataḥ /
tābhya īśānamūrtiryā sā merau saṃpratiṣṭhitā // 245
8.d:
शर्वादिकं यस्य सृष्टिर्धराद्या याजकान्ततः ।
ताभ्य ईशानमूर्तिर्या सा मेरौ संप्रतिष्ठिता ॥ 245
8.m: beginning with Śarva, whose creation extends from earth up to the sacrificer. / Among them, the cosmic form of Īśāna is established on Mount Meru, // 245

8.s:
śrīkaṇṭhaḥ sphaṭikādrau sā vyāptā tanvaṣṭakairjagat /
ye yogaṃ saguṇaṃ śambhoḥ saṃyatāḥ paryupāsate // 246
8.d:
श्रीकण्ठः स्फटिकाद्रौ सा व्याप्ता तन्वष्टकैर्जगत् ।
ये योगं सगुणं शम्भोः संयताः पर्युपासते ॥ 246
8.m: and Śrīkaṇṭha on the Crystal Mountain; she has pervaded the world with the eight cosmic forms. / Those who, self-controlled, worship the yoga of Śambhu with attributes, // 246

8.s:
tanmaṇḍalaṃ vā dṛṣṭvaiva muktadvaitā hṛtatrayāḥ /
guṇānāmādharauttaryācchuddhāśuddhatvasaṃsthiteḥ // 247
8.d:
तन्मण्डलं वा दृष्ट्वैव मुक्तद्वैता हृतत्रयाः ।
गुणानामाधरौत्तर्याच्छुद्धाशुद्धत्वसंस्थितेः ॥ 247
8.m: or who, freed from duality and relieved of the three [impurities], merely gaze upon that mandala— / owing to the lower and higher nature of the qualities and the status of purity and impurity, // 247

8.s:
tāratamyācca yogasya bhedātphalavicitratā /
tato bhogaphalāvāptibhedādbhedo'yamucyate // 248
8.d:
तारतम्याच्च योगस्य भेदात्फलविचित्रता ।
ततो भोगफलावाप्तिभेदाद्भेदोऽयमुच्यते ॥ 248
8.m: and owing to the graded hierarchy of yoga, there is a variety of results. / Therefore, this differentiation is explained on the basis of the different attainments of enjoyment and fruit. // 248

8.s:
mūrtyaṣṭakopariṣṭāttu suśivā dvādaśoditāḥ /
vāmādyekaśivāntāste kuṅkumābhāḥ sutejasaḥ // 249
8.d:
मूर्त्यष्टकोपरिष्टात्तु सुशिवा द्वादशोदिताः ।
वामाद्येकशिवान्तास्ते कुङ्कुमाभाः सुतेजसः ॥ 249
8.m: Above the octad of forms, however, twelve Suśivas are declared; / beginning with Vāma and ending with Ekaśiva, they have the luster of saffron and are full of brilliance. // 249

8.s:
tadūrdhva vīrabhadrākhyo maṇḍalādhipatiḥ sthitaḥ /
yatta [sta] tsāyujyamāpannaḥ sa tena saha modate // 250
8.d:
तदूर्ध्व वीरभद्राख्यो मण्डलाधिपतिः स्थितः ।
यत्त [स्त] त्सायुज्यमापन्नः स तेन सह मोदते ॥ 250
8.m: Above that is situated the lord of the mandala named Vīrabhadra; / having attained union with him, one rejoices with him.

8.s:
tato'pyaṅguṣṭhamātrāntaṃ mahādevāṣṭakaṃ bhavet /
buddhitattvamidaṃ proktaṃ devayonyaṣṭakāditaḥ // 251
8.d:
ततोऽप्यङ्गुष्ठमात्रान्तं महादेवाष्टकं भवेत् ।
बुद्धितत्त्वमिदं प्रोक्तं देवयोन्यष्टकादितः ॥ 251
8.m: Above that also, up to the measure of a thumb, is the group of eight Mahādevas. / This is taught as the principle of intellect (buddhitattva), beginning from the eight wombs of divine beings.

8.s:
mahādevāṣṭakānte tad yogāṣṭakamihoditam /
tatra śraikaṇṭhamuktaṃ yat tasyaivomāpatistathā // 252
8.d:
महादेवाष्टकान्ते तद् योगाष्टकमिहोदितम् ।
तत्र श्रैकण्ठमुक्तं यत् तस्यैवोमापतिस्तथा ॥ 252
8.m: At the end of the group of eight Mahādevas, the group of eight yogas is proclaimed here. / In that context, that which was spoken of as Śrīkaṇṭha is likewise the Lord of Umā (Umāpati).

8.s:
mūrtayaḥ suśivā vīro mahādevāṣṭakaṃ vapuḥ /
upariṣṭāddhiyo'dhaśca prakṛterguṇasaṃjñitam // 253
8.d:
मूर्तयः सुशिवा वीरो महादेवाष्टकं वपुः ।
उपरिष्टाद्धियोऽधश्च प्रकृतेर्गुणसंज्ञितम् ॥ 253
8.m: The forms, the Suśivas, the Vīra, the eightfold Mahādeva are [the intellect's] form. / Above the intellect and below Prakṛti is that known as the principle of the qualities (guṇatattva).

8.s:
tattvaṃ tatra tu saṃkṣubdhā guṇāḥ prasuvate dhiyam /
na vaiṣamyamanāpannaṃ kāraṇaṃ kāryasūtaye // 254
8.d:
तत्त्वं तत्र तु संक्षुब्धा गुणाः प्रसुवते धियम् ।
न वैषम्यमनापन्नं कारणं कार्यसूतये ॥ 254
8.m: There, the agitated qualities generate the intellect. / A cause that has not attained imbalance cannot produce an effect.

8.s:
guṇasāmyatmikā tena prakṛtiḥ kāraṇaṃ bhavet /
nanvevaṃ sāpi saṃkṣobhaṃ vinā tānviṣamānguṇān // 255
8.d:
गुणसाम्यत्मिका तेन प्रकृतिः कारणं भवेत् ।
नन्वेवं सापि संक्षोभं विना तान्विषमान्गुणान् ॥ 255
8.m: Therefore Prakṛti, consisting of the equilibrium of qualities, must be the cause. / [Objection:] Surely, even so, without agitation, how could it produce those imbalanced qualities?

8.s:
kathaṃ suvīta tatrādye kṣobhe syādanavasthitiḥ /
sāṃkhyasya doṣa evāyaṃ yadi vā tena te guṇāḥ // 256
8.d:
कथं सुवीत तत्राद्ये क्षोभे स्यादनवस्थितिः ।
सांख्यस्य दोष एवायं यदि वा तेन ते गुणाः ॥ 256
8.m: [If so,] an infinite regress would arise regarding the initial agitation. / [Reply:] This is only a fault for the Sāṃkhya; or rather, according to him, those qualities

8.s:
avyaktamiṣṭāḥ sāmyaṃ tu saṅgamātraṃ na cetarat /
asmākaṃ tu svatantreśatathecchākṣobhasaṃgatam // 257
8.d:
अव्यक्तमिष्टाः साम्यं तु सङ्गमात्रं न चेतरत् ।
अस्माकं तु स्वतन्त्रेशतथेच्छाक्षोभसंगतम् ॥ 257
8.m: are held to be the unmanifest (avyakta), while equilibrium is mere contact and nothing else. / For us, however, it is united with the agitation [caused by] the will of the autonomous Lord as it is.

8.s:
avyaktaṃ buddhitattvasya kāraṇaṃ kṣobhitā guṇāḥ /
nanu tattveśvarecchāto yaḥ kṣobhaḥ prakṛteḥ purā // 258
8.d:
अव्यक्तं बुद्धितत्त्वस्य कारणं क्षोभिता गुणाः ।
ननु तत्त्वेश्वरेच्छातो यः क्षोभः प्रकृतेः पुरा ॥ 258
8.m: The unmanifest is the cause of the intellect-principle, [namely,] the agitated qualities. / [Objection:] Surely, the agitation of Prakṛti that arises earlier from the will of the Lord of principles

8.s:
tadeva buddhitattvaṃ syāt kimanyaiḥ kalpitairguṇaiḥ /
naitatkāraṇatārūpaparāmarśāvarodhi yat // 259
8.d:
तदेव बुद्धितत्त्वं स्यात् किमन्यैः कल्पितैर्गुणैः ।
नैतत्कारणतारूपपरामर्शावरोधि यत् ॥ 259
8.m: must be the intellect-principle itself; what need is there for other postulated qualities? / [Reply:] This is not so, because another agitation, which prevents the apprehension of [merely] being a cause,

8.s:
kṣobhāntaraṃ tataḥ kārya bījocchūnāṅkurādivat /
kramāttamorajaḥsattve gurūṇāṃ paṅktayaḥ sthitāḥ // 260
8.d:
क्षोभान्तरं ततः कार्य बीजोच्छूनाङ्कुरादिवत् ।
क्रमात्तमोरजःसत्त्वे गुरूणां पङ्क्तयः स्थिताः ॥ 260
8.m: is the effect after that, just like the seed, the swollen [seed], and the sprout. / In succession, in tamas, rajas, and sattva, there are lines of gurus,

8.s:
tisro dvātriṃśadekātastriṃśadapyekaviṃśatiḥ /
svajñanayogabalataḥ krīḍanto daiśikottamāḥ // 261
8.d:
तिस्रो द्वात्रिंशदेकातस्त्रिंशदप्येकविंशतिः ।
स्वज्ञनयोगबलतः क्रीडन्तो दैशिकोत्तमाः ॥ 261
8.m: three [in number]: thirty-two, thirty-one, and also twenty-one, / eminent masters sporting through the power of their own knowledge and yoga.

8.s:
trinetrāḥ pāśanirmuktāste'trānugrahakāriṇaḥ /
buddheśca guṇaparyantamubhe saptādhike śate // 262
8.d:
त्रिनेत्राः पाशनिर्मुक्तास्तेऽत्रानुग्रहकारिणः ।
बुद्धेश्च गुणपर्यन्तमुभे सप्ताधिके शते ॥ 262
8.m: Three-eyed, freed from bonds, they bestow grace here. / From the intellect up to the qualities, both [the number of Rudras] and the worlds are one hundred and seven;

8.s:
rudrāṇāṃ bhuvanānāṃ ca mukhyato'nye tadantare /
yogāṣṭakaṃ guṇaskandhe proktaṃ śivatanau punaḥ // 263
8.d:
रुद्राणां भुवनानां च मुख्यतोऽन्ये तदन्तरे ।
योगाष्टकं गुणस्कन्धे प्रोक्तं शिवतनौ पुनः ॥ 263
8.m: these are the principal [worlds] of the Rudras, and others are within them. / The group of eight yogas is taught in the shoulder of qualities (guṇaskandha), whereas in the body of Śiva,

8.s:
yonīratītya gauṇe skandhe syuryogadātāraḥ /
akṛtakṛtavibhuviriñcā harirguhaḥ kramavaśāttato devī // 264
8.d:
योनीरतीत्य गौणे स्कन्धे स्युर्योगदातारः ।
अकृतकृतविभुविरिञ्चा हरिर्गुहः क्रमवशात्ततो देवी ॥ 264
8.m: transcending the wombs, in the qualitative shoulder, there are the bestowal-granters of yoga: / Akṛta, Kṛta, Vibhu, Viriñca, Hari, Guha, and then in due order the Goddess.

8.s:
karaṇānyaṇimādiguṇāḥ kāryāṇi pratyayaprapañcaśca /
avyaktādutpannā guṇāśca sattvādayo'mīṣām // 265
8.d:
करणान्यणिमादिगुणाः कार्याणि प्रत्ययप्रपञ्चश्च ।
अव्यक्तादुत्पन्ना गुणाश्च सत्त्वादयोऽमीषाम् ॥ 265
8.m: The instruments, the qualities such as lightness (aṇimā), the effects, the expansion of cognitive states, / and the qualities such as sattva arisen from the unmanifest—for all these,

8.s:
dharmajñānavirāgānaiśvaryaṃ tatphalāni vividhāni /
yacchanti guṇebhyo'mī puruṣebhyo yogadātāraḥ // 266
8.d:
धर्मज्ञानविरागानैश्वर्यं तत्फलानि विविधानि ।
यच्छन्ति गुणेभ्योऽमी पुरुषेभ्यो योगदातारः ॥ 266
8.m: virtue, knowledge, dispassion, sovereignty, and their diverse fruits / are bestowed from the qualities upon the puruṣas by these bestowers of yoga.

8.s:
tebhyaḥ parato bhuvanaṃ sattvādiguṇāsanasya devasya /
sakalajagadekamāturbhartuḥ śrīkaṇṭhanāthasya // 267
8.d:
तेभ्यः परतो भुवनं सत्त्वादिगुणासनस्य देवस्य ।
सकलजगदेकमातुर्भर्तुः श्रीकण्ठनाथस्य ॥ 267
8.m: Beyond them is the world of the God whose seat is the qualities such as sattva, / the lord of the sole mother of all universe, the venerable lord Śrīkaṇṭha,

8.s:
yenomāguhanīlabrahmaṛbhukṣakṛtākṛtādibhuvaneṣu /
graharūpiṇyā śaktyā prābhvyādhiṣṭhāni bhūtāni // 268
8.d:
येनोमागुहनीलब्रह्मऋभुक्षकृताकृतादिभुवनेषु ।
ग्रहरूपिण्या शक्त्या प्राभ्व्याधिष्ठानि भूतानि ॥ 268
8.m: by whom, in the worlds of Umā, Guha, Nīla, Brahmā, Indra, Kṛtākṛta, and the rest, / through his power in the form of the planets, beings are presided over with preeminent majesty;

8.s:
upasaṃjihīrṣuriha yaścaturānanapaṅkajaṃ samāviśya /
dagdhvā caturo lokāñjanalokānnirmiṇoti punaḥ // 269
8.d:
उपसंजिहीर्षुरिह यश्चतुराननपङ्कजं समाविश्य ।
दग्ध्वा चतुरो लोकाञ्जनलोकान्निर्मिणोति पुनः ॥ 269
8.m: who here, wishing to dissolve [the universe], enters the lotus of the four-faced [Brahmā], / and having burnt the four worlds, creates them again from the Janaloka;

8.s:
yasyecchātaḥ sattvādiguṇaśarīrā visṛjati rudrāṇī /
anukalpo rudrāṇyā vedī tatrejyate'nukalpena // 270
8.d:
यस्येच्छातः सत्त्वादिगुणशरीरा विसृजति रुद्राणी ।
अनुकल्पो रुद्राण्या वेदी तत्रेज्यतेऽनुकल्पेन ॥ 270
8.m: by whose will Rudrāṇī, having a body of the qualities such as sattva, creates. / The secondary ritual (anukalpa) belongs to Rudrāṇī; the altar is worshipped there by means of the secondary ritual.

8.s:
paśupatirindropendraviriñcairatha tadupalambhato devaiḥ /
gandharvayakṣarākṣasapitṛmunibhiścitritāstathā yāgāḥ // 271
8.d:
पशुपतिरिन्द्रोपेन्द्रविरिञ्चैरथ तदुपलम्भतो देवैः ।
गन्धर्वयक्षराक्षसपितृमुनिभिश्चित्रितास्तथा यागाः ॥ 271
8.m: The sacrifices are made manifold by Paśupati, Indra, Upendra, Viriñci, and then, through obtaining that, by the gods, / Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, ancestors, and sages.

8.s:
guṇānāṃ yatparaṃ sāmyaṃ tadavyaktaṃ guṇordhvataḥ /
krodheśacaṇḍasaṃvartā jyotiḥpiṅgalasūrakau // 272
8.d:
गुणानां यत्परं साम्यं तदव्यक्तं गुणोर्ध्वतः ।
क्रोधेशचण्डसंवर्ता ज्योतिःपिङ्गलसूरकौ ॥ 272
8.m: The supreme equilibrium of the qualities is the unmanifest (avyakta), above the qualities. / Krodheśa, Caṇḍa, Saṃvarta, Jyotiḥ, Piṅgala, Sūraka,

8.s:
pañcāntakaikavīrau ca śikhodaścāṣṭa tatra te /
gahanaṃ puruṣanidhānaṃ prakṛtirmūlaṃ pradhānamavyaktam // 273
8.d:
पञ्चान्तकैकवीरौ च शिखोदश्चाष्ट तत्र ते ।
गहनं पुरुषनिधानं प्रकृतिर्मूलं प्रधानमव्यक्तम् ॥ 273
8.m: Pañcāntaka, Ekavīra, and Śikhoda—these are the eight there. / Gahana ('abyss'), Puruṣanidhāna ('resting-place of the puruṣa'), Prakṛti, Mūla ('root'), Pradhāna, Avyakta ('unmanifest'),

8.s:
guṇakāraṇamityete māyāprabhavasya paryāyāḥ /
yāvantaḥ kṣetrajñāḥ sahajāgantukamalopadigdhacitaḥ // 274
8.d:
गुणकारणमित्येते मायाप्रभवस्य पर्यायाः ।
यावन्तः क्षेत्रज्ञाः सहजागन्तुकमलोपदिग्धचितः ॥ 274
8.m: and Guṇakāraṇa ('cause of qualities')—these are synonyms for what arises from Māyā. / As many knowers of the field (kṣetrajña) as there are whose consciousness is smeared with innate and adventitious impurities,

8.s:
te sarve'tra vinihitā rudrāśca tadutthabhogabhujaḥ /
mūḍhavivṛttavilīnaiḥ karaṇaiḥ kecittu vikaraṇakāḥ // 275
8.d:
ते सर्वेऽत्र विनिहिता रुद्राश्च तदुत्थभोगभुजः ।
मूढविवृत्तविलीनैः करणैः केचित्तु विकरणकाः ॥ 275
8.m: they are all placed here, along with the Rudras who experience the enjoyments arising therefrom. / Some possess deluded, outward-turned, or dissolved instruments, while others are entirely instrumentless (vikaraṇa).

8.s:
akṛtādhiṣṭhānatayā kṛtyāśaktāni mūḍhāni /
pratiniyataviṣayabhāñji sphuṭāni śāstre vivṛttāni // 276
8.d:
अकृताधिष्ठानतया कृत्याशक्तानि मूढानि ।
प्रतिनियतविषयभाञ्जि स्फुटानि शास्त्रे विवृत्तानि ॥ 276
8.m: Because they have not formed an abode, they are incapable of activity: [such instruments are] deluded. / Those that relate to determinate objects are clearly distinguished in the scripture as outward-turned.

8.s:
bhagnāni mahāpralaye sṛṣṭau notpāditāni līnāni /
icchādhīnāni punarvikaraṇasaṃjñāni kāryamapyevam // 277
8.d:
भग्नानि महाप्रलये सृष्टौ नोत्पादितानि लीनानि ।
इच्छाधीनानि पुनर्विकरणसंज्ञानि कार्यमप्येवम् ॥ 277
8.m: Broken in the great dissolution and not brought forth in creation, they are dissolved. / Again, those dependent on the will are called instrumentless; the effect is likewise.

8.s:
puṃstattve tuṣṭinavakaṃ siddhayo'ṣṭau ca tatpuraḥ /
tāvatya evāṇimādibhuvanāṣṭakameva ca // 278
8.d:
पुंस्तत्त्वे तुष्टिनवकं सिद्धयोऽष्टौ च तत्पुरः ।
तावत्य एवाणिमादिभुवनाष्टकमेव च ॥ 278
8.m: In the puruṣa-principle there is the group of nine contentments (tuṣṭi) and eight spiritual accomplishments (siddhi) before it; / there are just as many [worlds], and also the group of eight worlds of aṇimā and the rest.

8.s:
atattve tattvabuddhyā yaḥ santoṣastuṣṭiratra sā /
heye'pyādeyadhīḥ siddhiḥ tathā coktaṃ hi kāpilaiḥ // 279
8.d:
अतत्त्वे तत्त्वबुद्ध्या यः सन्तोषस्तुष्टिरत्र सा ।
हेयेऽप्यादेयधीः सिद्धिः तथा चोक्तं हि कापिलैः ॥ 279
8.m: Satisfaction with the notion that what is non-reality is reality is 'contentment' (tuṣṭi) here; / the notion that what should be abandoned is to be adopted is 'accomplishment' (siddhi); for it is said thus by the followers of Kapila:

8.s:
ādhyātmikāścatasraḥ prakṛtyupādānakālabhāgyākhyāḥ /
pañca viṣayoparamato'rjanarakṣāsaṅgasaṃkṣayavighātaiḥ // 280
8.d:
आध्यात्मिकाश्चतस्रः प्रकृत्युपादानकालभाग्याख्याः ।
पञ्च विषयोपरमतोऽर्जनरक्षासङ्गसंक्षयविघातैः ॥ 280
8.m: 'Four are internal, named nature, means, time, and fortune; / five are from cessation regarding objects, through the afflictions of acquisition, preservation, attachment, decay, and injury.

8.s:
ūhaḥ śabdo'dhyayanaṃ duḥkhavighātāstrayaḥ suhṛtprāptiḥ /
dānaṃ ca siddhayo'ṣṭau siddheḥ pūrvo'ṅkuśastrividhaḥ // 281
8.d:
ऊहः शब्दोऽध्ययनं दुःखविघातास्त्रयः सुहृत्प्राप्तिः ।
दानं च सिद्धयोऽष्टौ सिद्धेः पूर्वोऽङ्कुशस्त्रिविधः ॥ 281
8.m: Reasoning, oral instruction, study, the three suppressions of suffering, acquisition of friends, / and gifting are the eight accomplishments; the threefold previous [set] is the curb on accomplishment.'

8.s:
aṇimādyūrdhvatastisraḥ paṅktayo guruśiṣyagāḥ /
tatrāpi triguṇacchāyāyogāt tritvamudāhṛtam // 282
8.d:
अणिमाद्यूर्ध्वतस्तिस्रः पङ्क्तयो गुरुशिष्यगाः ।
तत्रापि त्रिगुणच्छायायोगात् त्रित्वमुदाहृतम् ॥ 282
8.m: Above the worlds of aṇimā and the rest are three lines comprising gurus and disciples; / there too, because of the combination of the reflection of the three qualities, a triad is declared.

8.s:
nāḍīvidyāṣṭakaṃ cordhvaṃ paṅktīnāṃ syādiḍādikam /
puṃsi nādamayī śaktiḥ prasarākhyā ca yatsthitā // 283
8.d:
नाडीविद्याष्टकं चोर्ध्वं पङ्क्तीनां स्यादिडादिकम् ।
पुंसि नादमयी शक्तिः प्रसराख्या च यत्स्थिता ॥ 283
8.m: Above the lines is the group of eight sciences of subtle channels (nāḍīvidyāṣṭaka), beginning with Iḍā; / because the power consisting of sound (nāda) and named expansion resides in the puruṣa.

8.s:
na hyakartā pumānkartuḥ kāraṇatvaṃ ca saṃsthitam /
akartaryapi vā puṃsi sahakāritayā sthite // 284
8.d:
न ह्यकर्ता पुमान्कर्तुः कारणत्वं च संस्थितम् ।
अकर्तर्यपि वा पुंसि सहकारितया स्थिते ॥ 284
8.m: For the puruṣa is not a non-agent, and the causality of the agent is established; / or, even if the puruṣa is a non-agent, since he stands as an auxiliary,

8.s:
śeṣakāryātmataiṣṭavyānyathā satkāryahānitaḥ /
tasmāttathāvidhe kārye yā śaktiḥ puruṣasya sā // 285
8.d:
शेषकार्यात्मतैष्टव्यान्यथा सत्कार्यहानितः ।
तस्मात्तथाविधे कार्ये या शक्तिः पुरुषस्य सा ॥ 285
8.m: the nature of the remaining effect must be accepted [to be in him], otherwise the doctrine of the pre-existent effect (satkārya) would be ruined. / Therefore, with respect to such an effect, that power of the puruṣa,

8.s:
tāvanti rūpāṇyādāya pūrṇatāmadhigacchati /
nāḍyaṣṭakordhve kathitaṃ vigrahāṣṭakamucyate // 286
8.d:
तावन्ति रूपाण्यादाय पूर्णतामधिगच्छति ।
नाड्यष्टकोर्ध्वे कथितं विग्रहाष्टकमुच्यते ॥ 286
8.m: taking on so many forms, attains completeness. / Above the eight subtle channels is declared what is called the group of eight bodily forms (vigrahāṣṭaka).

8.s:
kāryaṃ heturduḥkhaṃ sukhaṃ ca vijñānasādhyakaraṇāni /
sādhanamiti vigrahatāyugaṣṭakaṃ bhavati puṃstattve // 287
8.d:
कार्यं हेतुर्दुःखं सुखं च विज्ञानसाध्यकरणानि ।
साधनमिति विग्रहतायुगष्टकं भवति पुंस्तत्त्वे ॥ 287
8.m: Effect, cause, pain, pleasure, and the cognitive instruments that bring about knowledge, / and the means—thus there is an eightfold pair of bodily forms in the puruṣa-principle.

8.s:
bhuvanaṃ dehadharmāṇāṃ daśānāṃ vigrahāṣṭakāt /
ahiṃsā satyamasteyaṃ brahmākalkākrudho guroḥ // 288
8.d:
भुवनं देहधर्माणां दशानां विग्रहाष्टकात् ।
अहिंसा सत्यमस्तेयं ब्रह्माकल्काक्रुधो गुरोः ॥ 288
8.m: From the eight bodily forms arises the world of the ten bodily duties: / non-violence, truth, non-stealing, celibacy, guilelessness, freedom from anger, service to the guru,

8.s:
śuśrūṣāśaucasantoṣā ṛjuteti daśoditāḥ /
puṃstattva eva gandhāntaṃ sthitaṃ ṣoḍaśakaṃ punaḥ // 289
8.d:
शुश्रूषाशौचसन्तोषा ऋजुतेति दशोदिताः ।
पुंस्तत्त्व एव गन्धान्तं स्थितं षोडशकं पुनः ॥ 289
8.m: purity, contentment, and uprightness—these are taught as the ten. / In the puruṣa-principle itself, there is situated the group of sixteen ending with smell;

8.s:
ārabhya dehapāśākhyaṃ puraṃ buddhiguṇāstataḥ /
tatraivāṣṭāvahaṃkārastridhā kāmādikāstathā // 290
8.d:
आरभ्य देहपाशाख्यं पुरं बुद्धिगुणास्ततः ।
तत्रैवाष्टावहंकारस्त्रिधा कामादिकास्तथा ॥ 290
8.m: beginning with the city named the bond of the body, then the qualities of the intellect, / there too eight [dispositions], egoity of three kinds, and likewise passion and the rest.

8.s:
pāśā āgantukagāṇeśavaidyeśvarabheditāḥ /
trividhāste sthitāḥ puṃsi mokṣamārgoparodhakāḥ // 291
8.d:
पाशा आगन्तुकगाणेशवैद्येश्वरभेदिताः ।
त्रिविधास्ते स्थिताः पुंसि मोक्षमार्गोपरोधकाः ॥ 291
8.m: The bonds are divided into adventitious, pertaining to Gaṇeśa, and pertaining to Vaidyeśvara; / standing in three ways within the puruṣa, they block the path to liberation.

8.s:
yatkiṃcitparamādvaitasaṃvitsvātantryasundarāt /
parācchivāduktarūpādanyattatpāśa ucyate // 292
8.d:
यत्किंचित्परमाद्वैतसंवित्स्वातन्त्र्यसुन्दरात् ।
पराच्छिवादुक्तरूपादन्यत्तत्पाश उच्यते ॥ 292
8.m: Whatever is other than the supreme Śiva described as having that nature, / beautiful through the absolute autonomy of supreme non-dual consciousness, is called a bond.

8.s:
tadevaṃ puṃstvamāpanne pūrṇe'pi parameśvare /
tatsvarūpāparijñānaṃ citraṃ hi puruṣāstataḥ // 293
8.d:
तदेवं पुंस्त्वमापन्ने पूर्णेऽपि परमेश्वरे ।
तत्स्वरूपापरिज्ञानं चित्रं हि पुरुषास्ततः ॥ 293
8.m: Thus, even though the Supreme Lord is full, when He attains the status of puruṣa, / there is non-recognition of His own true nature; wondrous indeed are the puruṣas thenceforward!

8.s:
uktānuktāstu ye pāśāḥ paratantroktalakṣaṇāḥ /
te puṃsi sarve tāṃstatra śodhayanmucyate bhavāt // 294
8.d:
उक्तानुक्तास्तु ये पाशाः परतन्त्रोक्तलक्षणाः ।
ते पुंसि सर्वे तांस्तत्र शोधयन्मुच्यते भवात् ॥ 294
8.m: The bonds—both stated and unstated—whose characteristics are taught in other tantras, / are all present in the puruṣa; by purifying them there, one is freed from worldly existence.

8.s:
puṃsa ūrdhva tu niyatistatrasthāḥ śaṃkarā daśa /
hemābhāḥ susitāḥ kālatattve tu daśa te śivāḥ // 295
8.d:
पुंस ऊर्ध्व तु नियतिस्तत्रस्थाः शंकरा दश ।
हेमाभाः सुसिताः कालतत्त्वे तु दश ते शिवाः ॥ 295
8.m: Above the puruṣa, however, is niyati; situated there are ten Śaṅkaras / with golden luster, whereas in the tattva of kāla there are ten extremely white Śivas.

8.s:
koṭiḥ ṣoḍaśasāhasraṃ pratyekaṃ parivāriṇaḥ /
rāge vīreśabhuvanaṃ gurvantevāsināṃ puram // 296
8.d:
कोटिः षोडशसाहस्रं प्रत्येकं परिवारिणः ।
रागे वीरेशभुवनं गुर्वन्तेवासिनां पुरम् ॥ 296
8.m: Each of them has an entourage of one crore sixteen thousand. / In rāga is the world of Vīreśa, the city of gurus and their disciples.

8.s:
puraṃ cāśuddhavidyāyāṃ syācchaktinavakojjvalam /
manonmanyantagāstāśca vāmādyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ // 297
8.d:
पुरं चाशुद्धविद्यायां स्याच्छक्तिनवकोज्ज्वलम् ।
मनोन्मन्यन्तगास्ताश्च वामाद्याः परिकीर्तिताः ॥ 297
8.m: In aśuddhavidyā there is a city blazing with nine powers; / they are proclaimed to be Vāmā and the others, ending with Manonmanī.

8.s:
kalāyāṃ syānmahādevatrayasya puramuttamam /
tato māyā tripuṭikā mukhyato'nantakoṭibhiḥ // 298
8.d:
कलायां स्यान्महादेवत्रयस्य पुरमुत्तमम् ।
ततो माया त्रिपुटिका मुख्यतोऽनन्तकोटिभिः ॥ 298
8.m: In kalā is the supreme city of the three Mahādevas. / Beyond that is māyā, consisting of three folds, primarily with endless crores [of worlds],

8.s:
ākrāntā sā bhagabilaiḥ proktaṃ śaivyāṃ tanau punaḥ /
aṅguṣṭhamātraparyantaṃ mahādevāṣṭakaṃ niśi // 299
8.d:
आक्रान्ता सा भगबिलैः प्रोक्तं शैव्यां तनौ पुनः ।
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रपर्यन्तं महादेवाष्टकं निशि ॥ 299
8.m: pervaded by the apertures of the womb (bhagabila). In the Śaiva body, moreover, / an octad of Mahādevas reaching only up to the measure of a thumb is taught in the Night (niśi).

8.s:
cakrāṣṭakādhipatyena tathā śrīmālinīmate /
vāmādyāḥ puruṣādau ye proktāḥ śrīpūrvaśāsane // 300
8.d:
चक्राष्टकाधिपत्येन तथा श्रीमालिनीमते ।
वामाद्याः पुरुषादौ ये प्रोक्ताः श्रीपूर्वशासने ॥ 300
8.m: Likewise, in the venerable Mālinīmata, through lordship over an octad of cakras, / the powers beginning with Vāmā that were taught in the revered Pūrvaśāsana at the level of puruṣa and the rest,

8.s:
te māyātattva evoktāstanau śaivyāmanantataḥ /
kapālavratinaḥ svāṅgahotāraḥ kaṣṭatāpasāḥ // 301
8.d:
ते मायातत्त्व एवोक्तास्तनौ शैव्यामनन्ततः ।
कपालव्रतिनः स्वाङ्गहोतारः कष्टतापसाः ॥ 301
8.m: are declared to be in the māyātattva itself. In the Śaiva body, starting from Ananta, / the Kapālavratins, those who offer their own limbs, austere ascetics,

8.s:
sarvābhayāḥ khaḍgadhārāvratāstattattvavedinaḥ /
kramāttattattvamāyānti yatreśo'nanta ucyate // 302
8.d:
सर्वाभयाः खड्गधाराव्रतास्तत्तत्त्ववेदिनः ।
क्रमात्तत्तत्त्वमायान्ति यत्रेशोऽनन्त उच्यते ॥ 302
8.m: those devoid of fear, those observing the razor's edge vow, and those who know their respective realities, / gradually reach those respective tattvas where Ananta is said to be the lord.

8.s:
uktaṃ ca tasya parataḥ sthānamanantādhipasya devasya /
sthitivilayasargakarturguhābhagadvārapālasya // 303
8.d:
उक्तं च तस्य परतः स्थानमनन्ताधिपस्य देवस्य ।
स्थितिविलयसर्गकर्तुर्गुहाभगद्वारपालस्य ॥ 303
8.m: And it is declared that beyond him is the abode of the god who is the lord of Ananta, / the agent of maintenance, dissolution, and emission, the guardian of the door to the womb of the cave (guhā).

8.s:
dharmānaṇimādiguṇāñjñānāni tapaḥsukhāni yogāṃśca /
māyābilātpradatte puṃsāṃ niṣkṛṣya niṣkṛṣya // 304
8.d:
धर्मानणिमादिगुणाञ्ज्ञानानि तपःसुखानि योगांश्च ।
मायाबिलात्प्रदत्ते पुंसां निष्कृष्य निष्कृष्य ॥ 304
8.m: He bestows upon bound souls righteousness, qualities such as anima, kinds of knowledge, / the joys of austerity, and yogas, extracting them one by one from the chasm of māyā.

8.s:
tacchaktīddhasvabalā guhādhikārāndhakāraguṇadīpāḥ /
sarve'nantapramukhā dīpyante śatabhavapramukhāntāḥ // 305
8.d:
तच्छक्तीद्धस्वबला गुहाधिकारान्धकारगुणदीपाः ।
सर्वेऽनन्तप्रमुखा दीप्यन्ते शतभवप्रमुखान्ताः ॥ 305
8.m: With their own power ignited by his power, like lamps to the darkness of cosmic office in the cave, / all [the lords] headed by Ananta down to those headed by Śatabhava blaze forth.

8.s:
so'vyaktamadhiṣṭhāya prakaroti jaganniyogataḥ śambhoḥ /
śuddhāśuddhasroto'dhikārahetuḥ śivo yasmāt // 306
8.d:
सोऽव्यक्तमधिष्ठाय प्रकरोति जगन्नियोगतः शम्भोः ।
शुद्धाशुद्धस्रोतोऽधिकारहेतुः शिवो यस्मात् ॥ 306
8.m: Presiding over the unmanifest (avyakta), he creates the universe by the command of Śambhu, / because Śiva is the cause of cosmic office over both the pure and impure streams.

8.s:
śivaguṇayoge tasmin mahati pade ye pratiṣṭhitāḥ prathamam /
te'nantāderjagataḥ sargasthitivilayakartāraḥ // 307
8.d:
शिवगुणयोगे तस्मिन् महति पदे ये प्रतिष्ठिताः प्रथमम् ।
तेऽनन्तादेर्जगतः सर्गस्थितिविलयकर्तारः ॥ 307
8.m: Those who were established in the beginning in that great state endowed with the qualities of Śiva / are the agents of emission, maintenance, and dissolution of the universe, beginning with Ananta.

8.s:
māyābilamidamuktaṃ paratastu guhā jagadyoniḥ /
utpattyā teṣvasyāḥ patiśaktikṣobhamanuvidhīyamāneṣu // 308
8.d:
मायाबिलमिदमुक्तं परतस्तु गुहा जगद्योनिः ।
उत्पत्त्या तेष्वस्याः पतिशक्तिक्षोभमनुविधीयमानेषु ॥ 308
8.m: This has been described as the chasm of māyā; beyond it, however, is the cave (guhā), the womb of the universe. / By their arising in these [cavities], when they submit to the stirring of the Lord's power,

8.s:
yonivivareṣu nānākāmasamṛddheṣu bhagasaṃjñā /
kāmayate patirenāmicchānuvidhāyinīṃ yadā devīm // 309
8.d:
योनिविवरेषु नानाकामसमृद्धेषु भगसंज्ञा ।
कामयते पतिरेनामिच्छानुविधायिनीं यदा देवीम् ॥ 309
8.m: the term 'bhaga' applies to the apertures of the womb abundant with various desires. / When the Lord desires this goddess who conforms to his will,

8.s:
pratibhagamavyaktādyāḥ prajāstadāsyāḥ prajāyante /
teṣāmatisūkṣmāṇāmetāvattvaṃ na varṇyate vidhiṣu // 310
8.d:
प्रतिभगमव्यक्ताद्याः प्रजास्तदास्याः प्रजायन्ते ।
तेषामतिसूक्ष्माणामेतावत्त्वं न वर्ण्यते विधिषु ॥ 310
8.m: then in every womb are born her progeny, beginning with the unmanifest. / Because they are exceedingly subtle, their precise measure is not described in the rules.

8.s:
avavarakāṇyekasminyadvatsāle bahūni baddhāni /
yonibilānyekasmiṃstadvanmāyāśiraḥsāle // 311
8.d:
अववरकाण्येकस्मिन्यद्वत्साले बहूनि बद्धानि ।
योनिबिलान्येकस्मिंस्तद्वन्मायाशिरःसाले ॥ 311
8.m: Just as many inner chambers are constructed within a single surrounding wall, / so are the apertures of the womb within the single wall at the summit of māyā.

8.s:
māyāpaṭalaiḥ sūkṣmaiḥ kuḍyaiḥ pihitāḥ parasparamadṛśyāḥ /
nivasanti tatra rudrāḥ sukhinaḥ pratibilamasaṃkhyātāḥ // 312
8.d:
मायापटलैः सूक्ष्मैः कुड्यैः पिहिताः परस्परमदृश्याः ।
निवसन्ति तत्र रुद्राः सुखिनः प्रतिबिलमसंख्याताः ॥ 312
8.m: Concealed by subtle veils of māyā as walls, invisible to one another, / innumerably happy Rudras reside there in each aperture.

8.s:
sthāne sāyujyagatāḥ sāmīpyagatāḥ pare salokasthāḥ /
pratibhuvanamevamayaṃ nivāsināṃ gurubhiruddiṣṭaḥ // 313
8.d:
स्थाने सायुज्यगताः सामीप्यगताः परे सलोकस्थाः ।
प्रतिभुवनमेवमयं निवासिनां गुरुभिरुद्दिष्टः ॥ 313
8.m: Some have attained union with the abode, some proximity, and others dwell in the same realm; / this has been taught by the gurus for the inhabitants in each world.

8.s:
api sarvasiddhavācaḥ kṣīyerandīrghakālamudgīrṇāḥ /
na punaryonyānantyāducyante srotasāṃ saṃkhyāḥ // 314
8.d:
अपि सर्वसिद्धवाचः क्षीयेरन्दीर्घकालमुद्गीर्णाः ।
न पुनर्योन्यानन्त्यादुच्यन्ते स्रोतसां संख्याः ॥ 314
8.m: Even the words of all the Siddhas uttered over an immense time would be exhausted, / yet the numbers of streams would still not be told, due to the endlessness of the wombs.

8.s:
tasmānnirayādyekaṃ yatproktaṃ dvārapālaparyantam /
srotastenānyānyapi tulyavidhānāni vedyāni // 315
8.d:
तस्मान्निरयाद्येकं यत्प्रोक्तं द्वारपालपर्यन्तम् ।
स्रोतस्तेनान्यान्यपि तुल्यविधानानि वेद्यानि ॥ 315
8.m: Therefore, through that single stream that has been described, extending from hell up to the gatekeeper, / the other streams should also be known to possess similar arrangements.

8.s:
avyaktakale guhayā prakṛtikalābhyāṃ vikāra ātmīyaḥ /
otaḥ proto vyāptaḥ kalitaḥ pūrṇaḥ parikṣiptaḥ // 316
8.d:
अव्यक्तकले गुहया प्रकृतिकलाभ्यां विकार आत्मीयः ।
ओतः प्रोतो व्याप्तः कलितः पूर्णः परिक्षिप्तः ॥ 316
8.m: In avyakta and kalā, through the cave and by means of prakṛti and kalā, its own transformation / is woven warp and woof, pervaded, configured, completed, and encompassed.

8.s:
madhye puṭatrayaṃ tasyā rudrāḥ ṣaḍadhare'ntare /
eka ūrdhve ca pañceti dvādaśaite nirūpitāḥ // 317
8.d:
मध्ये पुटत्रयं तस्या रुद्राः षडधरेऽन्तरे ।
एक ऊर्ध्वे च पञ्चेति द्वादशैते निरूपिताः ॥ 317
8.m: In the middle of it is a triad of folds: six Rudras below, in the interior / one, and five above; thus these twelve have been set forth:

8.s:
gahanāsādhyau hariharadaśeśvarau trikalagopatī ṣaḍime /
madhye'nantaḥ kṣemo dvijeśavidyeśaviśvaśivāḥ // 318
8.d:
गहनासाध्यौ हरिहरदशेश्वरौ त्रिकलगोपती षडिमे ।
मध्येऽनन्तः क्षेमो द्विजेशविद्येशविश्वशिवाः ॥ 318
8.m: Gahana, Asādhya, Hari, Hara, Daśeśvara, and Trikalagopati—these are the six [below]; / in the center is Ananta; Kṣema, Dvijīśa, Vidyeśa, and Viśvaśiva

8.s:
iti pañca teṣu pañcasu ṣaṭsu ca puṭageṣu tatparāvṛttyā /
parivarttate sthitiḥ kila devo'nantastu sarvathā madhye // 319
8.d:
इति पञ्च तेषु पञ्चसु षट्सु च पुटगेषु तत्परावृत्त्या ।
परिवर्त्तते स्थितिः किल देवोऽनन्तस्तु सर्वथा मध्ये ॥ 319
8.m: are the five. Through their rotation in those five and six folds, / their stability is said to alternate, while Lord Ananta remains entirely in the center.

8.s:
ūrdhvādharagakapālakapuṭaṣaṭkayugena tatparāvṛttyā /
madhyato'ṣṭābhirdiksthairvyāpto granthirmataṅgaśāstroktaḥ // 320
8.d:
ऊर्ध्वाधरगकपालकपुटषट्कयुगेन तत्परावृत्त्या ।
मध्यतोऽष्टाभिर्दिक्स्थैर्व्याप्तो ग्रन्थिर्मतङ्गशास्त्रोक्तः ॥ 320
8.m: Encompassed by the pair of sixfold skull-bowls above and below through their alternation, / and in the middle by eight located in the directions, is the knot (granthi) taught in the Mataṅgaśāstra.

8.s:
śrīsāraśāsane punareṣā ṣaṭpuṭatayā vinirdiṣṭā /
granthyākhyamidaṃ tattvaṃ māyākāryaṃ tato māyā // 321
8.d:
श्रीसारशासने पुनरेषा षट्पुटतया विनिर्दिष्टा ।
ग्रन्थ्याख्यमिदं तत्त्वं मायाकार्यं ततो माया ॥ 321
8.m: In the venerable Sāraśāsana, however, this is taught as having six folds. / This tattva known as the knot is the effect of māyā, and beyond it is māyā.

8.s:
māyātattvaṃ vibhu kila gahanamarūpaṃ samastavilayapadam /
tatra na bhuvanavibhāgo yukto granthāvasau tasmāt // 322
8.d:
मायातत्त्वं विभु किल गहनमरूपं समस्तविलयपदम् ।
तत्र न भुवनविभागो युक्तो ग्रन्थावसौ तस्मात् ॥ 322
8.m: The māyātattva is indeed all-pervading, fathomless, formless, the place of total dissolution; / a division into worlds is not appropriate there, hence it is placed in the knot.

8.s:
māyātattvādhipatiḥ so'nantaḥ samuditānvicāryāṇūn /
yugapatkṣobhayati niśāṃ sā sūte saṃpuṭairanantaiḥ svaiḥ // 323
8.d:
मायातत्त्वाधिपतिः सोऽनन्तः समुदितान्विचार्याणून् ।
युगपत्क्षोभयति निशां सा सूते संपुटैरनन्तैः स्वैः ॥ 323
8.m: Lord Ananta, the master of māyātattva, having examined all the souls assembled together, / agitates the Night (niśā) simultaneously; through her endless folds, she gives birth.

8.s:
tena kalādidharāntaṃ yaduktamāvaraṇajālamakhilaṃ tat /
niḥsaṃkhyaṃ ca vicitraṃ māyaivaikā tvabhinneyam // 324
8.d:
तेन कलादिधरान्तं यदुक्तमावरणजालमखिलं तत् ।
निःसंख्यं च विचित्रं मायैवैका त्वभिन्नेयम् ॥ 324
8.m: Therefore, that entire network of coverings described from kalā down to earth, / both countless and diverse, is nothing but this single, undivided māyā.

8.s:
uktaṃ śrīpūrvaśāstre ca dharāvyaktātmakaṃ dvayam /
asaṃkhyātaṃ niśāśaktisaṃjñaṃ tvekasvarūpakam // 325
8.d:
उक्तं श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे च धराव्यक्तात्मकं द्वयम् ।
असंख्यातं निशाशक्तिसंज्ञं त्वेकस्वरूपकम् ॥ 325
8.m: And it is declared in the venerable Pūrvaśāstra: 'The pair consisting of earth and avyakta / is countless, yet designated as the Night power (niśāśakti), possessing a single nature.'

8.s:
pāśāḥ puroktāḥ praṇavāḥ pañcamānāṣṭakaṃ muneḥ /
kulaṃ yoniśca vāgīśī yasyāṃ jāto na jāyate // 326
8.d:
पाशाः पुरोक्ताः प्रणवाः पञ्चमानाष्टकं मुनेः ।
कुलं योनिश्च वागीशी यस्यां जातो न जायते ॥ 326
8.m: The bonds previously mentioned are the Praṇavas, the sage's five measures, the eightfold set, / the family (kula), the womb, and the mistress of speech (Vāgīśī), born from whom one is not born again.

8.s:
dīkṣākāle'dharādhvasthaśuddhau yaccādharādhvagam /
anantasya samīpe tu tatsarvaṃ pariniṣṭhitam // 327
8.d:
दीक्षाकालेऽधराध्वस्थशुद्धौ यच्चाधराध्वगम् ।
अनन्तस्य समीपे तु तत्सर्वं परिनिष्ठितम् ॥ 327
8.m: At the time of initiation, whatever belongs to the lower path in the purification of what abides in the lower path, / all of that is situated in the proximity of Ananta.

8.s:
sādhyo dātā damano dhyāno bhasmeti bindavaḥ pañca /
pañcārthaguhyarudrāṅkuśahṛdayalakṣaṇaṃ ca savyūham // 328
8.d:
साध्यो दाता दमनो ध्यानो भस्मेति बिन्दवः पञ्च ।
पञ्चार्थगुह्यरुद्राङ्कुशहृदयलक्षणं च सव्यूहम् ॥ 328
8.m: Sādhya, Dātā, Damana, Dhyāna, and Bhasman are the five points (bindu); / and the group comprising the secret Rudrāṅkuśahṛdaya of the five matters along with their array,

8.s:
ākarṣādarśau cetyaṣṭakametatpramāṇānām /
aluptavibhavāḥ sarve māyātattvādhikāriṇaḥ // 329
8.d:
आकर्षादर्शौ चेत्यष्टकमेतत्प्रमाणानाम् ।
अलुप्तविभवाः सर्वे मायातत्त्वाधिकारिणः ॥ 329
8.m: and the two, Ākarṣa and Ādarśa—this makes eight authorities. / Possessing undiminished majesty, all these are presiding officers over māyātattva.

8.s:
māyāmayaśarīrāste bhogaṃ svaṃ paribhuñjate /
pralayānte hyanantena saṃhṛtāste tvaharmukhe // 330
8.d:
मायामयशरीरास्ते भोगं स्वं परिभुञ्जते ।
प्रलयान्ते ह्यनन्तेन संहृतास्ते त्वहर्मुखे ॥ 330
8.m: Endowed with bodies formed of māyā, they enjoy their own experiences. / At the end of cosmic dissolution, they are withdrawn by Ananta, but at the dawn of the cosmic day,

8.s:
anyānantaprasādena vibudhā api taṃ param /
suptabuddhaṃ manyamānāḥ svatantrammanyatājaḍāḥ // 331
8.d:
अन्यानन्तप्रसादेन विबुधा अपि तं परम् ।
सुप्तबुद्धं मन्यमानाः स्वतन्त्रम्मन्यताजडाः ॥ 331
8.m: by the grace of another Ananta, even these wise beings, regarding that supreme one / as a sleeper or an awakened one, being dull with self-conceit,

8.s:
svātmānameva jānanti hetuṃ māyāntarālagāḥ /
ataḥ paraṃ sthitā māyā devī jantuvimohinī // 332
8.d:
स्वात्मानमेव जानन्ति हेतुं मायान्तरालगाः ।
अतः परं स्थिता माया देवी जन्तुविमोहिनी ॥ 332
8.m: consider themselves alone to be the cause, abiding within the interior of māyā. / Beyond this stands the goddess Māyā, who deludes living beings.

8.s:
devadevasya sā śaktiratidurghaṭakāritā /
nirvairaparipanthinyā tayā bhramitabuddhayaḥ // 333
8.d:
देवदेवस्य सा शक्तिरतिदुर्घटकारिता ।
निर्वैरपरिपन्थिन्या तया भ्रमितबुद्धयः ॥ 333
8.m: She is the power of the God of gods, who brings about the most difficult feats; / with her intellects bewildered by her who opposes without enmity,

8.s:
idaṃ tattvamidaṃ neti vivadantīha vādinaḥ /
gurudevāgniśāstreṣu ye na bhaktā narādhamāḥ // 334
8.d:
इदं तत्त्वमिदं नेति विवदन्तीह वादिनः ।
गुरुदेवाग्निशास्त्रेषु ये न भक्ता नराधमाः ॥ 334
8.m: disputants argue here, saying 'this is the true principle' or 'this is not.' / Those lowest of men who have no devotion toward guru, deity, fire, and scriptures—

8.s:
satpathaṃ tānparityājya sotpathaṃ nayati dhruvam /
asadyuktivicārajñāñchuṣkatarkāvalambinaḥ // 335
8.d:
सत्पथं तान्परित्याज्य सोत्पथं नयति ध्रुवम् ।
असद्युक्तिविचारज्ञाञ्छुष्कतर्कावलम्बिनः ॥ 335
8.m: she certainly makes them abandon the true path and leads them to the wrong path. / Those who cling to dry logic, skilled in examining fallacious arguments,

8.s:
bhramayatyeva tānmāyā hyamokṣe mokṣalipsayā /
śivadīkṣāsinā cchinnā śivajñānāsinā tathā // 336
8.d:
भ्रमयत्येव तान्माया ह्यमोक्षे मोक्षलिप्सया ।
शिवदीक्षासिना च्छिन्ना शिवज्ञानासिना तथा ॥ 336
8.m: māyā continually confuses in what is non-liberation through their desire for liberation. / Once severed by the sword of Śaiva initiation as well as the sword of Śaiva knowledge,

8.s:
na prarohetpunarnānyo hetustacchedanaṃ prati /
mahāmāyordhvataḥ śuddhā mahāvidyātha mātṛkā // 337
8.d:
न प्ररोहेत्पुनर्नान्यो हेतुस्तच्छेदनं प्रति ।
महामायोर्ध्वतः शुद्धा महाविद्याथ मातृका ॥ 337
8.m: she does not sprout again; there is no other cause for severing her. / Above Mahāmāyā is the pure Mahāvidyā, and then Mātṛkā.

8.s:
vāgīśvarī ca tatrasthaṃ vāmādinavasatpuram /
vāmā jyeṣṭhā raudrī kālī kalavikaraṇībalavikārike tathā // 338
8.d:
वागीश्वरी च तत्रस्थं वामादिनवसत्पुरम् ।
वामा ज्येष्ठा रौद्री काली कलविकरणीबलविकारिके तथा ॥ 338
8.m: And Vāgīśvarī, and situated there the nine true cities of Vāmā and the rest: / Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, Raudrī, Kālī, Kalavikaraṇī, and Balavikārikā;

8.s:
mathanī damanī manonmanī ca tridṛśaḥ pītāḥ samastāstāḥ /
saptakoṭyo mukhyamantrā vidyātattve'tra saṃsthitāḥ // 339
8.d:
मथनी दमनी मनोन्मनी च त्रिदृशः पीताः समस्तास्ताः ।
सप्तकोट्यो मुख्यमन्त्रा विद्यातत्त्वेऽत्र संस्थिताः ॥ 339
8.m: Mathanī, Damanī, and Manonmanī—all three-eyed and yellow. / In this Vidyātattva are situated seventy million principal mantras,

8.s:
ekaikārbudalakṣāṃśāḥ padmākārapurā iha /
vidyārājñyastriguṇyādyāḥ sapta saptārbudeśvarāḥ // 340
8.d:
एकैकार्बुदलक्षांशाः पद्माकारपुरा इह ।
विद्याराज्ञ्यस्त्रिगुण्याद्याः सप्त सप्तार्बुदेश्वराः ॥ 340
8.m: each having one hundred-thousandth portion of ten million [souls], having cities shaped like lotuses. / The queens of Vidyā, beginning with Triguṇyā, are seven, rulers over seventy million.

8.s:
vidyātattvordhvamaiśaṃ tu tattvaṃ tatra kramordhvagam /
śikhaṇḍyādyamanantāntaṃ purāṣṭakayutaṃ puram // 341
8.d:
विद्यातत्त्वोर्ध्वमैशं तु तत्त्वं तत्र क्रमोर्ध्वगम् ।
शिखण्ड्याद्यमनन्तान्तं पुराष्टकयुतं पुरम् ॥ 341
8.m: Above the level of Vidyā is the level of Īśa; there, rising in order, / is the city endowed with the group of eight cities, beginning with Śikhaṇḍin and ending with Ananta:

8.s:
śikhaṇḍī śrīgalo mūrtirekanetraikarudrakau /
śivottamaḥ sūkṣmarudro'nanto vidyeśvarāṣṭakam // 342
8.d:
शिखण्डी श्रीगलो मूर्तिरेकनेत्रैकरुद्रकौ ।
शिवोत्तमः सूक्ष्मरुद्रोऽनन्तो विद्येश्वराष्टकम् ॥ 342
8.m: Śikhaṇḍī, Śrīgaḷa, Mūrti, Ekanetra, Ekarudraka, / Śivottama, Sūkṣmarudra, and Ananta—the eight Lords of Vidyā (Vidyeśvaras),

8.s:
kramādūrdhvordhvasaṃsthānaṃ saptānāṃ nāyako vibhuḥ /
ananta eva dhyeyaśca pūjyaścāpyuttarottaraḥ // 343
8.d:
क्रमादूर्ध्वोर्ध्वसंस्थानं सप्तानां नायको विभुः ।
अनन्त एव ध्येयश्च पूज्यश्चाप्युत्तरोत्तरः ॥ 343
8.m: residing higher and higher in succession. The all-pervading leader of the seven / is Ananta; he is to be meditated upon and worshipped, each higher one exceeding the previous.

8.s:
mukhyamantreśvarāṇāṃ yat sārdhaṃ koṭitrayaṃ sthitam /
tannāyakā ime tena vidyeśāścakravartinaḥ // 344
8.d:
मुख्यमन्त्रेश्वराणां यत् सार्धं कोटित्रयं स्थितम् ।
तन्नायका इमे तेन विद्येशाश्चक्रवर्तिनः ॥ 344
8.m: The thirty-five million principal lords of mantras that exist— / these are their leaders, and for that reason these Lords of Vidyā are sovereign emperors.

8.s:
uktaṃ ca gurubhiritthaṃ śivatanvādyeṣu śāsaneṣvetat /
bhagabilaśatakalitaguhāmūrdhāsanago'ṣṭaśaktiyugdevaḥ // 345
8.d:
उक्तं च गुरुभिरित्थं शिवतन्वाद्येषु शासनेष्वेतत् ।
भगबिलशतकलितगुहामूर्धासनगोऽष्टशक्तियुग्देवः ॥ 345
8.m: And so it has been stated by the gurus in the scriptures such as the Śivatanu: / 'The God, seated on a throne above a cave marked with a hundred openings of the vulva, united with eight powers,

8.s:
gahanādyaṃ nirayāntaṃ sṛjati ca rudrāṃśca viniyuṅkte /
uddharati manonmanyā puṃsasteṣveva bhavati madhyasthaḥ // 346
8.d:
गहनाद्यं निरयान्तं सृजति च रुद्रांश्च विनियुङ्क्ते ।
उद्धरति मनोन्मन्या पुंसस्तेष्वेव भवति मध्यस्थः ॥ 346
8.m: creates [the world] from Gahana down to the hells, commissions the Rudras, / redeems souls by means of Manonmanī, and remains neutral among them.

8.s:
te tenodastacitaḥ paratattvālocane'bhiniviśante /
sa punaradhaḥ pathavartiṣvadhikṛta evāṇuṣu śivena // 347
8.d:
ते तेनोदस्तचितः परतत्त्वालोचनेऽभिनिविशन्ते ।
स पुनरधः पथवर्तिष्वधिकृत एवाणुषु शिवेन ॥ 347
8.m: With their consciousness raised by him, they enter into the contemplation of the supreme reality. / He, however, is commissioned by Śiva over the bound souls who reside on the lower path.

8.s:
avasitapativiniyogaḥ sārdhamanekātmamantrakoṭībhiḥ /
nirvātyanantanāthastaddhāmāviśati sūkṣmarudrastu // 348
8.d:
अवसितपतिविनियोगः सार्धमनेकात्ममन्त्रकोटीभिः ।
निर्वात्यनन्तनाथस्तद्धामाविशति सूक्ष्मरुद्रस्तु ॥ 348
8.m: When the Lord's commission is completed, together with crores of mantras consisting of manifold souls, / Anantanātha attains liberation, and Sūkṣmarudra enters his abode.

8.s:
anugṛhyāṇumapūrvaṃ sthāpayati patiḥ śikhaṇḍinaḥ sthāne /
ityaṣṭau paripāṭyā yāvaddhāmāni yāti gururekaḥ // 349
8.d:
अनुगृह्याणुमपूर्वं स्थापयति पतिः शिखण्डिनः स्थाने ।
इत्यष्टौ परिपाट्या यावद्धामानि याति गुरुरेकः ॥ 349
8.m: Having graced a new bound soul, the Lord installs him in the place of Śikhaṇḍin.' / In this manner, as one guru proceeds through the eight abodes in order,

8.s:
tāvadasaṃkhyātānāṃ jantūnāṃ nirvṛtiṃ kurute /
te'ṣṭāvapi śaktyaṣṭakayogāmalajalaruhāsanāsīnāḥ // 350
8.d:
तावदसंख्यातानां जन्तूनां निर्वृतिं कुरुते ।
तेऽष्टावपि शक्त्यष्टकयोगामलजलरुहासनासीनाः ॥ 350
8.m: so he effects the liberation of countless living beings. / All eight of them, seated on immaculate lotus thrones by union with the eight powers,

8.s:
ālokayanti devaṃ hṛdayasthaṃ kāraṇaṃ paramam /
taṃ bhagavantamanantaṃ dhyāyantaḥ svahṛdi kāraṇaṃ śāntam // 351
8.d:
आलोकयन्ति देवं हृदयस्थं कारणं परमम् ।
तं भगवन्तमनन्तं ध्यायन्तः स्वहृदि कारणं शान्तम् ॥ 351
8.m: gaze upon the God residing in the heart, the supreme cause. / Meditating upon that Lord Ananta, the tranquil cause, within their own hearts,

8.s:
saptānudhyāyantyapi mantrāṇāṃ koṭayaḥ śuddhāḥ /
māyādiravīcyanto bhavastvanantādirucyate'pyabhavaḥ // 352
8.d:
सप्तानुध्यायन्त्यपि मन्त्राणां कोटयः शुद्धाः ।
मायादिरवीच्यन्तो भवस्त्वनन्तादिरुच्यतेऽप्यभवः ॥ 352
8.m: the seven crores of pure mantras also meditate upon him. / Transmigratory existence (bhava) is from Māyā down to the Avīci hell; but non-transmigratory existence (abhava) is said to begin with Ananta,

8.s:
śivaśuddhaguṇādhīkārāntaḥ so'pyeṣa heyaśca /
atrāpi yato dṛṣṭānugrāhyāṇāṃ niyojyatā śaivī // 353
8.d:
शिवशुद्धगुणाधीकारान्तः सोऽप्येष हेयश्च ।
अत्रापि यतो दृष्टानुग्राह्याणां नियोज्यता शैवी ॥ 353
8.m: ending with the sphere of authority of Śiva's pure qualities; yet even this is to be abandoned, / because even here the Śaiva commissioning of visible recipients of grace is observed,

8.s:
iṣṭā ca tannivṛttirhyabhavastvadhare na bhūyate yasmāt /
patyurapasarpati yataḥ kāraṇatā kāryatā ca siddhebhyaḥ // 354
8.d:
इष्टा च तन्निवृत्तिर्ह्यभवस्त्वधरे न भूयते यस्मात् ।
पत्युरपसर्पति यतः कारणता कार्यता च सिद्धेभ्यः ॥ 354
8.m: and its cessation is desired; for in the lower [realm] non-transmigratory existence does not occur, / because the Lord's state of being a cause and the state of being an effect depart from the perfected beings.

8.s:
kañcukavacchivasiddhau tāvatibhavasaṃjñayātimadhyasthau /
dharmajñānavirāgaiśyacatuṣṭayapuraṃ tu yat // 355
8.d:
कञ्चुकवच्छिवसिद्धौ तावतिभवसंज्ञयातिमध्यस्थौ ।
धर्मज्ञानविरागैश्यचतुष्टयपुरं तु यत् ॥ 355
8.m: In the state of Śiva's perfection, [both] are like a cuirass; they stand completely intermediate under the designation 'transmigratory existence' and 'non-existence'. / As for the city of the fourfold Dharma, Jñāna, Vairāgya, and Aiśvarya,

8.s:
rūpāvaraṇasaṃjñaṃ tattattve'sminnaiśvare viduḥ /
vāmā jyeṣṭhā ca raudrīti bhuvanatrayaśobhitam // 356
8.d:
रूपावरणसंज्ञं तत्तत्त्वेऽस्मिन्नैश्वरे विदुः ।
वामा ज्येष्ठा च रौद्रीति भुवनत्रयशोभितम् ॥ 356
8.m: known by the name Rūpāvaraṇa, they recognize it in this tattva of Īśvara. / Adorned with the triad of worlds—Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, and Raudrī—

8.s:
sūkṣmāvaraṇamākhyātamīśatattve gurūttamaiḥ /
aiśātsādāśivaṃ jñānakriyāyugalamaṇḍitam // 357
8.d:
सूक्ष्मावरणमाख्यातमीशतत्त्वे गुरूत्तमैः ।
ऐशात्सादाशिवं ज्ञानक्रियायुगलमण्डितम् ॥ 357
8.m: the Sūkṣmāvaraṇa has been declared in the Īśatattva by the best of gurus. / Beyond the Aiśa is the Sādāśiva, adorned with the pair of knowledge and action;

8.s:
śuddhāvaraṇamityāhuruktā śuddhāvṛteḥ param /
vidyāvṛtistato bhāvābhāvaśaktidvayojjvalā // 358
8.d:
शुद्धावरणमित्याहुरुक्ता शुद्धावृतेः परम् ।
विद्यावृतिस्ततो भावाभावशक्तिद्वयोज्ज्वला ॥ 358
8.m: they call it the Śuddhāvaraṇa. Beyond the Śuddhāvṛti is said to be / the Vidyāvṛti; after that, radiant with the two powers of existence and non-existence,

8.s:
śaktyāvṛtiḥ pramāṇākhyā tataḥ śāstre nirūpitā /
śaktyāvṛtestu tejasvidhruveśābhyāmalaṅkṛtam // 359
8.d:
शक्त्यावृतिः प्रमाणाख्या ततः शास्त्रे निरूपिता ।
शक्त्यावृतेस्तु तेजस्विध्रुवेशाभ्यामलङ्कृतम् ॥ 359
8.m: the Śaktyāvṛti named Pramāṇa is expounded in the scripture. / Beyond the Śaktyāvṛti is the Tejasvyāvaraṇa,

8.s:
tejasvyāvaraṇaṃ vedapurā mānāvṛtistataḥ /
mānāvṛteḥ suśuddhāvṛtpuratritayaśobhitā // 360
8.d:
तेजस्व्यावरणं वेदपुरा मानावृतिस्ततः ।
मानावृतेः सुशुद्धावृत्पुरत्रितयशोभिता ॥ 360
8.m: adorned by Tejasvin and Dhruveśa. Then is the Mānāvṛti having four cities; / beyond the Mānāvṛti is the Suśuddhāvṛt, adorned with a triad of cities.

8.s:
suśuddhāvaraṇādūrdhva śaivamekapuraṃ bhavet /
śivāvṛterūrdhvamāhurmokṣāvaraṇasaṃjñitam // 361
8.d:
सुशुद्धावरणादूर्ध्व शैवमेकपुरं भवेत् ।
शिवावृतेरूर्ध्वमाहुर्मोक्षावरणसंज्ञितम् ॥ 361
8.m: Above the Suśuddhāvaraṇa there is a single Śaiva city. / Above the Śivāvṛti they speak of that which is named Mokṣāvaraṇa.

8.s:
asyāṃ mokṣāvṛtau rudrā ekādaśa nirūpitāḥ /
mokṣāvaraṇatastvekapuramāvaraṇaṃ dhruvam // 362
8.d:
अस्यां मोक्षावृतौ रुद्रा एकादश निरूपिताः ।
मोक्षावरणतस्त्वेकपुरमावरणं ध्रुवम् ॥ 362
8.m: In this Mokṣāvṛti, eleven Rudras are described. / Beyond the Mokṣāvaraṇa is the Dhruvāvaraṇa consisting of one city.

8.s:
ūrdhve dhruvāvṛtericchāvaraṇaṃ tatra te śivāḥ /
īśvarecchāgṛhāntasthāstatpuraṃ caikamucyate // 363
8.d:
ऊर्ध्वे ध्रुवावृतेरिच्छावरणं तत्र ते शिवाः ।
ईश्वरेच्छागृहान्तस्थास्तत्पुरं चैकमुच्यते ॥ 363
8.m: Above the Dhruvāvṛti is the Icchāvaraṇa; there those Śivas / reside inside the abode of the will of Īśvara, and its city is said to be one.

8.s:
icchāvṛteḥ prabuddhākhyaṃ digrudrāṣṭakacarcitam /
prabuddhāvaraṇādūrdhva samayāvaraṇaṃ mahat // 364
8.d:
इच्छावृतेः प्रबुद्धाख्यं दिग्रुद्राष्टकचर्चितम् ।
प्रबुद्धावरणादूर्ध्व समयावरणं महत् ॥ 364
8.m: Beyond the Icchāvṛti is that named Prabuddha, attended by the eight Rudras of the directions. / Above the Prabuddhāvaraṇa is the great Samayāvaraṇa,

8.s:
bhuvanaiḥ pañcabhirgarbhīkṛtānantasamāvṛti /
sāmayātsauśivaṃ tatra sādākhyaṃ bhuvanaṃ mahat // 365
8.d:
भुवनैः पञ्चभिर्गर्भीकृतानन्तसमावृति ।
सामयात्सौशिवं तत्र सादाख्यं भुवनं महत् ॥ 365
8.m: an infinite enclosure encompassing five worlds. / Beyond the Sāmaya is the Sauśiva; there is the great world called Sādākhya.

8.s:
tasminsadāśivo devastasya savyāpasavyayoḥ /
jñānakriye parecchā tu śaktirutsaṅgagāminī // 366
8.d:
तस्मिन्सदाशिवो देवस्तस्य सव्यापसव्ययोः ।
ज्ञानक्रिये परेच्छा तु शक्तिरुत्सङ्गगामिनी ॥ 366
8.m: In it is the god Sadāśiva; on his right and left / are knowledge and action, while the power of supreme will rests upon his lap.

8.s:
sṛṣṭyādipañcakṛtyāni kurute sa tayecchayā /
pañca brahmāṇyaṅgaṣaṭkaṃ sakalādyaṣṭakaṃ śivāḥ // 367
8.d:
सृष्ट्यादिपञ्चकृत्यानि कुरुते स तयेच्छया ।
पञ्च ब्रह्माण्यङ्गषट्कं सकलाद्यष्टकं शिवाः ॥ 367
8.m: Through that will he performs the fivefold acts of creation and the rest. / The five Brahmans, the six auxiliary limbs, the group of eight beginning with Sakala, the Śivas,

8.s:
daśāṣṭādaśa rudrāśca taireva suśivo vṛtaḥ /
sadyo vāmāghorau puruṣeśau brahmapañcakaṃ hṛdayam // 368
8.d:
दशाष्टादश रुद्राश्च तैरेव सुशिवो वृतः ।
सद्यो वामाघोरौ पुरुषेशौ ब्रह्मपञ्चकं हृदयम् ॥ 368
8.m: and the ten and eighteen Rudras: by them alone Suśiva is surrounded. / Sadyo[jāta], Vāma, Aghora, and the two Puruṣas (Tatpuruṣa and Īśāna) are the five Brahmans. The heart,

8.s:
mūrdhaśikhāvarmadṛgastramaṅgāni ṣaṭ prāhuḥ /
