sakalākalaśūnyaiḥ saha kalāḍhyakhamalaṅkṛte kṣapaṇamantyam // 369
8.d:
मूर्धशिखावर्मदृगस्त्रमङ्गानि षट् प्राहुः ।
सकलाकलशून्यैः सह कलाढ्यखमलङ्कृते क्षपणमन्त्यम् ॥ 369
8.m: head, crest, armour, eye, and weapon are called the six limbs. / Along with Sakala, Akala, and Śūnya, the space endowed with kalās is adorned, and the final is Kṣapaṇa;

8.s:
kaṇṭhyauṣṭhyamaṣṭamaṃ kila sakalāṣṭakametadāmnātam /
oṃ kāraśivau dīpto hetvīśadaśeśakau suśivakālau // 370
8.d:
कण्ठ्यौष्ठ्यमष्टमं किल सकलाष्टकमेतदाम्नातम् ।
ओं कारशिवौ दीप्तो हेत्वीशदशेशकौ सुशिवकालौ ॥ 370
8.m: the eighth is indeed Kaṇṭhyauṣṭhya—this is handed down as the Sakalāṣṭaka. / Oṅkāra and Śiva, Dīpta, Hetvīśa and Daśeśaka, Suśiva and Kāla,

8.s:
sūkṣmasutejaḥśarvāḥ śivāḥ daśaite'tra pūrvādeḥ /
vijayo niḥśvāsaśca svāyambhuvo vahnivīrarauravakāḥ // 371
8.d:
सूक्ष्मसुतेजःशर्वाः शिवाः दशैतेऽत्र पूर्वादेः ।
विजयो निःश्वासश्च स्वायम्भुवो वह्निवीररौरवकाः ॥ 371
8.m: Sūkṣma, Sutejas, and Śarva—these are the ten Śivas here, beginning from the east. / Vijaya and Niḥśvāsa, Svāyambhuva, the Vahnivīras, Rauravaka,

8.s:
mukuṭavisarenduvinduprodgītā lalitasiddharudrau ca /
santānaśivau parakiraṇapārameśā iti smṛtā rudrāḥ // 372
8.d:
मुकुटविसरेन्दुविन्दुप्रोद्गीता ललितसिद्धरुद्रौ च ।
सन्तानशिवौ परकिरणपारमेशा इति स्मृता रुद्राः ॥ 372
8.m: Mukuṭa, Visara, Indu, Vindu, Prodgīta, Lalitarudra and Siddharudra, / Santāna and Śiva, Parakiraṇa and Pārameśa—these are remembered as the [eighteen] Rudras.

8.s:
sarveṣāmeteṣāṃ jñānāni viduḥ svatulyanāmāni /
mantramunikoṭiparivṛta matha vibhuvāmādirudratacchaktiyutam // 373
8.d:
सर्वेषामेतेषां ज्ञानानि विदुः स्वतुल्यनामानि ।
मन्त्रमुनिकोटिपरिवृत मथ विभुवामादिरुद्रतच्छक्तियुतम् ॥ 373
8.m: They recognize that the knowledge-revelations of all of these bear names identical to their own. / Surrounded by tens of millions of mantras and sages, endowed with the all-pervading Rudras—Vāmā and the rest—and their powers,

8.s:
tārādiśaktijuṣṭaṃ suśivāsanamatisitakajamasaṃkhyadalam /
yaḥ śaktirudravargaḥ parivāre viṣṭare ca suśivasya // 374
8.d:
तारादिशक्तिजुष्टं सुशिवासनमतिसितकजमसंख्यदलम् ।
यः शक्तिरुद्रवर्गः परिवारे विष्टरे च सुशिवस्य ॥ 374
8.m: enjoyed by powers beginning with Tārā, is the throne of Suśiva: an exceedingly white lotus of countless petals. / The host of powers and Rudras that forms the retinue and throne of Suśiva—

8.s:
pratyekamasya nijanijaparivāre parārdhakoṭayo'saṃkhyāḥ /
māyāmalanirmuktāḥ kevalamadhikāramātrasaṃrūḍhāḥ // 375
8.d:
प्रत्येकमस्य निजनिजपरिवारे परार्धकोटयोऽसंख्याः ।
मायामलनिर्मुक्ताः केवलमधिकारमात्रसंरूढाः ॥ 375
8.m: each one of them has in its own retinue countless quadrillions [of attendants]. / Liberated from the impurity of Māyā, established merely in cosmic office,

8.s:
suśivāvaraṇe rudrāḥ sarvajñāḥ sarvaśaktisampūrṇāḥ /
adhikārabandhavilaye śāntāḥ śivarūpiṇo punarbhavinaḥ // 376
8.d:
सुशिवावरणे रुद्राः सर्वज्ञाः सर्वशक्तिसम्पूर्णाः ।
अधिकारबन्धविलये शान्ताः शिवरूपिणो पुनर्भविनः ॥ 376
8.m: the Rudras in the enclosure of Suśiva are omniscient and full of all powers. / Upon the dissolution of the bond of office, peaceful, of the nature of Śiva, they are not reborn.

8.s:
ūrdhve bindvāvṛtirdīptā tatra tatra padmaṃ śaśiprabham /
śāntyatītaḥ śivastatra tacchaktyutsaṅgabhūṣitaḥ // 377
8.d:
ऊर्ध्वे बिन्द्वावृतिर्दीप्ता तत्र तत्र पद्मं शशिप्रभम् ।
शान्त्यतीतः शिवस्तत्र तच्छक्त्युत्सङ्गभूषितः ॥ 377
8.m: Above is the radiant Bindvāvṛti; there is a lotus shining like the moon. / Śāntyatīta Śiva is there, adorned by his power sitting upon his lap,

8.s:
nivṛttyādikalāvargaparivārasamāvṛtaḥ /
asaṃkhyarudratacchaktipurakoṭibhirāvṛtaḥ // 378
8.d:
निवृत्त्यादिकलावर्गपरिवारसमावृतः ।
असंख्यरुद्रतच्छक्तिपुरकोटिभिरावृतः ॥ 378
8.m: surrounded by the retinue of the groups of kalās beginning with Nivṛtti, / enveloped by millions of cities of countless Rudras and their powers.

8.s:
śrīmanmataṅgaśāstre ca layākhyaṃ tattvamuttamam /
pāribhāṣikamityetannāmnā bindurihocyate // 379
8.d:
श्रीमन्मतङ्गशास्त्रे च लयाख्यं तत्त्वमुत्तमम् ।
पारिभाषिकमित्येतन्नाम्ना बिन्दुरिहोच्यते ॥ 379
8.m: And in the venerable Mataṅga treatise, the supreme principle named Laya / is conventionally referred to here by the name Bindu.

8.s:
caturmūrtimayaṃ śubhraṃ yattatsakalaniṣkalam /
tasminbhogaḥ samuddiṣṭa ityatredaṃ ca varṇitam // 380
8.d:
चतुर्मूर्तिमयं शुभ्रं यत्तत्सकलनिष्कलम् ।
तस्मिन्भोगः समुद्दिष्ट इत्यत्रेदं च वर्णितम् ॥ 380
8.m: That which consists of four forms, luminous, which is both Sakala and Niṣkala: / in it experiential enjoyment is taught; thus this has been described here.

8.s:
nivṛttyādeḥ susūkṣmatvāddharādyārabdhadehatā /
mātuḥ sphūrjanmahājñānalīnatvānna vibhāvyate // 381
8.d:
निवृत्त्यादेः सुसूक्ष्मत्वाद्धराद्यारब्धदेहता ।
मातुः स्फूर्जन्महाज्ञानलीनत्वान्न विभाव्यते ॥ 381
8.m: Because Nivṛtti and the others are extremely subtle, the condition of having a body formed from earth and the rest / is not perceived, since the knower is absorbed in flaming great knowledge. // 381

8.s:
udrikta taijasatvena hemno bhūparamāṇavaḥ /
yathā pṛthaṅna bhāntyevamūrdhvādhorudradehagāḥ // 382
8.d:
उद्रिक्त तैजसत्वेन हेम्नो भूपरमाणवः ।
यथा पृथङ्न भान्त्येवमूर्ध्वाधोरुद्रदेहगाः ॥ 382
8.m: Just as the earth-atoms in gold do not appear separate, / because the fiery nature is predominant, so too for those residing in the bodies of the Rudras above and below. // 382

8.s:
bindūrdhve'rdhenduretasya kalā jyotsnā ca tadvatī /
kāntiḥ prabhā ca vimalā pañcaitā rodhikāstataḥ // 383
8.d:
बिन्दूर्ध्वेऽर्धेन्दुरेतस्य कला ज्योत्स्ना च तद्वती ।
कान्तिः प्रभा च विमला पञ्चैता रोधिकास्ततः ॥ 383
8.m: Above the Bindu is the half-moon (Ardhendu); its Kalās are Jyotsnā and Tadvatī, / Kānti, Prabhā, and Vimalā: these are five; next is Rodhikā. // 383

8.s:
rundhanī rodhanī roddhrī jñānabodhā tamopahā /
etāḥ pañca kalāḥ prāhurnirodhinyāṃ gurūttamāh // 384
8.d:
रुन्धनी रोधनी रोद्ध्री ज्ञानबोधा तमोपहा ।
एताः पञ्च कलाः प्राहुर्निरोधिन्यां गुरूत्तमाह् ॥ 384
8.m: Rundhanī, Rodhanī, Roddhrī, Jñānabodhā, and Tamopahā: / the best of gurus state these five Kalās to be in Nirodhinī. // 384

8.s:
ardhamātraḥ smṛto bindurvyomarūpī catuṣkalaḥ /
tadardhamardhacandrastadaṣṭāṃśena nirodhikā // 385
8.d:
अर्धमात्रः स्मृतो बिन्दुर्व्योमरूपी चतुष्कलः ।
तदर्धमर्धचन्द्रस्तदष्टांशेन निरोधिका ॥ 385
8.m: The Bindu is taught as having half a mora, possessing the form of space and having four Kalās. / Half of that is Ardhacandra; by an eighth part thereof is Nirodhikā. // 385

8.s:
hetūnbrahmādikān runddhe rodhikāṃ tāṃ tyajettataḥ /
nirodhikāmimāṃ bhittvā sādākhyaṃ bhuvanaṃ param // 386
8.d:
हेतून्ब्रह्मादिकान् रुन्द्धे रोधिकां तां त्यजेत्ततः ।
निरोधिकामिमां भित्त्वा सादाख्यं भुवनं परम् ॥ 386
8.m: She obstructs the causal deities such as Brahmā; one should therefore abandon that Rodhikā. / Having pierced this Nirodhikā, [there is] the supreme realm of Sadākhya, // 386

8.s:
pararūpeṇa yatrāste pañcamantramahātanuḥ /
ityardhendunirodhyantabindvāvṛtyūrdhvato mahān // 387
8.d:
पररूपेण यत्रास्ते पञ्चमन्त्रमहातनुः ।
इत्यर्धेन्दुनिरोध्यन्तबिन्द्वावृत्यूर्ध्वतो महान् ॥ 387
8.m: where He resides in supreme form, whose great body consists of the five Mantras. / Thus, above the enclosure of the Bindu that ends with Ardhendu and Nirodhī, [resides] the great // 387

8.s:
nādaḥ kiñjalkasadṛśo mahadbhiḥ puruṣairvṛtaḥ /
catvāri bhuvanānyatra dikṣu madhye ca pañcamam // 388
8.d:
नादः किञ्जल्कसदृशो महद्भिः पुरुषैर्वृतः ।
चत्वारि भुवनान्यत्र दिक्षु मध्ये च पञ्चमम् ॥ 388
8.m: Nāda, resembling a lotus filament, surrounded by great beings (puruṣas). / There are four realms here in the cardinal directions, and a fifth in the center. // 388

8.s:
indhikā dīpikā caiva rodhikā mocikordhvagā /
madhye'tra padmaṃ tatrordhvagāmī tacchaktibhirvṛtaḥ // 389
8.d:
इन्धिका दीपिका चैव रोधिका मोचिकोर्ध्वगा ।
मध्येऽत्र पद्मं तत्रोर्ध्वगामी तच्छक्तिभिर्वृतः ॥ 389
8.m: Indhikā, Dīpikā, Rodhikā, Mocikā, and Ūrdhvagā. / Here in the center is a lotus; upon it is Ūrdhvagāmin, surrounded by His powers. // 389

8.s:
nādordhvatastu sauṣumnaṃ tatra tacchaktibhṛtprabhuḥ /
tadīśaḥ piṅgalelābhyāṃ vṛtaḥ savyāpasavyayoḥ // 390
8.d:
नादोर्ध्वतस्तु सौषुम्नं तत्र तच्छक्तिभृत्प्रभुः ।
तदीशः पिङ्गलेलाभ्यां वृतः सव्यापसव्ययोः ॥ 390
8.m: Above Nāda is the Suṣumnā realm; there the Lord resides bearing His powers, / the Lord of that realm, flanked by Piṅgalā and Iḍā to the right and the left. // 390

8.s:
yā prabhoraṅkagā devī suṣumnā śaśisaprabhā /
grathito'dhvā tayā sarva ūrdhvaścādhastanastathā // 391
8.d:
या प्रभोरङ्कगा देवी सुषुम्ना शशिसप्रभा ।
ग्रथितोऽध्वा तया सर्व ऊर्ध्वश्चाधस्तनस्तथा ॥ 391
8.m: The Goddess on the Lord's lap is Suṣumnā, possessing the splendor of the moon; / by Her the entire path—both upper and lower—is woven together. // 391

8.s:
nādaḥsuṣumnādhārastu bhittvā viśvamidaṃ jagat /
adhaḥśaktyā vinirgacchedūrdhvaśaktyā ca mūrdhataḥ // 392
8.d:
नादःसुषुम्नाधारस्तु भित्त्वा विश्वमिदं जगत् ।
अधःशक्त्या विनिर्गच्छेदूर्ध्वशक्त्या च मूर्धतः ॥ 392
8.m: Nāda, supported by Suṣumnā, having pierced this entire universe, / would issue forth by the lower power, and from the crown of the head by the upper power. // 392

8.s:
nāḍyā brahmabile līnaḥ so'vyaktadhvanirakṣaraḥ /
nadansarveṣu bhūteṣu śivaśaktyā hyadhiṣṭhitaḥ // 393
8.d:
नाड्या ब्रह्मबिले लीनः सोऽव्यक्तध्वनिरक्षरः ।
नदन्सर्वेषु भूतेषु शिवशक्त्या ह्यधिष्ठितः ॥ 393
8.m: Absorbed in the opening of Brahmā (brahmabila) via the channel, it is unmanifest, imperishable sound, / resounding in all beings, presided over indeed by Śiva's power. // 393

8.s:
suṣumnordhve brahmabilasaṃjñayāvaraṇaṃ tridṛk /
tatra brahmā sitaḥ śūlī pañcāsyaḥ śaśiśekharaḥ // 394
8.d:
सुषुम्नोर्ध्वे ब्रह्मबिलसंज्ञयावरणं त्रिदृक् ।
तत्र ब्रह्मा सितः शूली पञ्चास्यः शशिशेखरः ॥ 394
8.m: Above Suṣumnā is the enclosure named the opening of Brahmā, having three eyes; / there resides white Brahmā, holding a trident, five-faced, moon-crested. // 394

8.s:
tasyotsaṅge parā devī brahmāṇī mokṣamārgagā /
roddhrī dātrī ca mokṣasya tāṃ bhittvā cordhvakuṇḍalī // 395
8.d:
तस्योत्सङ्गे परा देवी ब्रह्माणी मोक्षमार्गगा ।
रोद्ध्री दात्री च मोक्षस्य तां भित्त्वा चोर्ध्वकुण्डली ॥ 395
8.m: On His lap is the supreme Goddess Brahmāṇī, situated on the path of liberation, / who both obstructs and grants liberation. Piercing Her, [there is] Ūrdhvakuṇḍalī. // 395

8.s:
śaktiḥ suptāhisadṛśī sā viśvādhāra ucyate /
tasyāṃ sūkṣmā susūkṣmā ca tathānye amṛtāmite // 396
8.d:
शक्तिः सुप्ताहिसदृशी सा विश्वाधार उच्यते ।
तस्यां सूक्ष्मा सुसूक्ष्मा च तथान्ये अमृतामिते ॥ 396
8.m: The power resembles a sleeping serpent; She is called the support of the universe. / In Her reside Sūkṣmā and Susūkṣmā, and likewise the other two, Amṛtā and Amitā. // 396

8.s:
madhyato vyāpinī tasyāṃ vyāpīśo vyāpinīdharaḥ /
śaktitattvamidaṃ yasya prapañco'yaṃ dharāntakaḥ // 397
8.d:
मध्यतो व्यापिनी तस्यां व्यापीशो व्यापिनीधरः ।
शक्तितत्त्वमिदं यस्य प्रपञ्चोऽयं धरान्तकः ॥ 397
8.m: In the middle is Vyāpinī; in Her is Vyāpīśa, the bearer of Vyāpinī. / This is the tattva of Śakti, whose expansion terminates with earth. // 397

8.s:
śivatattvaṃ tatastatra caturdikkaṃ vyavasthitāḥ /
vyāpī vyomātmako'nanto'nāthastacchaktibhāginaḥ // 398
8.d:
शिवतत्त्वं ततस्तत्र चतुर्दिक्कं व्यवस्थिताः ।
व्यापी व्योमात्मकोऽनन्तोऽनाथस्तच्छक्तिभागिनः ॥ 398
8.m: Above that is Śivatattva; there, stationed in the four directions, / are Vyāpin, the space-formed Ananta, and Anātha, who share His power. // 398

8.s:
madhye tvanāśritaṃ tatra devadevo hyanāśritaḥ /
tacchaktyutsaṅgabhṛtsūryaśatakoṭisamaprabhaḥ // 399
8.d:
मध्ये त्वनाश्रितं तत्र देवदेवो ह्यनाश्रितः ।
तच्छक्त्युत्सङ्गभृत्सूर्यशतकोटिसमप्रभः ॥ 399
8.m: In the center, however, is Anāśrita; there the God of gods, indeed Anāśrita, / holds His power upon His lap, possessing a splendor equal to a billion suns. // 399

8.s:
śivatattvordhvataḥ śaktiḥ parā sā samanāhvayā /
sarveṣāṃ kāraṇānāṃ sā kartṛbhūtā vyavasthitā // 400
8.d:
शिवतत्त्वोर्ध्वतः शक्तिः परा सा समनाह्वया ।
सर्वेषां कारणानां सा कर्तृभूता व्यवस्थिता ॥ 400
8.m: Above Śivatattva is the supreme power named Samanā; / She is established as the active agent of all causal deities. // 400

8.s:
bibhartyaṇḍānyanekāni śivena samadhiṣṭhitā /
tadārūḍhaḥ śivaḥ kṛtyapañcakaṃ kurute prabhuḥ // 401
8.d:
बिभर्त्यण्डान्यनेकानि शिवेन समधिष्ठिता ।
तदारूढः शिवः कृत्यपञ्चकं कुरुते प्रभुः ॥ 401
8.m: Presided over by Śiva, She sustains many cosmic eggs. / Mounted upon Her, Lord Śiva performs the fivefold cosmic act. // 401

8.s:
samanā karaṇaṃ tasya hetukarturmahośituḥ /
anāśritaṃ tu vyāpāre nimittaṃ heturucyate // 402
8.d:
समना करणं तस्य हेतुकर्तुर्महोशितुः ।
अनाश्रितं तु व्यापारे निमित्तं हेतुरुच्यते ॥ 402
8.m: Samanā is the instrument of that supreme Lord who is the causal agent; / while Anāśrita is stated to be the prompting cause (hetu) in the activity. // 402

8.s:
tayādhitiṣṭhati vibhuḥ kāraṇānāṃ tu pañcakam /
anāśrito'nāthamayamanantaṃ khavapuḥ sadā // 403
8.d:
तयाधितिष्ठति विभुः कारणानां तु पञ्चकम् ।
अनाश्रितोऽनाथमयमनन्तं खवपुः सदा ॥ 403
8.m: Through Her the all-pervading Lord presides over the pentad of causal deities; / Anāśrita, composed of Anātha, is Ananta, ever having space as His body. // 403

8.s:
sa vyāpinaṃ prerayati svaśaktyā karaṇena tu /
karmarūpā sthitā māyā yadadhaḥ śaktikuṇḍalī // 404
8.d:
स व्यापिनं प्रेरयति स्वशक्त्या करणेन तु ।
कर्मरूपा स्थिता माया यदधः शक्तिकुण्डली ॥ 404
8.m: He impels Vyāpin by means of His own power, the instrument; / while Māyā stands in the form of the object, beneath which is Śaktikuṇḍalī. // 404

8.s:
nādabindvādikaṃ kāryamityādijagadudbhavaḥ /
yatsadāśivaparyantaṃ pārthivādyaṃ ca śāsane // 405
8.d:
नादबिन्द्वादिकं कार्यमित्यादिजगदुद्भवः ।
यत्सदाशिवपर्यन्तं पार्थिवाद्यं च शासने ॥ 405
8.m: The effect is Nāda, Bindu, and so on; thus proceeds the origination of the world. / In the teaching, whatever begins with the earth element and extends up to Sadāśiva // 405

8.s:
tatsarva prākṛtaṃ proktaṃ vināśotpattisaṃyutam /
atha sakalabhuvanamānaṃ yanmahyaṃ nigaditaṃ nijairgurubhiḥ // 406
8.d:
तत्सर्व प्राकृतं प्रोक्तं विनाशोत्पत्तिसंयुतम् ।
अथ सकलभुवनमानं यन्मह्यं निगदितं निजैर्गुरुभिः ॥ 406
8.m: is all declared to be material (prākṛta), accompanied by origination and destruction. / Now the extent of all the worlds that was imparted to me by my own gurus // 406

8.s:
tadvakṣyate samāsādbuddhau yenāśu saṅkrāmet /
aṇḍasyāntaranantaḥ kālaḥ kūṣmāṇḍahāṭakau brahmaharī // 407
8.d:
तद्वक्ष्यते समासाद्बुद्धौ येनाशु सङ्क्रामेत् ।
अण्डस्यान्तरनन्तः कालः कूष्माण्डहाटकौ ब्रह्महरी ॥ 407
8.m: will be stated concisely so that it may enter quickly into the intellect: / within the egg are Ananta, Kāla, Kūṣmāṇḍa, Hāṭaka, Brahmā, and Hari; // 407

8.s:
rudrāḥ śataṃ savīraṃ bahirnivṛttistu sāṣṭaśatabhuvanā syāt /
jalatejaḥsamīranabho'haṃkṛddhīmūlasaptake pratyekam // 408
8.d:
रुद्राः शतं सवीरं बहिर्निवृत्तिस्तु साष्टशतभुवना स्यात् ।
जलतेजःसमीरनभोऽहंकृद्धीमूलसप्तके प्रत्येकम् ॥ 408
8.m: outside are a hundred Rudras together with the heroes (vīras). Nivṛtti comprises one hundred and eight worlds: / in the seven, namely water, fire, wind, space, egoity, intellect, and the root [prakṛti], each has // 408

8.s:
aṣṭau ṣaṭpañcāśadbhuvanā tena pratiṣṭheti kalā kathitā /
atra prāhuḥ śodhyānaṣṭau kecinnijāṣṭakādhipatīn // 409
8.d:
अष्टौ षट्पञ्चाशद्भुवना तेन प्रतिष्ठेति कला कथिता ।
अत्र प्राहुः शोध्यानष्टौ केचिन्निजाष्टकाधिपतीन् ॥ 409
8.m: eight [worlds]; thus the Kalā called Pratiṣṭhā is said to consist of fifty-six worlds. / Here some say that only eight—the lords of their respective octads—are to be purified, // 409

8.s:
anye tu samastānāṃ śodhyatvaṃ varṇayanti bhuvanānām /
śrībhūtirājamiśrā guravaḥ prāhuḥ punarbahī rudraśatam // 410
8.d:
अन्ये तु समस्तानां शोध्यत्वं वर्णयन्ति भुवनानाम् ।
श्रीभूतिराजमिश्रा गुरवः प्राहुः पुनर्बही रुद्रशतम् ॥ 410
8.m: while others describe that all the worlds are to be purified. / The guru, illustrious Bhūtirājamiśra, however, taught that outside are a hundred Rudras, // 410

8.s:
aṣṭāvantaḥ sākaṃ śarveṇetīdṛśī nivṛttiriyaṃ syāt /
rudrāḥ kālī vīro dharābdhilakṣmyaḥ sarasvatī guhyam // 411
8.d:
अष्टावन्तः साकं शर्वेणेतीदृशी निवृत्तिरियं स्यात् ।
रुद्राः काली वीरो धराब्धिलक्ष्म्यः सरस्वती गुह्यम् ॥ 411
8.m: and inside eight together with Śarva; such would be this Nivṛtti. / The Rudras, Kālī, the hero, Dharā, Abdhi, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, and Guhya: // 411

8.s:
ityaṣṭakaṃ jale'nau vahnyatiguhyadvayaṃ maruti vāyoḥ /
svapuraṃ gayādi khe ca vyoma pavitrāṣṭakaṃ ca bhuvanayugam // 412
8.d:
इत्यष्टकं जलेऽनौ वह्न्यतिगुह्यद्वयं मरुति वायोः ।
स्वपुरं गयादि खे च व्योम पवित्राष्टकं च भुवनयुगम् ॥ 412
8.m: this is the octad in water. In fire, there is the pair of Vahni and Atiguhya; in wind, the wind's / own city and Gayā, etc.; and in space, Vyoma and the pair of pure worlds (Pavitrāṣṭaka). // 412

8.s:
abhimāne'haṅkāracchagalādyaṣṭakamathāntarā nabho'haṃkṛt /
tanmātrārkenduśratipurāṣṭakaṃ buddhikarmadevānām // 413
8.d:
अभिमानेऽहङ्कारच्छगलाद्यष्टकमथान्तरा नभोऽहंकृत् ।
तन्मात्रार्केन्दुश्रतिपुराष्टकं बुद्धिकर्मदेवानाम् ॥ 413
8.m: In pride (egoity) is the octad beginning with Ahaṅkāra and Chagala; then between space and egoity / is the octad of worlds of the tanmātras, sun, moon, and Śruti; of the deities of the intellect and action [organs], // 413

8.s:
daśa tanmātrasamūhe bhuvanaṃ punarakṣavargavinipatite /
manasaścetyabhimāne dvāviṃśatireva bhuvanānām // 414
8.d:
दश तन्मात्रसमूहे भुवनं पुनरक्षवर्गविनिपतिते ।
मनसश्चेत्यभिमाने द्वाविंशतिरेव भुवनानाम् ॥ 414
8.m: ten; in the aggregate of the subtle elements, a world; again, in the category falling under the sense organs / and mind [there are worlds]; thus in pride (egoity) there are twenty-two worlds. // 414

8.s:
dhiyi daivīnāmaṣṭau kruttejoyogasaṃjñakaṃ trayaṃ tadumā /
tatpatiratha mūrtyaṣṭakasuśivadvādaśakavīrabhadrāḥ syuḥ // 415
8.d:
धियि दैवीनामष्टौ क्रुत्तेजोयोगसंज्ञकं त्रयं तदुमा ।
तत्पतिरथ मूर्त्यष्टकसुशिवद्वादशकवीरभद्राः स्युः ॥ 415
8.m: In the intellect are eight worlds of the goddesses, the triad called Krut, Tejas, and Yoga, their Umā / and their lord; then the octad of forms (Mūrtyaṣṭaka), the twelve Suśivas, and the Vīrabhadras; // 415

8.s:
tadatha mahādevāṣṭakamiti buddhau saptadaśa saṃkhyā /
guṇatattve paṅktitrayamiti ṣaṭpañcāśataṃ purāṇi viduḥ // 416
8.d:
तदथ महादेवाष्टकमिति बुद्धौ सप्तदश संख्या ।
गुणतत्त्वे पङ्क्तित्रयमिति षट्पञ्चाशतं पुराणि विदुः ॥ 416
8.m: then the octad of Mahādevas: thus in the intellect the number is seventeen. / In the Gunatattva are three rows; thus they know fifty-six cities. // 416

8.s:
yadyapi guṇasāmyātmani mūle krodheśvarāṣṭakaṃ tathāpi dhiyi /
tacchodhitamiti gaṇanāṃ na punaḥ prāptaṃ pratiṣṭhāyām // 417
8.d:
यद्यपि गुणसाम्यात्मनि मूले क्रोधेश्वराष्टकं तथापि धियि ।
तच्छोधितमिति गणनां न पुनः प्राप्तं प्रतिष्ठायाम् ॥ 417
8.m: Although the octad of Krodheśvaras is in the root [matter] characterized by equilibrium of the gunas, nevertheless / it is purified in the intellect; hence it is not counted again in Pratiṣṭhā. // 417

8.s:
iti jalatattvānmūlaṃ tattvacaturviṃśatiḥ pratiṣṭhāyām /
ambādituṣṭivargastārādyāḥ siddhayo'ṇimādigaṇaḥ // 418
8.d:
इति जलतत्त्वान्मूलं तत्त्वचतुर्विंशतिः प्रतिष्ठायाम् ।
अम्बादितुष्टिवर्गस्ताराद्याः सिद्धयोऽणिमादिगणः ॥ 418
8.m: Thus, from the water tattva to the root, twenty-four tattvas are in Pratiṣṭhā. / The group of satisfactions (tuṣṭis) beginning with Ambā, the accomplishments (siddhis) beginning with Tārā, the host of Aṇimā and the rest, // 418

8.s:
guravo guruśiṣyā ṛṣivarga iḍādiśca vigrahāṣṭakayuk /
gandhādivikārapuraṃ buddhiguṇāṣṭakamahaṃkriyā viṣayaguṇāḥ // 419
8.d:
गुरवो गुरुशिष्या ऋषिवर्ग इडादिश्च विग्रहाष्टकयुक् ।
गन्धादिविकारपुरं बुद्धिगुणाष्टकमहंक्रिया विषयगुणाः ॥ 419
8.m: the gurus, the guru-disciples, the group of sages, Iḍā and so forth endowed with an octad of bodies, / the city of the transformations of fragrance and so on, the octad of intellect-qualities, ego-making, the sense-qualities, // 419

8.s:
kāmādisaptaviṃśakamāgantu tathā gaṇeśavidyeśamayau /
iti pāśeṣu puratrayamitthaṃ puruṣe'tra bhuvanaṣoḍaśakam // 420
8.d:
कामादिसप्तविंशकमागन्तु तथा गणेशविद्येशमयौ ।
इति पाशेषु पुरत्रयमित्थं पुरुषेऽत्र भुवनषोडशकम् ॥ 420
8.m: the twenty-seven beginning with Kāma, the adventitious, as well as those consisting of Gaṇeśa and the Vidyeśvaras: / thus there is a triad of cities in the fetters; in this manner, there are sixteen worlds in Puruṣa. // 420

8.s:
niyatau śaṅkaradaśakaṃ kāle śivadaśakamiti puradvitayam /
rāge suhṛṣṭabhuvanaṃ guruśiṣyapuraṃ ca vitkalāyugale // 421
8.d:
नियतौ शङ्करदशकं काले शिवदशकमिति पुरद्वितयम् ।
रागे सुहृष्टभुवनं गुरुशिष्यपुरं च वित्कलायुगले ॥ 421
8.m: In Niyati there is the decad of Śaṅkaras, in Kāla the decad of Śivas: thus a pair of cities; / in Rāga is the world Suhṛṣṭa, and the city of Guru-śiṣyas in the pair of Vidyā and Kalā; // 421

8.s:
bhuvanaṃ bhuvanaṃ niśi puṭapuratrayaṃ vākpuraṃ pramāṇapuram /
iti saptaviṃśatipurā vidyā puruṣāditattvasaptakayuk // 422
8.d:
भुवनं भुवनं निशि पुटपुरत्रयं वाक्पुरं प्रमाणपुरम् ।
इति सप्तविंशतिपुरा विद्या पुरुषादितत्त्वसप्तकयुक् ॥ 422
8.m: one world [each]; in night (Māyā) the triad of Puṭa cities, the city of Vāc, and the city of Pramāṇa: / thus Vidyā comprises twenty-seven cities, joined with the heptad of tattvas beginning with Puruṣa. // 422

8.s:
vāmeśarūpasūkṣmaṃ śuddhaṃ vidyātha śaktitejasvimitiḥ /
suviśuddhiśivau mokṣa dhuveṣisaṃbuddhasamayasauśivasaṃjñāḥ // 423
8.d:
वामेशरूपसूक्ष्मं शुद्धं विद्याथ शक्तितेजस्विमितिः ।
सुविशुद्धिशिवौ मोक्ष धुवेषिसंबुद्धसमयसौशिवसंज्ञाः ॥ 423
8.m: Vāmeśa, Rūpa, Sūkṣma, Śuddha, Vidyā, Śaktitejas, Miti, / Suviśuddha, Śiva, Mokṣa, Dhuveśa, Saṃbuddha, Samaya, and Sauśiva: [these] are the names [of the worlds].

8.s:
saptadaśapurā śāntā vidyeśasadāśivapuratritayayuktā /
bindvardhendunirodhyaḥ parasauśivamindhikādipurasauṣumne // 424
8.d:
सप्तदशपुरा शान्ता विद्येशसदाशिवपुरत्रितययुक्ता ।
बिन्द्वर्धेन्दुनिरोध्यः परसौशिवमिन्धिकादिपुरसौषुम्ने ॥ 424
8.m: Śāntā has seventeen worlds, conjoined with the triad of the worlds of Vidyeśa and Sadāśiva; / Bindu, Ardhendu, Nirodhikā, Parasauśiva, and in the Suṣumnā the worlds Indhikā and the rest,

8.s:
paranādo brahmabilaṃ sūkṣmādiyutordhvakuṇḍalī śaktiḥ /
vyāpivyomānantānāthānāśritapurāṇi pañca tataḥ // 425
8.d:
परनादो ब्रह्मबिलं सूक्ष्मादियुतोर्ध्वकुण्डली शक्तिः ।
व्यापिव्योमानन्तानाथानाश्रितपुराणि पञ्च ततः ॥ 425
8.m: Paranāda, Brahmabila, the Śakti as Ūrdhvakuṇḍalī endowed with Sūkṣmā and the rest, / then the five worlds Vyāpin, Vyoman, Ananta, Anātha, and Anāśrita.

8.s:
ṣaṣṭhaṃ ca paramamanāśritamatha samanābhuvanaṣoḍaśī yadi vā /
bindvāvaraṇaṃ parasauśivaṃ ca pañcendhikādibhuvanāni // 426
8.d:
षष्ठं च परममनाश्रितमथ समनाभुवनषोडशी यदि वा ।
बिन्द्वावरणं परसौशिवं च पञ्चेन्धिकादिभुवनानि ॥ 426
8.m: And the sixth, supreme Anāśrita; or else there is a group of sixteen worlds of Samanā: / the envelopment of Bindu, Parasauśiva, the five worlds beginning with Indhikā,

8.s:
sauṣumnaṃ brahmabilaṃ kuṇḍalinī vyāpipañcakaṃ samanā /
iti ṣoḍaśabhuvaneyaṃ tattvayugaṃ śāntyatītā syāt // 427
8.d:
सौषुम्नं ब्रह्मबिलं कुण्डलिनी व्यापिपञ्चकं समना ।
इति षोडशभुवनेयं तत्त्वयुगं शान्त्यतीता स्यात् ॥ 427
8.m: the Suṣumnā, Brahmabila, Kuṇḍalinī, the group of five Vyāpins, and Samanā. / Thus, Śāntyatītā would comprise this set of sixteen worlds [and] two principles.

8.s:
śrīmanmataṅgaśāstre ca kramo'yaṃ purapūgagaḥ /
kālāgnirnarakāḥ khābdhiyutaṃ mukhyatayā śatam // 428
8.d:
श्रीमन्मतङ्गशास्त्रे च क्रमोऽयं पुरपूगगः ।
कालाग्निर्नरकाः खाब्धियुतं मुख्यतया शतम् ॥ 428
8.m: And in the venerable Mataṅga treatise, this sequence is followed regarding the collection of worlds: / Kālāgni, the hells, and principally one hundred and forty [worlds],

8.s:
kūṣmāṇḍaḥ saptapātālī saptalokī maheśvaraḥ /
ityaṇḍamadhyaṃ tadbāhye śataṃ rudrā iti sthitāḥ // 429
8.d:
कूष्माण्डः सप्तपाताली सप्तलोकी महेश्वरः ।
इत्यण्डमध्यं तद्बाह्ये शतं रुद्रा इति स्थिताः ॥ 429
8.m: Kūṣmāṇḍa, the seven netherworlds, the seven lokas, and Maheśvara; / thus is the interior of the egg, and outside it are established one hundred Rudras.

8.s:
sthānānāṃ dviśatī bhūmiḥ saptapañcāśatā yutā /
pañcāṣṭakasya madhyāddvātriṃśadbhūtacatuṣṭaye // 430
8.d:
स्थानानां द्विशती भूमिः सप्तपञ्चाशता युता ।
पञ्चाष्टकस्य मध्याद्द्वात्रिंशद्भूतचतुष्टये ॥ 430
8.m: The earth comprises two hundred and fifty-seven stations. / Out of the forty [stations], thirty-two are in the four elements;

8.s:
tanmātreṣu ca pañca syurviśvedevāstato'ṣṭakam /
pañcamaṃ sendriye garve buddhau devāṣṭakaṃ guṇe // 431
8.d:
तन्मात्रेषु च पञ्च स्युर्विश्वेदेवास्ततोऽष्टकम् ।
पञ्चमं सेन्द्रिये गर्वे बुद्धौ देवाष्टकं गुणे ॥ 431
8.m: and in the subtle elements there are five; next, the group of eight Viśvedevas / is fifth in the egoity endowed with sense faculties; in the intellect is the octad of gods; in the qualities,

8.s:
yogāṣṭakaṃ krodhasaṃjñaṃ mūle kāle sanaiyate /
patadrugādyāścāṅguṣṭhamātrādyā rāgatattvagāḥ // 432
8.d:
योगाष्टकं क्रोधसंज्ञं मूले काले सनैयते ।
पतद्रुगाद्याश्चाङ्गुष्ठमात्राद्या रागतत्त्वगाः ॥ 432
8.m: the octad of yoga called Krodha; in the root [matter] and in time, together with Niyati; / Patadruga and the rest, and Aṅguṣṭhamātra and the rest reside in the principle of attachment;

8.s:
dvādaśaikaśivādyāḥ syurvidyāyāṃ kalane daśa /
vāmādyāstriśatī seyaṃ triparvaṇyabdhirasyayuk // 433
8.d:
द्वादशैकशिवाद्याः स्युर्विद्यायां कलने दश ।
वामाद्यास्त्रिशती सेयं त्रिपर्वण्यब्धिरस्ययुक् ॥ 433
8.m: there are twelve, Ekāśiva and the rest; in Vidyā [there are] ten in Kalana, / Vāmā and the rest. This [group of] three hundred and sixty-four consists of three stages.

8.s:
śaivāḥ kecidihānantāḥ śraikaṇṭhā iti saṃgrahaḥ /
yatra yadā parabhogān bubhukṣate tatra yojanaṃ kāryam // 434
8.d:
शैवाः केचिदिहानन्ताः श्रैकण्ठा इति संग्रहः ।
यत्र यदा परभोगान् बुभुक्षते तत्र योजनं कार्यम् ॥ 434
8.m: Certain Śaivas here [reckon them] endless, while the followers of Śrīkaṇṭha make this summary. / Wherever [and] whenever one desires to experience higher enjoyments, unification is to be performed there,

8.s:
śodhanamatha taddhānau śeṣaṃ tvantargataṃ kāryam /
ityāgamaṃ prathayituṃ darśitametadvikalpitaṃ tena // 435
8.d:
शोधनमथ तद्धानौ शेषं त्वन्तर्गतं कार्यम् ।
इत्यागमं प्रथयितुं दर्शितमेतद्विकल्पितं तेन ॥ 435
8.m: or purification; upon abandoning that, however, the remainder is to be internalized. / Thus has this variation been shown by him in order to elucidate the scripture.

8.s:
anye'pi bahuvikalpāḥ svadhiyācāryaiḥ samabhyūhyāḥ /
śrīpūrvaśāsane punaraṣṭādaśādhikaṃ śataṃ kathitam // 436
8.d:
अन्येऽपि बहुविकल्पाः स्वधियाचार्यैः समभ्यूह्याः ।
श्रीपूर्वशासने पुनरष्टादशाधिकं शतं कथितम् ॥ 436
8.m: Other numerous variations also are to be deduced by the masters by their own intelligence. / In the venerable Pūrvaśāsana, however, one hundred and eighteen are stated.

8.s:
tadiha pradhānamadhikaṃ saṃkṣepeṇocyate śodhyam /
kālāgniḥ kūṣmāṇḍo narakeśo hāṭako'tha bhūtalapaḥ // 437
8.d:
तदिह प्रधानमधिकं संक्षेपेणोच्यते शोध्यम् ।
कालाग्निः कूष्माण्डो नरकेशो हाटकोऽथ भूतलपः ॥ 437
8.m: That which is primary and foremost to be purified is stated here in brief: / Kālāgni, Kūṣmāṇḍa, Narakeśa, Hāṭaka, then the protector of the earth-plane,

8.s:
brahmā munilokeśo rudrāḥ pañcāntarālasthāḥ /
adhare'nantaḥ prācyāḥ kapālivahnyantanirṛtibalākhyāḥ // 438
8.d:
ब्रह्मा मुनिलोकेशो रुद्राः पञ्चान्तरालस्थाः ।
अधरेऽनन्तः प्राच्याः कपालिवह्न्यन्तनिरृतिबलाख्याः ॥ 438
8.m: Brahmā, Munilokeśa, the five Rudras abiding in the intermediate space, / at the base Ananta, [then] the eastern [Rudras] named Kapālin, Vahnyanta, Nirṛti, and Bala,

8.s:
laghunidhipatividyādhipaśambhūrdhvāntaṃ savīrabhadrapati /
ekādaśabhirbāhye brahmāṇḍaṃ pañcabhistathāntarikaiḥ // 439
8.d:
लघुनिधिपतिविद्याधिपशम्भूर्ध्वान्तं सवीरभद्रपति ।
एकादशभिर्बाह्ये ब्रह्माण्डं पञ्चभिस्तथान्तरिकैः ॥ 439
8.m: Laghunidhipati, Vidyādhipa, Śambhu, and ending with the upward [regent], along with the lord Vīrabhadra; / by eleven [Rudras] on the outside, and likewise by five internal [Rudras], the egg of Brahmā [is filled].

8.s:
iti ṣoḍaśapurametannivṛttikalayeha kalanīyam /
lakulīśabhārabhūtī diṇḍyāṣāḍhī ca puṣkaranimeṣau // 440
8.d:
इति षोडशपुरमेतन्निवृत्तिकलयेह कलनीयम् ।
लकुलीशभारभूती दिण्ड्याषाढी च पुष्करनिमेषौ ॥ 440
8.m: Thus this sixteen-world [domain] is to be reckoned here in the Nivṛtti-kalā. / Lakulīśa, Bhārabhūti, Diṇḍin, Āṣāḍhin, Puṣkara, Nimeṣa,

8.s:
prabhāsasureśāviti salile pratyātmakaṃ saparivāre /
bhairavakedāramahākālā madhyāmrajalpākhyāḥ // 441
8.d:
प्रभाससुरेशाविति सलिले प्रत्यात्मकं सपरिवारे ।
भैरवकेदारमहाकाला मध्याम्रजल्पाख्याः ॥ 441
8.m: Prabhāsa, and Sureśa: thus [eight] in water, each individual along with their retinue; / Bhairava, Kedāra, Mahākāla, Madhyama, Jalpa,

8.s:
śrīśailahariścandrāviti guhyāṣṭakamidaṃ mahasi /
bhīmendrāṭṭahāsavimalakanakhalanākhalakurusthitigayākhyāḥ // 442
8.d:
श्रीशैलहरिश्चन्द्राविति गुह्याष्टकमिदं महसि ।
भीमेन्द्राट्टहासविमलकनखलनाखलकुरुस्थितिगयाख्याः ॥ 442
8.m: Śrīśaila, and Hariścandra: this secret octad is in fire; / Bhīma, Indra, Aṭṭahāsa, Vimala, Kanakhala, Nākala, Kurukṣetra, and Gayā:

8.s:
atiguhyāṣṭakametanmaruti ca satanmātrake ca sākṣe ca /
sthāṇusuvarṇākhyau kila bhadro gokarṇako mahālayakaḥ // 443
8.d:
अतिगुह्याष्टकमेतन्मरुति च सतन्मात्रके च साक्षे च ।
स्थाणुसुवर्णाख्यौ किल भद्रो गोकर्णको महालयकः ॥ 443
8.m: this most secret octad is in wind, in the subtle elements, and in the sense faculties; / Sthāṇu, Suvarṇa, Bhadra, Gokarṇa, Mahālaya,

8.s:
avimuktarudrakoṭī vastrāpada ityadaḥ pavitraṃ khe /
sthūlasthūleśaśaṅkuśrutikālañjarāśca maṇḍalabhṛt // 444
8.d:
अविमुक्तरुद्रकोटी वस्त्रापद इत्यदः पवित्रं खे ।
स्थूलस्थूलेशशङ्कुश्रुतिकालञ्जराश्च मण्डलभृत् ॥ 444
8.m: Avimukta, Rudrakoṭi, and Vastrāpada: this sacred [octad] is in space; / Sthūla, Sthūleśa, Śaṅkuśruti, Kālañjara, Maṇḍalabhṛt,

8.s:
mākoṭāṇḍadvitayacchagalāṇḍā aṣṭakaṃ hyahaṅkāre /
anye'haṅkārāntastanmātrāṇīndriyāṇi cāpyāhuḥ // 445
8.d:
माकोटाण्डद्वितयच्छगलाण्डा अष्टकं ह्यहङ्कारे ।
अन्येऽहङ्कारान्तस्तन्मात्राणीन्द्रियाणि चाप्याहुः ॥ 445
8.m: Mākoṭa, the pair of Aṇḍas, and Chagalaṇḍa: this octad is in egoity; / others say that up to egoity are the subtle elements and the sense faculties as well.

8.s:
dhiyi yonyaṣṭakamuktaṃ prakṛtau yogāṣṭakaṃ kilākṛtaprabhṛti /
iti saptāṣṭakabhuvanā pratiṣṭhitiḥ salilato hi mūlāntā // 446
8.d:
धियि योन्यष्टकमुक्तं प्रकृतौ योगाष्टकं किलाकृतप्रभृति ।
इति सप्ताष्टकभुवना प्रतिष्ठितिः सलिलतो हि मूलान्ता ॥ 446
8.m: In the intellect the octad of wombs is taught, and in Prakṛti the octad of yoga beginning with Akṛta; / thus Pratiṣṭhā consists of fifty-six worlds, from water up to the root [matter].

8.s:
nari vāmo bhīmograu bhaveśavīrāḥ pracaṇḍagaurīśau /
ajasānantaikaśivau vidyāyāṃ krodhacaṇḍayugmaṃ syāt // 447
8.d:
नरि वामो भीमोग्रौ भवेशवीराः प्रचण्डगौरीशौ ।
अजसानन्तैकशिवौ विद्यायां क्रोधचण्डयुग्मं स्यात् ॥ 447
8.m: In the Puruṣa: Vāma, Bhīma, Ugra, Bhaveśa, Vīra, Pracaṇḍa, Gaurīśa, / Aja, Sānanta, and Ekaśiva; in Vidyā there is the pair Krodha and Caṇḍa,

8.s:
saṃvarto jyotiratho kalāniyatyāṃ ca sūrapañcāntau /
vīraśikhīśaśrīkaṇṭhasaṃjñametattrayaṃ ca kāle syāt // 448
8.d:
संवर्तो ज्योतिरथो कलानियत्यां च सूरपञ्चान्तौ ।
वीरशिखीशश्रीकण्ठसंज्ञमेतत्त्रयं च काले स्यात् ॥ 448
8.m: Saṃvarta, and Jyotis; then in Kalā and Niyati, Sūrapañcānta; / Vīra, Śikhīśa, and Śrīkaṇṭha: this triad is in Kāla;

8.s:
samahātejā vāmo bhavodbhavaścaikapiṅgaleśānau /
bhuvaneśapuraḥsarakāvaṅguṣṭha ime niśi sthitā hyaṣṭau // 449
8.d:
समहातेजा वामो भवोद्भवश्चैकपिङ्गलेशानौ ।
भुवनेशपुरःसरकावङ्गुष्ठ इमे निशि स्थिता ह्यष्टौ ॥ 449
8.m: along with Mahātejas: Vāma, Bhavodbhava, Ekapiṅgala, Īśāna, / preceded by Bhuvaneśa, and Aṅguṣṭha: these eight reside in night (Māyā).

8.s:
aṣṭāviṃśatibhuvanā vidyā puruṣānniśāntamiyam /
hālāhalarudrakrudambikāghorikāḥ savāmāḥ syuḥ // 450
8.d:
अष्टाविंशतिभुवना विद्या पुरुषान्निशान्तमियम् ।
हालाहलरुद्रक्रुदम्बिकाघोरिकाः सवामाः स्युः ॥ 450
8.m: This Vidyā[-kalā] consists of twenty-eight worlds, extending from Puruṣa to the end of night (Māyā); / Hālāhala, Rudrakrud, Ambikā, and Aghorikā, along with Vāmā,

8.s:
vidyāyāṃ vidyeśāstvaṣṭāvīśe sadāśive pañca /
vāmā jyeṣṭhā raudrī śaktiḥ sakalā ca śontayam // 451
8.d:
विद्यायां विद्येशास्त्वष्टावीशे सदाशिवे पञ्च ।
वामा ज्येष्ठा रौद्री शक्तिः सकला च शोन्तयम् ॥ 451
8.m: are in Vidyā; the eight Vidyeśas are in Īśa; in Sadāśiva are five: / Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, Raudrī, Śakti, and Sakalā; [this] is the Śāntā-kalā.

8.s:
aṣṭādaśa bhuvanā syāt śāntyatītā tvabhuvanaiva /
iti deśādhvavibhāgaḥ kathitaḥ śrīśambhunā samādiṣṭaḥ // 452
8.d:
अष्टादश भुवना स्यात् शान्त्यतीता त्वभुवनैव ।
इति देशाध्वविभागः कथितः श्रीशम्भुना समादिष्टः ॥ 452
8.m: It has eighteen worlds, whereas Śāntyatītā is indeed without worlds. / Thus has been explained the division of the spatial path as commanded by the venerable Śambhu.
